source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including written/read and other notes; no normalized reconstruction.
source.public_versification_note: Public 11:21 binds Hebrew 12:1; public 12:1–21 bind Hebrew 12:2–22. All other public verses bind matching original labels.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial choices are independent of overlap scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Retains the immediate political consequence.
verses.before: After the death of Ahab, Moab rebelled against Israel.
verses.after: After Ahab’s death, Moab rebelled against Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: After the death of Ahab, Moab rebelled against Israel.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes the fall, illness, and requested oracle.
verses.before: Ahaziah fell through the lattice in his upper room that was in Samaria and became sick. So he sent messengers and said to them, “Go, inquire of Baal-Zebub, god of Ekron, whether I will recover from this sickness.”
verses.after: Ahaziah fell through the lattice of his upper room in Samaria and was injured. He sent messengers with this command: “Go and consult Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron. Ask whether I will recover from this illness.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Ahaziah fell through the lattice in his upper room that was in Samaria and became sick. So he sent messengers and said to them, “Go, inquire of Baal-Zebub, god of Ekron, whether I will recover from this sickness.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the rhetorical question and divine messenger.
verses.before: But the messenger of the LORD said to Elijah the Tishbite, “Rise, go up to meet the messengers of the king of Samaria and say to them, ‘Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are going to inquire of Baal-Zebub, god of Ekron?’
verses.after: But the LORD’s angel told Elijah the Tishbite, “Go up to meet the king of Samaria’s messengers. Say to them, ‘Is there no God in Israel, that you are going to consult Baal-zebub, Ekron’s god?’
verses.tsw_comparator: But the messenger of the LORD said to Elijah the Tishbite, “Rise, go up to meet the messengers of the king of Samaria and say to them, ‘Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are going to inquire of Baal-Zebub, god of Ekron?’

verses.rationale: Retains bed image and emphatic death sentence.
verses.before: So thus says the LORD: ‘You will not come down from the bed to which you have gone up, but you will surely die.’” Then Elijah went.
verses.after: Therefore the LORD says: ‘You will not come down from the bed you have climbed into. You will certainly die.’” So Elijah went.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore thus says the LORD: ‘You shall not come down from the bed to which you have gone up, but you shall surely die.’” Then Elijah went.

verses.rationale: Identifies the king receiving the unexpected return.
verses.before: The messengers returned to Ahaziah, and he said to them, “Why have you returned?”
verses.after: The messengers returned to Ahaziah. “Why have you come back?” he asked.
verses.tsw_comparator: The messengers returned to Ahaziah, and he said to them, “Why have you returned?”

verses.rationale: Preserves the full repeated message rather than summarizing.
verses.before: They said to him, “A man came up to meet us and said to us, ‘Go, return to the king who sent you and say to him: Thus says the LORD: Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are sending to inquire of Baal-Zebub, god of Ekron? Therefore you will not come down from the bed to which you have gone up, but you will surely die.’”
verses.after: They answered, “A man met us and told us, ‘Go back to the king who sent you. Tell him: The LORD says, Is there no God in Israel, that you send to consult Baal-zebub, Ekron’s god? Therefore you will not come down from the bed you have climbed into. You will certainly die.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: They said to him, “A man came up to meet us and said to us, ‘Go, return to the king who sent you and say to him: Thus says the LORD: Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are sending to inquire of Baal-Zebub, god of Ekron? Therefore you shall not come down from the bed to which you have gone up, but you shall surely die.’”

verses.rationale: Turns the appearance inquiry into natural dialogue.
verses.before: He said to them, “What kind of man was he who came up to meet you and spoke these words to you?”
verses.after: He asked them, “What did the man who met you and said this look like?”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to them, “What kind of man was he who came up to meet you and spoke these words to you?”

verses.rationale: Retains hairy description with clothing alternative reserved for notes.
verses.before: They said to him, “A hairy man, with a leather belt bound around his waist.” He said, “It is Elijah the Tishbite.”
verses.after: “He was a hairy man,” they said, “with a leather belt around his waist.” “That is Elijah the Tishbite,” he replied.
verses.tsw_comparator: They said to him, “A hairy man, with a leather belt bound around his waist.” He said, “It is Elijah the Tishbite.”

verses.rationale: Keeps military scale and competing authority.
verses.before: Then the king sent to him a captain of fifty with his fifty. He went up to Elijah, and look, he was sitting on the top of the hill. He said to him, “Man of God, the king says, ‘Come down.’”
verses.after: The king sent a captain with his fifty men to Elijah. The captain went up and found him sitting on a hilltop. “Man of God,” he said, “the king commands you to come down.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the king sent to him a captain of fifty with his fifty. He went up to Elijah, and look, he was sitting on the top of the hill. He said to him, “Man of God, the king says, ‘Come down.’”

verses.rationale: Preserves the lethal response and repeated descent.
verses.before: Elijah answered and said to the captain of fifty, “If I am a man of God, let fire come down from the heavens and consume you and your fifty.” Then fire came down from the heavens and consumed him and his fifty.
verses.after: Elijah answered the captain, “If I am a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty men.” Fire came down from heaven and consumed them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Elijah answered and said to the captain of fifty, “If I am a man of God, let fire come down from the heavens and consume you and your fifty.” Then fire came down from the heavens and consumed him and his fifty.

verses.rationale: Keeps escalation in the second command.
verses.before: Again the king sent to him another captain of fifty with his fifty. He answered and said to him, “Man of God, thus says the king: ‘Come down quickly.’”
verses.after: The king sent another captain with fifty men. He said to Elijah, “Man of God, the king says, ‘Come down at once!’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Again the king sent to him another captain of fifty with his fifty. He answered and said to him, “Man of God, thus says the king: ‘Come down quickly.’”

verses.rationale: Retains explicit divine attribution of the second fire.
verses.before: Elijah answered and said to them, “If I am a man of God, let fire come down from the heavens and consume you and your fifty.” Then the fire of God came down from the heavens and consumed him and his fifty.
verses.after: Elijah answered, “If I am a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty men.” God’s fire came down from heaven and consumed them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Elijah answered and said to them, “If I am a man of God, let fire come down from the heavens and consume you and your fifty.” Then the fire of God came down from the heavens and consumed him and his fifty.

verses.rationale: Keeps the appeal for the soldiers’ lives.
verses.before: Again the king sent a third captain of fifty with his fifty. The third captain of fifty went up, came, and knelt on his knees before Elijah. He pleaded with him and said to him, “Man of God, please let my life and the life of these fifty servants of yours be precious in your eyes.
verses.after: Again the king sent a third captain with fifty men. This captain went up, knelt before Elijah, and pleaded, “Man of God, please let my life and the lives of these fifty servants of yours be precious in your eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: Again the king sent a third captain of fifty with his fifty. The third captain of fifty went up, came, and knelt on his knees before Elijah. He pleaded with him and said to him, “Man of God, please let my life and the life of these fifty servants of yours be precious in your eyes.

verses.rationale: Retains fearful repetition rather than dismissing it.
verses.before: Look, fire came down from the heavens and consumed the first two captains of fifty with their fifties. But now let my life be precious in your eyes.”
verses.after: Fire came down from heaven and consumed the first two captains, each with his fifty men. But now, please let my life be precious in your eyes.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, fire came down from the heavens and consumed the first two captains of fifty with their fifties. But now let my life be precious in your eyes.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the instruction and reassurance distinct.
verses.before: The messenger of the LORD said to Elijah, “Go down with him. Do not be afraid of him.” So he arose and went down with him to the king.
verses.after: The LORD’s angel told Elijah, “Go down with him. Do not be afraid of him.” Elijah got up and went with him to the king.
verses.tsw_comparator: The messenger of the LORD said to Elijah, “Go down with him. Do not be afraid of him.” So he arose and went down with him to the king.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated accusation and interrupting question.
verses.before: He said to him, “Thus says the LORD: Because you sent messengers to inquire of Baal-Zebub, god of Ekron—is it because there is no God in Israel to inquire of his word?—therefore you will not come down from the bed to which you have gone up, but you will surely die.”
verses.after: Elijah told him, “The LORD says: Because you sent messengers to consult Baal-zebub, Ekron’s god—is there no God in Israel whose word you can seek?—you will not come down from the bed you have climbed into. You will certainly die.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to him, “Thus says the LORD: Because you sent messengers to inquire of Baal-Zebub, god of Ekron—is it because there is no God in Israel to inquire of his word?—therefore you shall not come down from the bed to which you have gone up, but you shall surely die.”

verses.rationale: Keeps two same-named kings and this passage’s date.
verses.before: So he died according to the word of the LORD that Elijah had spoken. Jehoram became king in his place in the second year of Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, because Ahaziah had no son.
verses.after: Ahaziah died according to the LORD’s word spoken by Elijah. Because he had no son, Jehoram became king in his place, in the second year of Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: So he died according to the word of the LORD that Elijah had spoken. Jehoram became king in his place in the second year of Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, because Ahaziah had no son.

verses.rationale: Maintains the recurring source notice.
verses.before: Now the rest of the acts of Ahaziah that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.after: The rest of Ahaziah’s deeds—are they not written in the annals of the kings of Israel?
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the rest of the acts of Ahaziah that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

verses.rationale: Introduces the departure without adding a vehicle.
verses.before: And it happened when the LORD was about to take Elijah up into the heavens in a whirlwind, Elijah and Elisha went from Gilgal.
verses.after: When the LORD was about to take Elijah up to heaven in a whirlwind, Elijah and Elisha set out from Gilgal.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened when the LORD was about to take Elijah up into the heavens in a whirlwind, Elijah and Elisha went from Gilgal.

verses.rationale: Keeps the oath repeated through the journey.
verses.before: Elijah said to Elisha, “Please stay here, for the LORD has sent me as far as Bethel.” But Elisha said, “As the LORD lives and as your life lives, I will not leave you.” So they went down to Bethel.
verses.after: Elijah said to Elisha, “Stay here, please. The LORD has sent me to Bethel.” Elisha answered, “As the LORD lives, and as you live, I will not leave you.” So they went down to Bethel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Elijah said to Elisha, “Please stay here, for the LORD has sent me as far as Bethel.” But Elisha said, “As the LORD lives and as your life lives, I will not leave you.” So they went down to Bethel.

verses.rationale: Preserves the over-you image and restrained reply.
verses.before: The sons of the prophets who were at Bethel came out to Elisha and said to him, “Do you know that today the LORD is taking your master from over your head?” He said, “I also know. Be silent.”
verses.after: The company of prophets at Bethel came out to Elisha. “Do you know the LORD is taking your master away from over you today?” they asked. “Yes, I know,” he said. “Be quiet.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The sons of the prophets who were at Bethel came out to Elisha and said to him, “Do you know that today the LORD is taking your master from over your head?” He said, “I also know. Be silent.”

verses.rationale: Retains deliberate repetition with changed destination.
verses.before: Elijah said to him, “Elisha, please stay here, for the LORD has sent me to Jericho.” But he said, “As the LORD lives and as your life lives, I will not leave you.” So they came to Jericho.
verses.after: Elijah said, “Elisha, stay here, please. The LORD has sent me to Jericho.” He answered, “As the LORD lives, and as you live, I will not leave you.” So they went to Jericho.
verses.tsw_comparator: Elijah said to him, “Elisha, please stay here, for the LORD has sent me to Jericho.” But he said, “As the LORD lives and as your life lives, I will not leave you.” So they came to Jericho.

verses.rationale: Keeps the second prophetic exchange unchanged.
verses.before: The sons of the prophets who were at Jericho drew near to Elisha and said to him, “Do you know that today the LORD is taking your master from over your head?” He said, “I also know. Be silent.”
verses.after: The company of prophets at Jericho approached Elisha. “Do you know the LORD is taking your master away from over you today?” they asked. “Yes, I know,” he said. “Be quiet.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The sons of the prophets who were at Jericho drew near to Elisha and said to him, “Do you know that today the LORD is taking your master from over your head?” He said, “I also know. Be silent.”

verses.rationale: Completes the threefold refusal to leave.
verses.before: Elijah said to him, “Please stay here, for the LORD has sent me to the Jordan.” But he said, “As the LORD lives and as your life lives, I will not leave you.” So the two of them went on.
verses.after: Elijah said, “Stay here, please. The LORD has sent me to the Jordan.” He answered, “As the LORD lives, and as you live, I will not leave you.” So the two went on.
verses.tsw_comparator: Elijah said to him, “Please stay here, for the LORD has sent me to the Jordan.” But he said, “As the LORD lives and as your life lives, I will not leave you.” So the two of them went on.

verses.rationale: Preserves witnesses and distance.
verses.before: Fifty men from the sons of the prophets went and stood opposite them at a distance, while the two of them stood by the Jordan.
verses.after: Fifty men from the company of prophets followed and stood some distance away, while the two stood beside the Jordan.
verses.tsw_comparator: Fifty men from the sons of the prophets went and stood opposite them at a distance, while the two of them stood by the Jordan.

verses.rationale: Keeps material actions and dry-ground image.
verses.before: Elijah took his cloak, rolled it up, and struck the waters. They were divided to this side and that side, and the two of them crossed over on dry ground.
verses.after: Elijah took his cloak, rolled it up, and struck the water. It divided to either side, and the two crossed on dry ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: Elijah took his cloak, rolled it up, and struck the waters. They were divided to this side and that side, and the two of them crossed over on dry ground.

verses.rationale: Preserves inheritance-shaped request without quantifying power.
verses.before: And it happened when they had crossed over that Elijah said to Elisha, “Ask what I will do for you before I am taken from you.” Elisha said, “Please let a double portion of your spirit be upon me.”
verses.after: After they crossed, Elijah said, “Ask what I can do for you before I am taken from you.” Elisha answered, “Please let me receive a double share of your spirit.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened when they had crossed over that Elijah said to Elisha, “Ask what I shall do for you before I am taken from you.” Elisha said, “Please let a double portion of your spirit be upon me.”

verses.rationale: Keeps condition and contrasting outcomes.
verses.before: He said, “You have asked a difficult thing. If you see me when I am taken from you, it will be so for you, but if not, it will not be.”
verses.after: “You have asked a difficult thing,” Elijah said. “If you see me being taken from you, it will be yours. If not, it will not.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “You have asked a difficult thing. If you see me when I am taken from you, it shall be so for you, but if not, it shall not be.”

verses.rationale: Distinguishes separating chariot from ascending whirlwind.
verses.before: And it happened as they continued walking and speaking, look, a chariot of fire and horses of fire separated the two of them, and Elijah went up in a whirlwind into the heavens.
verses.after: As they walked along talking, a chariot of fire and horses of fire separated them. Elijah went up to heaven in the whirlwind.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened as they continued walking and speaking, look, a chariot of fire and horses of fire separated the two of them, and Elijah went up in a whirlwind into the heavens.

verses.rationale: Retains filial cry and military image.
verses.before: Elisha saw it and cried out, “My father, my father! The chariots of Israel and its horsemen!” Then he saw him no more. He took hold of his own clothes and tore them in two pieces.
verses.after: Elisha watched and cried, “My father, my father! Israel’s chariot and its horsemen!” When he could no longer see him, he grasped his clothes and tore them in two.
verses.tsw_comparator: Elisha saw it and cried out, “My father, my father! The chariots of Israel and its horsemen!” Then he saw him no more. He took hold of his own clothes and tore them in two pieces.

verses.rationale: Keeps the cloak’s transfer concrete.
verses.before: He picked up Elijah’s cloak that had fallen from him and returned and stood on the bank of the Jordan.
verses.after: He picked up Elijah’s cloak, which had fallen from him, and returned to stand on the Jordan’s bank.
verses.tsw_comparator: He picked up Elijah’s cloak that had fallen from him and returned and stood on the bank of the Jordan.

verses.rationale: Preserves the difficult he-too phrase and repeated striking.
verses.before: He took Elijah’s cloak that had fallen from him, struck the waters, and said, “Where is the LORD, the God of Elijah—where is he?” When he struck the waters, they divided to this side and that side, and Elisha crossed over.
verses.after: He took the fallen cloak and struck the water. “Where is the LORD, Elijah’s God?” he asked. He too struck the water, and it divided to either side. Elisha crossed.
verses.tsw_comparator: He took Elijah’s cloak that had fallen from him, struck the waters, and said, “Where is the LORD, the God of Elijah—where is he?” When he struck the waters, they divided to this side and that side, and Elisha crossed over.

verses.rationale: Keeps their interpretation attributed to witnesses.
verses.before: When the sons of the prophets who were at Jericho opposite him saw him, they said, “The spirit of Elijah rests upon Elisha.” They came to meet him and bowed down to the ground before him.
verses.after: The company of prophets from Jericho saw him from a distance. “Elijah’s spirit rests on Elisha,” they said. They came to meet him and bowed to the ground before him.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the sons of the prophets who were at Jericho opposite him saw him, they said, “The spirit of Elijah rests upon Elisha.” They came to meet him and bowed down to the ground before him.

verses.rationale: Retains their uncertain explanation and proposed search.
verses.before: They said to him, “Look now, there are with your servants fifty capable men. Please let them go and seek your master, lest the Spirit of the LORD has lifted him up and cast him upon one of the mountains or into one of the valleys.” He said, “You will not send them.”
verses.after: They said, “Your servants have fifty strong men. Please let them search for your master. Perhaps the LORD’s spirit lifted him up and dropped him on a mountain or in a valley.” “Do not send them,” he said.
verses.tsw_comparator: They said to him, “Look now, there are with your servants fifty capable men. Please let them go and seek your master, lest the Spirit of the LORD has lifted him up and cast him upon one of the mountains or into one of the valleys.” He said, “You shall not send them.”

verses.rationale: Keeps pressure, consent, duration and failed result.
verses.before: But they pressed him until he was ashamed, and he said, “Send.” So they sent fifty men, and they searched three days but did not find him.
verses.after: But they pressed him until he was embarrassed, and he said, “Send them.” They sent fifty men, who searched for three days but did not find Elijah.
verses.tsw_comparator: But they pressed him until he was ashamed, and he said, “Send.” So they sent fifty men, and they searched three days but did not find him.

verses.rationale: Retains the corrective question.
verses.before: They returned to him while he was staying at Jericho, and he said to them, “Did I not say to you, ‘Do not go’?”
verses.after: They returned to Elisha, who was staying in Jericho. “Didn’t I tell you not to go?” he said.
verses.tsw_comparator: They returned to him while he was staying at Jericho, and he said to them, “Did I not say to you, ‘Do not go’?”

verses.rationale: Preserves uncertainty about barrenness or miscarriage.
verses.before: The men of the city said to Elisha, “Look, the location of the city is good, as my lord sees, but the water is bad and the land causes miscarriage.”
verses.after: The town’s men told Elisha, “As my lord can see, the town is well situated. But the water is bad, and the land causes loss of life.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The men of the city said to Elisha, “Look, the location of the city is good, as my lord sees, but the water is bad and the land causes miscarriage.”

verses.rationale: Keeps new vessel and salt.
verses.before: He said, “Bring me a new bowl and put salt in it.” So they brought it to him.
verses.after: “Bring me a new bowl with salt in it,” he said. They brought it.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “Bring me a new bowl and put salt in it.” So they brought it to him.

verses.rationale: Retains healing and comprehensive ending of harm.
verses.before: He went out to the spring of the water, threw salt there, and said, “Thus says the LORD: I have healed this water. From there will no longer come death or miscarriage.”
verses.after: He went to the spring, threw the salt into it, and said, “The LORD says: I have healed this water. No more death or loss of life will come from it.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He went out to the spring of the water, threw salt there, and said, “Thus says the LORD: I have healed this water. From there shall no longer come death or miscarriage.”

verses.rationale: Keeps narrator’s continuing-time perspective.
verses.before: So the waters were healed to this day according to the word of Elisha that he spoke.
verses.after: The water has remained healed to this day, just as Elisha said.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the waters were healed to this day according to the word of Elisha that he spoke.

verses.rationale: Keeps youth and taunt without inventing an armed threat.
verses.before: He went up from there to Bethel. As he was going up on the way, some young boys came out from the city and mocked him and said to him, “Go up, baldhead! Go up, baldhead!”
verses.after: From there he went up toward Bethel. As he walked up the road, young boys came out of the town and mocked him: “Go up, baldhead! Go up, baldhead!”
verses.tsw_comparator: He went up from there to Bethel. As he was going up on the way, some young boys came out from the city and mocked him and said to him, “Go up, baldhead! Go up, baldhead!”

verses.rationale: Preserves sex, count and real harm without asserting every death.
verses.before: He turned behind him, saw them, and cursed them in the name of the LORD. Then two she-bears came out from the forest and tore forty-two of the boys.
verses.after: He turned, looked at them, and cursed them in the LORD’s name. Two female bears came out of the woods and tore forty-two of the children.
verses.tsw_comparator: He turned behind him, saw them, and cursed them in the name of the LORD. Then two she-bears came out from the forest and tore forty-two of the boys.

verses.rationale: Keeps the final itinerary.
verses.before: From there he went to Mount Carmel, and from there he returned to Samaria.
verses.after: From there he went to Mount Carmel and then returned to Samaria.
verses.tsw_comparator: From there he went to Mount Carmel, and from there he returned to Samaria.

verses.rationale: Retains this date alongside the different synchronism in 1:17.
verses.before: Jehoram son of Ahab became king over Israel in Samaria in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and he reigned twelve years.
verses.after: Jehoram son of Ahab became king over Israel in Samaria in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah. He ruled for twelve years.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jehoram son of Ahab became king over Israel in Samaria in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and he reigned twelve years.

verses.rationale: Keeps qualified assessment and limited reform.
verses.before: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, though not like his father and his mother, for he removed the pillar of Baal that his father had made.
verses.after: He did evil in the LORD’s eyes, though not like his father and mother. He removed the pillar of Baal his father had made.
verses.tsw_comparator: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, though not like his father and his mother, for he removed the pillar of Baal that his father had made.

verses.rationale: Retains persistence and corporate influence.
verses.before: Yet he clung to the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, which he caused Israel to sin. He did not turn away from them.
verses.after: But he held fast to the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who led Israel into sin. He did not turn away from them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet he clung to the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, which he caused Israel to sin. He did not turn away from them.

verses.rationale: Preserves both livestock quantities and wool tribute.
verses.before: Mesha king of Moab was a sheep breeder, and he rendered to the king of Israel one hundred thousand lambs and the wool of one hundred thousand rams.
verses.after: Mesha king of Moab raised sheep. He supplied Israel’s king with a hundred thousand lambs and the wool of a hundred thousand rams.
verses.tsw_comparator: Mesha king of Moab was a sheep breeder, and he rendered to the king of Israel one hundred thousand lambs and the wool of one hundred thousand rams.

verses.rationale: Repeats the political opening in fuller context.
verses.before: But when Ahab died, the king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel.
verses.after: But after Ahab died, Moab’s king rebelled against Israel’s king.
verses.tsw_comparator: But when Ahab died, the king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel.

verses.rationale: Keeps mobilization without expanding the force.
verses.before: So King Jehoram went out from Samaria at that time and mustered all Israel.
verses.after: King Jehoram left Samaria at that time and mustered all Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: So King Jehoram went out from Samaria at that time and mustered all Israel.

verses.rationale: Retains the pledge echoing 1 Kings 22.
verses.before: He went and sent to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, saying, “The king of Moab has rebelled against me. Will you go with me to Moab for battle?” He said, “I will go up. I am as you are, my people as your people, my horses as your horses.”
verses.after: He sent word to Jehoshaphat king of Judah: “Moab’s king has rebelled against me. Will you join me in war against Moab?” “I will,” he replied. “I am as you are, my people as your people, my horses as your horses.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He went and sent to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, saying, “The king of Moab has rebelled against me. Will you go with me to Moab for battle?” He said, “I will go up. I am as you are, my people as your people, my horses as your horses.”

verses.rationale: Leaves unnamed speakers where the source does.
verses.before: He said, “By which way will we go up?” And he said, “By the way of the wilderness of Edom.”
verses.after: “Which route shall we take?” he asked. The answer was, “Through the wilderness of Edom.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “By which way shall we go up?” And he said, “By the way of the wilderness of Edom.”

verses.rationale: Preserves three allies, duration and shared need.
verses.before: So the king of Israel, the king of Judah, and the king of Edom went. They went around on the road seven days, but there was no water for the camp or for the animals that followed them.
verses.after: The kings of Israel, Judah, and Edom set out. After a roundabout journey of seven days, there was no water for the army or the animals following them.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the king of Israel, the king of Judah, and the king of Edom went. They went around on the road seven days, but there was no water for the camp or for the animals that followed them.

verses.rationale: Keeps accusation as the king’s speech.
verses.before: Then the king of Israel said, “Ah! For the LORD has called these three kings to give them into the hand of Moab.”
verses.after: Israel’s king cried, “Alas! The LORD has called these three kings together to hand them over to Moab!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the king of Israel said, “Ah! For the LORD has called these three kings to give them into the hand of Moab.”

verses.rationale: Retains concrete service identifying Elisha.
verses.before: Yet Jehoshaphat said, “Is there no prophet of the LORD here, so that we may inquire of the LORD through him?” One of the servants of the king of Israel answered and said, “Elisha son of Shaphat is here, who poured water on the hands of Elijah.”
verses.after: Jehoshaphat asked, “Is there no prophet of the LORD here through whom we can consult him?” A servant of Israel’s king answered, “Elisha son of Shaphat is here—the one who poured water over Elijah’s hands.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But Jehoshaphat said, “Is there no prophet of the LORD here, so that we may inquire of the LORD through him?” One of the servants of the king of Israel answered and said, “Elisha son of Shaphat is here, who poured water on the hands of Elijah.”

verses.rationale: Keeps affirmation and named delegation.
verses.before: Jehoshaphat said, “The word of the LORD is with him.” So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat and the king of Edom went down to him.
verses.after: Jehoshaphat said, “The LORD’s word is with him.” So Israel’s king, Jehoshaphat, and Edom’s king went down to him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jehoshaphat said, “The word of the LORD is with him.” So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat and the king of Edom went down to him.

verses.rationale: Retains rejection and repeated desperate explanation.
verses.before: Elisha said to the king of Israel, “What have I to do with you? Go to the prophets of your father and to the prophets of your mother.” But the king of Israel said to him, “No, for the LORD has called these three kings to give them into the hand of Moab.”
verses.after: Elisha said to Israel’s king, “What have you to do with me? Go to your father’s prophets and your mother’s prophets.” The king answered, “No! The LORD has called these three kings together to hand them over to Moab.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Elisha said to the king of Israel, “What have I to do with you? Go to the prophets of your father and to the prophets of your mother.” But the king of Israel said to him, “No, for the LORD has called these three kings to give them into the hand of Moab.”

verses.rationale: Preserves oath and pointed conditional refusal.
verses.before: Elisha said, “As the LORD of Hosts lives, before whom I stand, surely if I did not respect the presence of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, I would not look at you or see you.
verses.after: Elisha said, “As the LORD of Armies lives, whom I serve, if I did not respect Jehoshaphat king of Judah, I would not so much as look at you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Elisha said, “As the LORD of Hosts lives, before whom I stand, surely if I did not respect the presence of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, I would not look at you or see you.

verses.rationale: Keeps music’s place without inventing a mechanism.
verses.before: And now, bring me a musician.” And it happened when the musician played that the hand of the LORD came upon him.
verses.after: Now bring me a musician.” As the musician played, the LORD’s hand came upon Elisha.
verses.tsw_comparator: And now, bring me a musician.” And it happened when the musician played that the hand of the LORD came upon him.

verses.rationale: Renders the infinitive as instruction; alternative noted later.
verses.before: He said, “Thus says the LORD: Make this valley full of ditches.
verses.after: He said, “The LORD says: Make this valley full of ditches.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “Thus says the LORD: Make this valley full of ditches.

verses.rationale: Preserves unseen weather and separate beneficiaries.
verses.before: For thus says the LORD: You will not see wind, and you will not see rain, yet this valley will be filled with water, and you will drink—you, your livestock, and your animals.
verses.after: For the LORD says: You will see neither wind nor rain, yet this valley will fill with water. You, your cattle, and your other animals will drink.
verses.tsw_comparator: For thus says the LORD: You shall not see wind, and you shall not see rain, yet this valley will be filled with water, and you shall drink—you, your livestock, and your animals.

verses.rationale: Keeps the comparative promise.
verses.before: This is a small thing in the eyes of the LORD. He will also give Moab into your hand.
verses.after: This is a small thing in the LORD’s eyes. He will also hand Moab over to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: This is a small thing in the eyes of the LORD. He will also give Moab into your hand.

verses.rationale: Preserves environmental devastation and repetition.
verses.before: You will strike every fortified city and every choice city, fell every good tree, stop every spring of water, and ruin every good field with stones.”
verses.after: You will strike every fortified town and every choice town. You will fell every good tree, stop up every spring, and ruin every good field with stones.”
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall strike every fortified city and every choice city, fell every good tree, stop every spring of water, and ruin every good field with stones.”

verses.rationale: Keeps timing and direction without invented rainfall.
verses.before: In the morning, about the time of the grain offering, look, water came from the direction of Edom, and the land was filled with water.
verses.after: In the morning, at the time of the offering, water came from the direction of Edom and filled the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the morning, about the time of the grain offering, look, water came from the direction of Edom, and the land was filled with water.

verses.rationale: Retains military-age idiom without an invented numerical age.
verses.before: Now all Moab had heard that the kings had come up to fight against them. Everyone able to put on armor, from the youngest upward, was summoned, and they stood at the border.
verses.after: All Moab heard that the kings had come to fight them. Every man old enough to strap on a belt and all who were older were called out, and they took their stand at the border.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now all Moab had heard that the kings had come up to fight against them. Everyone able to put on armor, from the youngest upward, was summoned, and they stood at the border.

verses.rationale: Keeps perception distinct from actual blood.
verses.before: They rose early in the morning, and the sun shone upon the water. The Moabites saw the water opposite them red like blood.
verses.after: They rose early. The sun shone on the water, and from across the way the Moabites saw it red as blood.
verses.tsw_comparator: They rose early in the morning, and the sun shone upon the water. The Moabites saw the water opposite them red like blood.

verses.rationale: Attributes mistaken inference to the Moabites.
verses.before: They said, “This is blood! The kings have surely fought one another and struck each man his companion. And now, to the spoil, Moab!”
verses.after: “It is blood!” they said. “The kings have destroyed each other! Now, Moab, to the plunder!”
verses.tsw_comparator: They said, “This is blood! The kings have surely fought one another and struck each man his companion. And now, to the spoil, Moab!”

verses.rationale: Follows read striking form and pursuit.
verses.before: But when they came to the camp of Israel, the Israelites arose and struck Moab, and they fled before them. They entered the land, striking Moab as they went.
verses.after: But when they reached Israel’s camp, the Israelites rose and struck them. Moab fled, and Israel continued striking into Moab.
verses.tsw_comparator: But when they came to the camp of Israel, the Israelites arose and struck Moab, and they fled before them. They entered the land, striking Moab as they went.

verses.rationale: Retains cumulative destruction and final stronghold.
verses.before: They tore down the cities, and each man threw his stone into every good field and filled it. They stopped every spring of water and felled every good tree, until only the stones of Kir-Hareseth remained. The slingers surrounded it and struck it.
verses.after: They demolished the towns. Each man threw stones onto every good field until it was covered. They stopped every spring and felled every good tree. Only Kir-hareseth’s stones were left, and slingers surrounded and attacked it.
verses.tsw_comparator: They tore down the cities, and each man threw his stone into every good field and filled it. They stopped every spring of water and felled every good tree, until only the stones of Kir-Hareseth remained. The slingers surrounded it and struck it.

verses.rationale: Keeps attempted breakthrough and failed result.
verses.before: When the king of Moab saw that the battle was too strong for him, he took with him seven hundred men who drew the sword to break through to the king of Edom, but they were not able.
verses.after: When Moab’s king saw the battle overpowering him, he took seven hundred swordsmen to break through toward Edom’s king. They could not.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the king of Moab saw that the battle was too strong for him, he took with him seven hundred men who drew the sword to break through to the king of Edom, but they were not able.

verses.rationale: Preserves child sacrifice and leaves the wrath’s source unnamed.
verses.before: Then he took his firstborn son, who was to reign in his place, and offered him as a burnt offering upon the wall. And there was great wrath against Israel, so they withdrew from him and returned to the land.
verses.after: Then he took his firstborn son, who was to succeed him, and offered him as a burnt offering on the wall. Great wrath came against Israel. They withdrew from him and returned to their own land.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he took his firstborn son, who was to reign in his place, and offered him as a burnt offering upon the wall. And there was great wrath against Israel, so they withdrew from him and returned to the land.

verses.rationale: Preserves bereavement and threatened debt enslavement.
verses.before: A woman from the wives of the sons of the prophets cried out to Elisha, saying, “Your servant my husband is dead, and you know that your servant feared the LORD. But the creditor has come to take my two children for himself as servants.”
verses.after: The wife of a man from the company of prophets cried out to Elisha, “Your servant, my husband, has died. You know he feared the LORD. Now his creditor is coming to take my two children as slaves.”
verses.tsw_comparator: A woman from the wives of the sons of the prophets cried out to Elisha, saying, “Your servant my husband is dead, and you know that your servant feared the LORD. But the creditor has come to take my two children for himself as servants.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the woman’s limited resources and deferential voice.
verses.before: Elisha said to her, “What will I do for you? Tell me, what do you have in the house?” She said, “Your servant has nothing at all in the house except a jar of oil.”
verses.after: Elisha asked, “What can I do for you? Tell me what you have at home.” “Your servant has nothing at home but a flask of oil,” she answered.
verses.tsw_comparator: Elisha said to her, “What shall I do for you? Tell me, what do you have in the house?” She said, “Your servant has nothing at all in the house except a jar of oil.”

verses.rationale: Renders the negative injunction naturally.
verses.before: He said, “Go, ask for vessels from outside, from all your neighbors—empty vessels, not a few.
verses.after: He said, “Go outside and borrow empty jars from all your neighbors. Gather plenty.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “Go, ask for vessels from outside, from all your neighbors—empty vessels, not a few.

verses.rationale: Preserves privacy and sequence.
verses.before: Then go in and shut the door behind you and behind your sons. Pour into all these vessels, and when one is full, set it aside.”
verses.after: Then go inside and shut the door behind you and your sons. Pour oil into all those jars, setting each full one aside.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then go in and shut the door behind you and behind your sons. Pour into all these vessels, and when one is full, set it aside.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the sons’ participation and continuing action.
verses.before: So she went from him and shut the door behind her and behind her sons. They brought the vessels to her, and she kept pouring.
verses.after: She left him and shut the door behind herself and her sons. They brought her the jars, and she kept pouring.
verses.tsw_comparator: So she went from him and shut the door behind her and behind her sons. They brought the vessels to her, and she kept pouring.

verses.rationale: Retains the stopping point without an invented cause.
verses.before: When the vessels were full, she said to her son, “Bring me another vessel.” But he said to her, “There is no more vessel.” Then the oil stopped.
verses.after: When the jars were full, she said to her son, “Bring another jar.” “There are no more,” he answered. Then the oil stopped.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the vessels were full, she said to her son, “Bring me another vessel.” But he said to her, “There is no more vessel.” Then the oil stopped.

verses.rationale: Keeps both debt repayment and continuing provision.
verses.before: She came and told the man of God, and he said, “Go, sell the oil and pay your debt, and you and your sons live on what remains.”
verses.after: She went and told the man of God. He said, “Go, sell the oil, and pay your debt. You and your sons can live on what remains.”
verses.tsw_comparator: She came and told the man of God, and he said, “Go, sell the oil and pay your debt, and you and your sons live on what remains.”

verses.rationale: Preserves her standing and initiative.
verses.before: One day Elisha passed through Shunem, and there was a great woman there, and she urged him to eat bread. So whenever he passed by, he would turn aside there to eat bread.
verses.after: One day Elisha passed through Shunem. A prominent woman there urged him to eat with her. After that, whenever he passed through, he stopped there for a meal.
verses.tsw_comparator: One day Elisha passed through Shunem, and there was a great woman there, and she urged him to eat bread. So whenever he passed by, he would turn aside there to eat bread.

verses.rationale: Keeps recognition attributed to the woman.
verses.before: She said to her husband, “Look now, I know that this is a holy man of God who continually passes by us.
verses.after: She told her husband, “I know this man who regularly passes our way is a holy man of God.
verses.tsw_comparator: She said to her husband, “Look now, I know that this is a holy man of God who continually passes by us.

verses.rationale: Retains modest room and all furnishings.
verses.before: Please let us make a small upper room with walls and put there for him a bed, a table, a chair, and a lamp. Then when he comes to us, he may turn aside there.”
verses.after: Let us make a small walled upper room and put a bed, table, chair, and lampstand there for him. When he visits, he can stay there.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Please let us make a small upper room with walls and put there for him a bed, a table, a chair, and a lamp. Then when he comes to us, he may turn aside there.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the hospitality’s use concrete.
verses.before: One day he came there, turned aside to the upper room, and lay down there.
verses.after: One day he arrived, went up to the room, and lay down there.
verses.tsw_comparator: One day he came there, turned aside to the upper room, and lay down there.

verses.rationale: Introduces Gehazi and preserves the pronoun’s openness.
verses.before: He said to Gehazi his servant, “Call this Shunammite.” He called her, and she stood before him.
verses.after: He told his servant Gehazi, “Call the Shunammite woman.” Gehazi called her, and she stood before him.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to Gehazi his servant, “Call this Shunammite.” He called her, and she stood before him.

verses.rationale: Keeps mediated offer and her understated refusal.
verses.before: He said to him, “Please say to her, ‘Look, you have taken all this trouble for us. What is to be done for you? Is there something to speak for you to the king or to the commander of the army?’” She said, “I live among my own people.”
verses.after: Elisha told him, “Say to her, ‘You have gone to all this trouble for us. What can be done for you? Shall we speak to the king or the army commander on your behalf?’” She answered, “I live among my own people.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to him, “Please say to her, ‘Look, you have taken all this trouble for us. What is to be done for you? Is there something to speak for you to the king or to the commander of the army?’” She said, “I live among my own people.”

verses.rationale: Does not turn Gehazi’s observation into her request.
verses.before: He said, “Then what is to be done for her?” Gehazi said, “Actually, she has no son, and her husband is old.”
verses.after: “Then what can be done for her?” he asked. Gehazi answered, “She has no son, and her husband is old.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “Then what is to be done for her?” Gehazi said, “Actually, she has no son, and her husband is old.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the renewed summons and threshold.
verses.before: He said, “Call her.” He called her, and she stood in the doorway.
verses.after: Elisha said, “Call her.” He called her, and she stood in the doorway.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “Call her.” He called her, and she stood in the doorway.

verses.rationale: Retains promised embrace and resistance to false hope.
verses.before: He said, “At this appointed time, according to the time of life, you will embrace a son.” She said, “No, my lord, man of God! Do not deceive your servant.”
verses.after: “At this time next year,” he said, “you will hold a son in your arms.” She answered, “No, my lord, man of God! Do not deceive your servant.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “At this appointed time, according to the time of life, you will embrace a son.” She said, “No, my lord, man of God! Do not deceive your servant.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the promise’s fulfillment.
verses.before: But the woman conceived and bore a son at that appointed time, according to the time of life, just as Elisha had spoken to her.
verses.after: The woman conceived and bore a son at that time the next year, just as Elisha had told her.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the woman conceived and bore a son at that appointed time, according to the time of life, just as Elisha had spoken to her.

verses.rationale: Sets the later crisis in the field.
verses.before: The child grew. One day he went out to his father, to the reapers.
verses.after: The child grew. One day he went out to his father among the harvesters.
verses.tsw_comparator: The child grew. One day he went out to his father, to the reapers.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated cry without diagnosing illness.
verses.before: He said to his father, “My head! My head!” He said to the servant, “Carry him to his mother.”
verses.after: “My head! My head!” he cried to his father. His father told a servant, “Carry him to his mother.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to his father, “My head! My head!” He said to the servant, “Carry him to his mother.”

verses.rationale: Preserves bodily closeness and explicit death.
verses.before: He carried him and brought him to his mother, and he sat on her knees until noon, and then he died.
verses.after: The servant carried him to his mother. He sat on her knees until noon, then died.
verses.tsw_comparator: He carried him and brought him to his mother, and he sat on her knees until noon, and then he died.

verses.rationale: Keeps her deliberate actions without invented feelings.
verses.before: She went up and laid him on the bed of the man of God, shut the door behind him, and went out.
verses.after: She went upstairs and laid him on the man of God’s bed, shut the door, and went out.
verses.tsw_comparator: She went up and laid him on the bed of the man of God, shut the door behind him, and went out.

verses.rationale: Clarifies the practical request.
verses.before: She called to her husband and said, “Please send me one of the young men and one of the donkeys, so that I may run to the man of God and return.”
verses.after: She called her husband: “Please send me a servant and a donkey so I can hurry to the man of God and return.”
verses.tsw_comparator: She called to her husband and said, “Please send me one of the young men and one of the donkeys, so that I may run to the man of God and return.”

verses.rationale: Keeps her brief shalom reply without explaining it away.
verses.before: He said, “Why are you going to him today? It is neither new moon nor Sabbath.” She said, “It is well.”
verses.after: “Why go to him today?” he asked. “It is neither new moon nor Sabbath.” “All is well,” she said.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “Why are you going to him today? It is neither new moon nor Sabbath.” She said, “It is well.”

verses.rationale: Preserves her urgency and direction.
verses.before: Then she saddled the donkey and said to her young man, “Drive and go forward. Do not slow the riding for me unless I tell you.”
verses.after: She saddled the donkey and told her servant, “Drive on. Do not slow down for me unless I tell you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then she saddled the donkey and said to her young man, “Drive and go forward. Do not slow the riding for me unless I tell you.”

verses.rationale: Keeps recognition and destination.
verses.before: So she went and came to the man of God at Mount Carmel. When the man of God saw her from a distance, he said to Gehazi his servant, “Look, there is the Shunammite.
verses.after: She traveled to the man of God at Mount Carmel. When he saw her in the distance, he told Gehazi, “There is the Shunammite woman.
verses.tsw_comparator: So she went and came to the man of God at Mount Carmel. When the man of God saw her from a distance, he said to Gehazi his servant, “Look, there is the Shunammite.

verses.rationale: Retains three inquiries and repeated reserved answer.
verses.before: Now run to meet her and say to her, ‘Is it well with you? Is it well with your husband? Is it well with the child?’” She said, “It is well.”
verses.after: Run to meet her. Ask, ‘Is all well with you? With your husband? With the child?’” She answered, “All is well.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Now run to meet her and say to her, ‘Is it well with you? Is it well with your husband? Is it well with the child?’” She said, “It is well.”

verses.rationale: Preserves her grief and the prophet’s admitted ignorance.
verses.before: But when she came to the man of God at the mountain, she took hold of his feet. Gehazi came near to push her away, but the man of God said, “Leave her alone, for her life is bitter within her, and the LORD has hidden it from me and has not told me.”
verses.after: When she reached the man of God on the mountain, she grasped his feet. Gehazi came to push her away, but the man of God said, “Leave her alone. She is in bitter distress, and the LORD has hidden it from me. He has not told me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But when she came to the man of God at the mountain, she took hold of his feet. Gehazi came near to push her away, but the man of God said, “Leave her alone, for her life is bitter within her, and the LORD has hidden it from me and has not told me.”

verses.rationale: Keeps her accusation rather than moralizing grief.
verses.before: Then she said, “Did I ask a son from my lord? Did I not say, ‘Do not deceive me’?”
verses.after: She said, “Did I ask my lord for a son? Didn’t I say, ‘Do not mislead me’?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then she said, “Did I ask a son from my lord? Did I not say, ‘Do not deceive me’?”

verses.rationale: Preserves all urgent instructions.
verses.before: He said to Gehazi, “Gird up your waist, take my staff in your hand, and go. If you meet anyone, do not greet him, and if someone greets you, do not answer him. Lay my staff upon the face of the boy.”
verses.after: Elisha told Gehazi, “Tuck up your clothes, take my staff, and go. If you meet anyone, do not greet them; if someone greets you, do not answer. Lay my staff on the boy’s face.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to Gehazi, “Gird up your waist, take my staff in your hand, and go. If you meet anyone, do not greet him, and if anyone greets you, do not answer him. Lay my staff upon the face of the boy.”

verses.rationale: Retains the oath echoing Elisha’s earlier loyalty.
verses.before: But the mother of the boy said, “As the LORD lives and as your life lives, I will not leave you.” So he arose and followed her.
verses.after: But the boy’s mother said, “As the LORD lives, and as you live, I will not leave you.” So Elisha got up and followed her.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the mother of the boy said, “As the LORD lives and as your life lives, I will not leave you.” So he arose and followed her.

verses.rationale: Does not conceal failure of the first intervention.
verses.before: Gehazi passed on before them and laid the staff upon the face of the boy, but there was no voice and no response. So he returned to meet him and told him, saying, “The boy has not awakened.”
verses.after: Gehazi went ahead and laid the staff on the boy’s face. There was no sound or response. He went back to meet Elisha and said, “The boy has not awakened.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Gehazi passed on before them and laid the staff upon the face of the boy, but there was no voice and no response. So he returned to meet him and told him, saying, “The boy has not awakened.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the narrator’s explicit confirmation.
verses.before: Elisha came into the house, and look, the boy was dead, lying on his bed.
verses.after: Elisha entered the house. The boy was dead, lying on his bed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Elisha came into the house, and look, the boy was dead, lying on his bed.

verses.rationale: Keeps privacy and prayer.
verses.before: He went in, shut the door behind the two of them, and prayed to the LORD.
verses.after: He went inside, shut the door on the two of them, and prayed to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: He went in, shut the door behind the two of them, and prayed to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains bodily sequence without modern medical explanation.
verses.before: Then he went up and lay upon the child, put his mouth upon his mouth, his eyes upon his eyes, and his palms upon his palms. He stretched himself upon him, and the flesh of the child became warm.
verses.after: He climbed onto the bed and lay over the child, mouth to mouth, eyes to eyes, hands to hands. As he stretched over him, the child’s body grew warm.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he went up and lay upon the child, put his mouth upon his mouth, his eyes upon his eyes, and his palms upon his palms. He stretched himself upon him, and the flesh of the child became warm.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated effort and seven sneezes.
verses.before: Then he returned and walked in the house once back and forth. He went up and stretched himself upon him again. The boy sneezed seven times, and the boy opened his eyes.
verses.after: Elisha got up and walked back and forth in the house, then climbed up and stretched over him again. The boy sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he returned and walked in the house once back and forth. He went up and stretched himself upon him again. The boy sneezed seven times, and the boy opened his eyes.

verses.rationale: Keeps the plain final invitation.
verses.before: He called Gehazi and said, “Call this Shunammite.” So he called her. When she came to him, he said, “Lift up your son.”
verses.after: He called Gehazi: “Call the Shunammite woman.” Gehazi called her, and she came. “Pick up your son,” Elisha said.
verses.tsw_comparator: He called Gehazi and said, “Call this Shunammite.” So he called her. When she came to him, he said, “Lift up your son.”

verses.rationale: Retains gratitude through actions rather than added speech.
verses.before: She came, fell at his feet, and bowed down to the ground. Then she lifted up her son and went out.
verses.after: She fell at his feet and bowed to the ground. Then she picked up her son and left.
verses.tsw_comparator: She came, fell at his feet, and bowed down to the ground. Then she lifted up her son and went out.

verses.rationale: Keeps communal hunger and practical response.
verses.before: Elisha returned to Gilgal, and there was famine in the land. The sons of the prophets were sitting before him, and he said to his servant, “Set on the large pot and cook stew for the sons of the prophets.”
verses.after: Elisha returned to Gilgal during a famine. The company of prophets sat before him. He told his servant, “Put the large pot on and cook stew for the prophets.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Elisha returned to Gilgal, and there was famine in the land. The sons of the prophets were sitting before him, and he said to his servant, “Set on the large pot and cook stew for the sons of the prophets.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the plant uncertainty and mistake.
verses.before: One went out into the field to gather herbs and found a wild vine and gathered from it his garment full of wild gourds. He came and sliced them into the stew pot, though they did not know what they were.
verses.after: One went into the fields to gather greens. He found a wild vine and filled his garment with wild gourds. He came back and sliced them into the stew, not knowing what they were.
verses.tsw_comparator: One went out into the field to gather herbs and found a wild vine and gathered from it his garment full of wild gourds. He came and sliced them into the stew pot, though they did not know what they were.

verses.rationale: Retains the vivid warning.
verses.before: They poured it out for the men to eat. And it happened as they were eating from the stew that they cried out and said, “Man of God, there is death in the pot!” And they were not able to eat it.
verses.after: They served the men, but as they tasted the stew they cried, “Death in the pot, man of God!” They could not eat it.
verses.tsw_comparator: They poured it out for the men to eat. And it happened as they were eating from the stew that they cried out and said, “Man of God, there is death in the pot!” And they were not able to eat it.

verses.rationale: Keeps remedy and outcome without explaining chemistry.
verses.before: He said, “Then bring flour.” He threw it into the pot and said, “Pour it out for the people, and let them eat.” And there was nothing harmful in the pot.
verses.after: “Bring flour,” Elisha said. He threw it into the pot and said, “Serve the people so they can eat.” There was nothing harmful in the pot.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “Then bring flour.” He threw it into the pot and said, “Pour it out for the people, and let them eat.” And there was nothing harmful in the pot.

verses.rationale: Preserves origin, offering and quantities.
verses.before: A man came from Baal-Shalishah and brought the man of God bread of firstfruits, twenty loaves of barley and fresh ears of grain in his sack. Elisha said, “Give it to the people so that they may eat.”
verses.after: A man came from Baal-shalishah with firstfruits bread for the man of God: twenty barley loaves and fresh grain in his sack. Elisha said, “Give it to the people to eat.”
verses.tsw_comparator: A man came from Baal-Shalishah and brought the man of God bread of firstfruits, twenty loaves of barley and fresh ears of grain in his sack. Elisha said, “Give it to the people so that they may eat.”

verses.rationale: Retains objection and repeated command.
verses.before: But his attendant said, “How can I set this before one hundred men?” He said, “Give it to the people so that they may eat, for thus says the LORD: ‘They will eat and have some left.’”
verses.after: His attendant asked, “How can I set this before a hundred men?” Elisha answered, “Give it to the people to eat. The LORD says, ‘They will eat and have some left.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: But his attendant said, “How can I set this before one hundred men?” He said, “Give it to the people so that they may eat, for thus says the LORD: ‘They will eat and have some left.’”

verses.rationale: Preserves fulfillment’s shared wording.
verses.before: So he set it before them, and they ate and had some left, according to the word of the LORD.
verses.after: He set it before them. They ate and had some left, according to the LORD’s word.
verses.tsw_comparator: So he set it before them, and they ate and had some left, according to the word of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves divine victory for Aram and avoids modern diagnosis.
verses.before: Naaman, commander of the army of the king of Aram, was a great man before his lord and highly regarded, for by him the LORD had given victory to Aram. The man was a mighty warrior, but he had a skin disease.
verses.after: Naaman, the commander of Aram’s army, was a great man in his master’s eyes and highly honored, because through him the LORD had given Aram victory. He was a mighty warrior, but he had a serious skin disease.
verses.tsw_comparator: Naaman, commander of the army of the king of Aram, was a great man before his lord and highly regarded, for by him the LORD had given victory to Aram. The man was a mighty warrior, but he had a skin disease.

verses.rationale: Keeps captivity and girl’s age explicit.
verses.before: Now Aramean raiding bands had gone out and had taken captive from the land of Israel a little girl, and she served Naaman’s wife.
verses.after: Aramean raiders had captured a young girl from Israel. She served Naaman’s wife.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now Aramean raiding bands had gone out and had taken captive from the land of Israel a little girl, and she served Naaman’s wife.

verses.rationale: Preserves her initiative without inventing motives.
verses.before: She said to her mistress, “If only my lord were before the prophet who is in Samaria! Then he would cure him of his skin disease.”
verses.after: She told her mistress, “If only my master could see the prophet in Samaria! He would cure him of his skin disease.”
verses.tsw_comparator: She said to her mistress, “If only my lord were before the prophet who is in Samaria! Then he would cure him of his skin disease.”

verses.rationale: Clarifies the report’s royal recipient.
verses.before: Naaman went and told his lord, saying, “Thus and thus spoke the girl who is from the land of Israel.”
verses.after: Naaman went and told his master what the girl from Israel had said.
verses.tsw_comparator: Naaman went and told his lord, saying, “Thus and thus spoke the girl who is from the land of Israel.”

verses.rationale: Preserves amounts with implicit shekel unit.
verses.before: The king of Aram said, “Go, go, and I will send a letter to the king of Israel.” So he went and took in his hand ten talents of silver, six thousand shekels of gold, and ten changes of clothing.
verses.after: Aram’s king said, “Go. I will send a letter to Israel’s king.” Naaman left, taking ten talents of silver, six thousand gold shekels, and ten changes of clothes.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king of Aram said, “Go, go, and I will send a letter to the king of Israel.” So he went and took in his hand ten talents of silver, six thousand shekels of gold, and ten changes of clothing.

verses.rationale: Retains the demand directed at the king.
verses.before: He brought the letter to the king of Israel, saying, “And now, when this letter comes to you, look, I have sent to you Naaman my servant, so that you may cure him of his skin disease.”
verses.after: He brought Israel’s king the letter: “With this letter I am sending my servant Naaman to you, so you may cure his skin disease.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He brought the letter to the king of Israel, saying, “And now, when this letter comes to you, look, I have sent to you Naaman my servant, so that you may cure him of his skin disease.”

verses.rationale: Keeps fearful royal inference attributed to him.
verses.before: When the king of Israel read the letter, he tore his clothes and said, “Am I God, to kill and make alive, that this man sends to me to cure a man of his skin disease? But surely know and see that he is seeking a quarrel with me.”
verses.after: When Israel’s king read it, he tore his clothes. “Am I God, able to kill and give life?” he said. “This man sends me someone to cure of skin disease! You can see he is looking for a quarrel with me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: When the king of Israel read the letter, he tore his clothes and said, “Am I God, to kill and make alive, that this man sends to me to cure a man of his skin disease? But surely know and see that he is seeking a quarrel with me.”

verses.rationale: Keeps recognition as the promised result.
verses.before: When Elisha the man of God heard that the king of Israel had torn his clothes, he sent to the king, saying, “Why have you torn your clothes? Please let him come to me, and he will know that there is a prophet in Israel.”
verses.after: Elisha the man of God heard that Israel’s king had torn his clothes. He sent word: “Why tear your clothes? Let him come to me, and he will know there is a prophet in Israel.”
verses.tsw_comparator: When Elisha the man of God heard that the king of Israel had torn his clothes, he sent to the king, saying, “Why have you torn your clothes? Please let him come to me, and he shall know that there is a prophet in Israel.”

verses.rationale: Preserves status display without editorial explanation.
verses.before: So Naaman came with his horses and his chariots and stood at the entrance of Elisha’s house.
verses.after: Naaman arrived with his horses and chariot and stopped at Elisha’s door.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Naaman came with his horses and his chariots and stood at the entrance of Elisha’s house.

verses.rationale: Retains mediated instruction and cleansing language.
verses.before: Elisha sent a messenger to him, saying, “Go and wash seven times in the Jordan, and your flesh will return to you, and you will be clean.”
verses.after: Elisha sent a messenger to say, “Go and wash seven times in the Jordan. Your flesh will be restored, and you will be clean.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Elisha sent a messenger to him, saying, “Go and wash seven times in the Jordan, and your flesh will return to you, and you will be clean.”

verses.rationale: Preserves his expectation as quoted speech.
verses.before: Yet Naaman became angry and went away. He said, “Look, I said to myself, ‘He will surely come out to me, stand, call on the name of the LORD his God, wave his hand over the place, and cure the skin disease.’
verses.after: Naaman went away angry. “I thought he would surely come out to me,” he said, “stand and call on the name of the LORD his God, wave his hand over the place, and cure the diseased skin.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Naaman became angry and went away. He said, “Look, I said to myself, ‘He will surely come out to me, stand, call on the name of the LORD his God, wave his hand over the place, and cure the skin disease.’

verses.rationale: Follows read Amana and retains river comparison.
verses.before: Are not Abana and Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? Could I not wash in them and be clean?” So he turned and went away in fury.
verses.after: Aren’t Amana and Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, better than all Israel’s waters? Couldn’t I wash in them and be clean?” He turned away in a rage.
verses.tsw_comparator: Are not Abana and Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? Could I not wash in them and be clean?” So he turned and went away in fury.

verses.rationale: Keeps respectful address and lesser-demand argument.
verses.before: But his servants came near and spoke to him and said, “My father, if the prophet had spoken to you a great thing, would you not have done it? How much more when he said to you, ‘Wash and be clean’?”
verses.after: His servants came near and said, “My father, if the prophet had asked you to do something great, wouldn’t you have done it? How much more when he tells you, ‘Wash and be clean’?”
verses.tsw_comparator: But his servants came near and spoke to him and said, “My father, if the prophet had spoken to you a great thing, would you not have done it? How much more when he said to you, ‘Wash and be clean’?”

verses.rationale: Preserves seven immersions and child comparison.
verses.before: So he went down and dipped himself in the Jordan seven times according to the word of the man of God. His flesh returned like the flesh of a little child, and he was clean.
verses.after: So he went down and dipped himself in the Jordan seven times, as the man of God had said. His flesh became like a young boy’s, and he was clean.
verses.tsw_comparator: So he went down and dipped himself in the Jordan seven times according to the word of the man of God. His flesh returned like the flesh of a little child, and he was clean.

verses.rationale: Keeps confession and offered blessing-gift.
verses.before: Then he returned to the man of God, he and all his camp, and came and stood before him. He said, “Look, now I know that there is no God in all the earth except in Israel. And now, please take a gift from your servant.”
verses.after: He returned to the man of God with his whole company and stood before him. “Now I know there is no God anywhere on earth except in Israel,” he said. “Please accept a gift from your servant.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he returned to the man of God, he and all his camp, and came and stood before him. He said, “Look, now I know that there is no God in all the earth except in Israel. And now, please take a gift from your servant.”

verses.rationale: Retains oath and resistance to pressure.
verses.before: But he said, “As the LORD lives, before whom I stand, I will not take it.” Naaman urged him to take it, but he refused.
verses.after: Elisha answered, “As the LORD lives, whom I serve, I will accept nothing.” Though Naaman urged him, he refused.
verses.tsw_comparator: But he said, “As the LORD lives, before whom I stand, I will not take it.” Naaman urged him to take it, but he refused.

verses.rationale: Preserves earth request without supplying its purpose.
verses.before: Then Naaman said, “If not, please let there be given to your servant two mule-loads of earth, for your servant will no longer make burnt offering or sacrifice to other gods, but to the LORD.
verses.after: Naaman said, “If not, please let your servant take two mule-loads of earth. From now on your servant will offer neither burnt offering nor sacrifice to other gods, only to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Naaman said, “If not, please let there be given to your servant two mule-loads of earth, for your servant will no longer make burnt offering or sacrifice to other gods, but to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated troubling request without doctrinal resolution.
verses.before: In this matter may the LORD pardon your servant: when my lord goes into the house of Rimmon to bow down there, and he leans on my hand, and I bow down in the house of Rimmon—when I bow down in the house of Rimmon, may the LORD please pardon your servant in this matter.”
verses.after: But may the LORD forgive your servant in this: when my master enters Rimmon’s temple to bow down, he leans on my arm, and I bow there too. When I bow in Rimmon’s temple, may the LORD forgive your servant in this.”
verses.tsw_comparator: In this matter may the LORD pardon your servant: when my lord goes into the house of Rimmon to bow down there, and he leans on my hand, and I bow down in the house of Rimmon—when I bow down in the house of Rimmon, may the LORD please pardon your servant in this matter.”

verses.rationale: Keeps restrained reply and following transition.
verses.before: He said to him, “Go in peace.” And he went from him a short distance.
verses.after: “Go in peace,” Elisha said. After Naaman had traveled a short distance,
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to him, “Go in peace.” And he went from him a short distance.

verses.rationale: Preserves the oath used for self-interest.
verses.before: Yet Gehazi, servant of Elisha the man of God, said, “Look, my master spared Naaman this Aramean by not taking from his hand what he brought. As the LORD lives, I will run after him and take something from him.”
verses.after: Gehazi, the servant of Elisha the man of God, said to himself, “My master has let this Aramean Naaman go without accepting what he brought. As the LORD lives, I will run after him and get something.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But Gehazi, servant of Elisha the man of God, said, “Look, my master spared Naaman this Aramean by not taking from his hand what he brought. As the LORD lives, I will run after him and take something from him.”

verses.rationale: Keeps Naaman’s concerned response.
verses.before: So Gehazi pursued Naaman. When Naaman saw someone running after him, he got down from the chariot to meet him and said, “Is all well?”
verses.after: Gehazi ran after Naaman. When Naaman saw him running behind him, he got down from his chariot to meet him. “Is all well?” he asked.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Gehazi pursued Naaman. When Naaman saw someone running after him, he got down from the chariot to meet him and said, “Is all well?”

verses.rationale: Preserves fabricated message as Gehazi’s speech.
verses.before: He said, “All is well. My master has sent me, saying, ‘Look, just now two young men from the sons of the prophets have come to me from the hill country of Ephraim. Please give them a talent of silver and two changes of clothing.’”
verses.after: “All is well,” Gehazi said. “My master sent me to say, ‘Two young men from the company of prophets have just come from Ephraim’s hills. Please give them a talent of silver and two changes of clothes.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “All is well. My master has sent me, saying, ‘Look, just now two young men from the sons of the prophets have come to me from the hill country of Ephraim. Please give them a talent of silver and two changes of clothing.’”

verses.rationale: Keeps doubled gift and carriers.
verses.before: Naaman said, “Please, take two talents.” He urged him and bound two talents of silver in two bags, with two changes of clothing, and gave them to two of his young men, and they carried them before him.
verses.after: Naaman said, “Please take two talents.” He urged him, tied two talents of silver into two bags, added two changes of clothes, and gave them to two servants to carry ahead of Gehazi.
verses.tsw_comparator: Naaman said, “Please, take two talents.” He urged him and bound two talents of silver in two bags, with two changes of clothing, and gave them to two of his young men, and they carried them before him.

verses.rationale: Preserves concealment through actions alone.
verses.before: When he came to the hill, he took them from their hand and deposited them in the house. Then he sent the men away, and they departed.
verses.after: When Gehazi reached the hill, he took the gifts from them and put them in the house. He sent the men away, and they left.
verses.tsw_comparator: When he came to the hill, he took them from their hand and deposited them in the house. Then he sent the men away, and they departed.

verses.rationale: Keeps direct inquiry and denial.
verses.before: He went in and stood before his master. Elisha said to him, “From where, Gehazi?” He said, “Your servant went nowhere.”
verses.after: He went in and stood before his master. Elisha asked, “Where have you been, Gehazi?” “Your servant has not gone anywhere,” he answered.
verses.tsw_comparator: He went in and stood before his master. Elisha said to him, “From where, Gehazi?” He said, “Your servant went nowhere.”

verses.rationale: Preserves heart image and expanded acquisitive list.
verses.before: He said to him, “Did not my heart go when the man turned from his chariot to meet you? Is it a time to take silver, to take garments, olive groves and vineyards, sheep and cattle, male servants and female servants?
verses.after: Elisha said, “Didn’t my heart go with you when the man stepped down from his chariot to meet you? Is this the time to acquire silver and clothes, olive groves and vineyards, sheep and cattle, male and female slaves?
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to him, “Did not my heart go when the man turned from his chariot to meet you? Is it a time to take silver, to take garments, olive groves and vineyards, sheep and cattle, male servants and female servants?

verses.rationale: Keeps inherited judgment and snow comparison.
