verses.before: So Naaman’s skin disease will cling to you and to your offspring forever.” Then he went out from before him diseased, like snow.
verses.after: Naaman’s skin disease will cling to you and your descendants forever.” Gehazi left him diseased, white as snow.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore Naaman’s skin disease shall cling to you and to your offspring forever.” Then he went out from before him diseased, like snow.

verses.rationale: Preserves shared space without deciding residence versus meeting.
verses.before: The sons of the prophets said to Elisha, “Look, the place where we live before you is too cramped for us.
verses.after: The company of prophets told Elisha, “The place where we meet with you is too small for us.
verses.tsw_comparator: The sons of the prophets said to Elisha, “Look, the place where we live before you is too cramped for us.

verses.rationale: Retains cooperative proposal and permission.
verses.before: Please let us go to the Jordan and take from there each person a beam, and let us make for ourselves a place there where we may live.” He said, “Go.”
verses.after: Let us go to the Jordan. Each of us can cut a beam, and we can make a place to stay there.” “Go,” he said.
verses.tsw_comparator: Please let us go to the Jordan and take from there each one a beam, and let us make for ourselves a place there where we may live.” He said, “Go.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the invitation and acceptance.
verses.before: One said, “Please agree to go with your servants.” He said, “I will go.”
verses.after: One asked, “Please come with your servants.” “I will,” Elisha answered.
verses.tsw_comparator: One said, “Please agree to go with your servants.” He said, “I will go.”

verses.rationale: Retains setting and work.
verses.before: So he went with them. They came to the Jordan and cut down trees.
verses.after: He went with them. They reached the Jordan and began cutting trees.
verses.tsw_comparator: So he went with them. They came to the Jordan and cut down trees.

verses.rationale: Preserves the practical cause of distress.
verses.before: And it happened as one was felling a beam that the iron axe head fell into the water. He cried out and said, “Ah, my lord! And it was borrowed!”
verses.after: As one of them cut a beam, the iron axhead fell into the water. “Oh, my lord!” he cried. “It was borrowed!”
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened as one was felling a beam that the iron axe head fell into the water. He cried out and said, “Ah, my lord! And it was borrowed!”

verses.rationale: Keeps the reported extraordinary action plainly.
verses.before: The man of God said, “Where did it fall?” He showed him the place. Then he cut a piece of wood, threw it there, and made the iron float.
verses.after: The man of God asked, “Where did it fall?” When he showed him, Elisha cut a stick and threw it there, and made the iron float.
verses.tsw_comparator: The man of God said, “Where did it fall?” He showed him the place. Then he cut a piece of wood, threw it there, and made the iron float.

verses.rationale: Preserves the man’s participation.
verses.before: He said, “Lift it for yourself.” So he stretched out his hand and took it.
verses.after: “Lift it out,” he said. The man reached out and took it.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “Lift it for yourself.” So he stretched out his hand and took it.

verses.rationale: Keeps unspecified location rather than inventing geography.
verses.before: Now the king of Aram was making war against Israel. He consulted with his servants, saying, “At such and such a place will be my camp.”
verses.after: Aram’s king was at war with Israel. He consulted his servants: “I will camp at such and such a place.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the king of Aram was making war against Israel. He consulted with his servants, saying, “At such and such a place shall be my camp.”

verses.rationale: Preserves warning and threat.
verses.before: But the man of God sent to the king of Israel, saying, “Guard yourself from passing this place, for the Arameans are going down there.”
verses.after: The man of God sent word to Israel’s king: “Be careful not to pass that place. The Arameans are coming down there.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But the man of God sent to the king of Israel, saying, “Guard yourself from passing this place, for the Arameans are going down there.”

verses.rationale: Supplies the implied messengers and retains the king’s personal caution and repeated warnings.
verses.before: So the king of Israel sent to the place concerning which the man of God had spoken to him and warned him. He guarded himself there, not once or twice.
verses.after: The king of Israel sent men to the place the man of God had warned him about. He was on his guard there, not just once or twice.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the king of Israel sent to the place concerning which the man of God had spoken to him and warned him. He guarded himself there, not once or twice.

verses.rationale: Retains suspicion as a royal question.
verses.before: The heart of the king of Aram was stormed over this matter, and he called his servants and said to them, “Will you not tell me who among us is for the king of Israel?”
verses.after: This greatly troubled Aram’s king. He called his servants and asked, “Will no one tell me which of us is on Israel’s king’s side?”
verses.tsw_comparator: The heart of the king of Aram was stormed over this matter, and he called his servants and said to them, “Will you not tell me who among us is for the king of Israel?”

verses.rationale: Preserves claim of intimate knowledge.
verses.before: One of his servants said, “No, my lord the king, but Elisha the prophet who is in Israel tells the king of Israel the words that you speak in your bedroom.”
verses.after: “None of us, my lord the king,” a servant answered. “Elisha, the prophet in Israel, tells Israel’s king even the words you speak in your bedroom.”
verses.tsw_comparator: One of his servants said, “No, my lord the king, but Elisha the prophet who is in Israel tells the king of Israel the words that you speak in your bedroom.”

verses.rationale: Keeps sequence from discovery to intended seizure.
verses.before: He said, “Go and see where he is, so that I may send and take him.” It was told to him, saying, “Look, he is in Dothan.”
verses.after: “Go and find out where he is,” the king said, “so I can send men to seize him.” He was told, “He is in Dothan.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “Go and see where he is, so that I may send and take him.” It was told to him, saying, “Look, he is in Dothan.”

verses.rationale: Preserves timing and encirclement.
verses.before: So he sent there horses, chariots, and a strong force. They came by night and surrounded the city.
verses.after: He sent horses, chariots, and a large force there. They arrived at night and surrounded the town.
verses.tsw_comparator: So he sent there horses, chariots, and a strong force. They came by night and surrounded the city.

verses.rationale: Keeps fearful perception through the attendant.
verses.before: The servant of the man of God rose early and went out, and look, an army with horses and chariots was surrounding the city. His servant said to him, “Ah, my lord! What will we do?”
verses.after: The man of God’s attendant rose early and went outside. An army with horses and chariots surrounded the town. “Oh, my lord, what shall we do?” he asked.
verses.tsw_comparator: The servant of the man of God rose early and went out, and look, an army with horses and chariots was surrounding the city. His servant said to him, “Ah, my lord! What shall we do?”

verses.rationale: Preserves comparison without naming unseen beings prematurely.
verses.before: He said, “Do not fear, for people who are with us are more than people who are with them.”
verses.after: “Do not be afraid,” Elisha answered. “Those with us outnumber those with them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “Do not fear, for those who are with us are more than those who are with them.”

verses.rationale: Keeps opened sight and fiery protection.
verses.before: Then Elisha prayed and said, “O LORD, please open his eyes so that he may see.” The LORD opened the eyes of the young man, and he saw, and look, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha.
verses.after: Elisha prayed, “LORD, please open his eyes so he can see.” The LORD opened the young man’s eyes. He saw the hills full of horses and chariots of fire around Elisha.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Elisha prayed and said, “O LORD, please open his eyes so that he may see.” The LORD opened the eyes of the young man, and he saw, and look, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha.

verses.rationale: Preserves divine action and prayer.
verses.before: When the Arameans came down to him, Elisha prayed to the LORD and said, “Please strike this nation with blindness.” So he struck them with blindness according to the word of Elisha.
verses.after: As the Arameans came down toward him, Elisha prayed to the LORD, “Please strike these people with blindness.” He struck them with blindness, as Elisha asked.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the Arameans came down to him, Elisha prayed to the LORD and said, “Please strike this nation with blindness.” So he struck them with blindness according to the word of Elisha.

verses.rationale: Does not explain away misleading speech.
verses.before: Elisha said to them, “This is not the way, and this is not the city. Follow me, and I will lead you to the man whom you seek.” And he led them to Samaria.
verses.after: Elisha told them, “This is not the road or the town. Follow me, and I will take you to the man you are looking for.” He led them to Samaria.
verses.tsw_comparator: Elisha said to them, “This is not the way, and this is not the city. Follow me, and I will lead you to the man whom you seek.” And he led them to Samaria.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated opening of eyes.
verses.before: And it happened when they came into Samaria that Elisha said, “O LORD, open the eyes of these men so that they may see.” The LORD opened their eyes, and they saw, and look, they were among Samaria.
verses.after: When they entered Samaria, Elisha said, “LORD, open their eyes so they can see.” The LORD opened their eyes, and they saw they were inside Samaria.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened when they came into Samaria that Elisha said, “O LORD, open the eyes of these men so that they may see.” The LORD opened their eyes, and they saw, and look, they were in the midst of Samaria.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated eagerness and filial address.
verses.before: When the king of Israel saw them, he said to Elisha, “Will I strike them? Will I strike them, my father?”
verses.after: When Israel’s king saw them, he asked Elisha, “Shall I strike them down, my father? Shall I?”
verses.tsw_comparator: When the king of Israel saw them, he said to Elisha, “Shall I strike them? Shall I strike them, my father?”

verses.rationale: Keeps rhetorical question and concrete mercy.
verses.before: He said, “You will not strike them. Would you strike those whom you have captured with your sword and your bow? Set bread and water before them so that they may eat and drink and go to their lord.”
verses.after: “Do not strike them,” he answered. “Would you strike down those you had captured with your sword and bow? Set bread and water before them. Let them eat and drink, then return to their master.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “You shall not strike them. Would you strike those whom you have captured with your sword and your bow? Set bread and water before them so that they may eat and drink and go to their lord.”

verses.rationale: Preserves feast and stated cessation of raids.
verses.before: So he prepared a great feast for them. They ate and drank, and he sent them away, and they went to their lord. And the raiding bands of Aram did not continue coming into the land of Israel.
verses.after: The king prepared a great feast. They ate and drank, and he sent them back to their master. Aramean raiding bands no longer came into Israel’s land.
verses.tsw_comparator: So he prepared a great feast for them. They ate and drank, and he sent them away, and they went to their lord. And the raiding bands of Aram did not continue coming into the land of Israel.

verses.rationale: Retains renewed war beside the preceding peace.
verses.before: After this Ben-Hadad king of Aram gathered all his army and went up and besieged Samaria.
verses.after: Afterward, Ben-hadad king of Aram gathered his whole army and besieged Samaria.
verses.tsw_comparator: After this Ben-Hadad king of Aram gathered all his army and went up and besieged Samaria.

verses.rationale: Keeps appalling prices and disputed dung term.
verses.before: There was a great famine in Samaria, and look, they besieged it until a donkey’s head was sold for eighty shekels of silver and a quarter of a kab of dove’s dung for five shekels of silver.
verses.after: Famine grew severe in Samaria under the siege. A donkey’s head sold for eighty silver shekels, and a quarter-kab of dove dung for five.
verses.tsw_comparator: There was a great famine in Samaria, and look, they besieged it until a donkey’s head was sold for eighty shekels of silver and a quarter of a kab of dove’s dung for five shekels of silver.

verses.rationale: Preserves appeal from a suffering subject.
verses.before: As the king of Israel was passing by upon the wall, a woman cried out to him, saying, “Save, my lord the king!”
verses.after: As Israel’s king walked along the wall, a woman cried to him, “Help me, my lord the king!”
verses.tsw_comparator: As the king of Israel was passing by upon the wall, a woman cried out to him, saying, “Save, my lord the king!”

verses.rationale: Uses conditional reading while preserving alternative for notes.
verses.before: He said, “If the LORD does not save you, from where will I save you? From the threshing floor or from the winepress?”
verses.after: He answered, “If the LORD does not help you, where can I find help for you? From the threshing floor? From the winepress?”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “If the LORD does not save you, from where shall I save you? From the threshing floor or from the winepress?”

verses.rationale: Keeps the horror in the woman’s testimony.
verses.before: The king said to her, “What is it with you?” She said, “This woman said to me, ‘Give your son, and we will eat him today, and my son we will eat tomorrow.’
verses.after: Then he asked, “What is wrong?” She said, “This woman told me, ‘Give up your son so we can eat him today. We will eat mine tomorrow.’
verses.tsw_comparator: The king said to her, “What is it with you?” She said, “This woman said to me, ‘Give your son, and we will eat him today, and my son we will eat tomorrow.’

verses.rationale: Preserves cannibalism explicitly without added spectacle.
verses.before: So we boiled my son and ate him. The next day I said to her, ‘Give your son, and we will eat him,’ but she hid her son.”
verses.after: We boiled my son and ate him. The next day I said, ‘Give up your son so we can eat him.’ But she hid her son.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So we boiled my son and ate him. The next day I said to her, ‘Give your son, and we will eat him,’ but she hid her son.”

verses.rationale: Keeps public grief and concealed sackcloth.
verses.before: When the king heard the words of the woman, he tore his clothes. As he passed by upon the wall, the people looked, and look, sackcloth was beneath upon his body.
verses.after: When the king heard her words, he tore his clothes. As he passed along the wall, the people saw sackcloth beneath them, against his skin.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the king heard the words of the woman, he tore his clothes. As he passed by upon the wall, the people looked, and behold, sackcloth was beneath upon his body.

verses.rationale: Retains oath threatening beheading.
verses.before: He said, “Thus may God do to me and more also if the head of Elisha son of Shaphat remains upon him today.”
verses.after: He said, “May God punish me, and more besides, if Elisha son of Shaphat’s head stays on his shoulders today!”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “Thus may God do to me and more also if the head of Elisha son of Shaphat remains upon him today.”

verses.rationale: Keeps accusation, defensive instruction and approaching master.
verses.before: Elisha was sitting in his house, and the elders were sitting with him. The king sent a man from before him. Before the messenger came to him, Elisha said to the elders, “Do you see how this son of a murderer has sent to remove my head? See, when the messenger comes, shut the door and hold him at the door. Is not the sound of his lord’s feet behind him?”
verses.after: Elisha was sitting at home with the elders. The king sent a man ahead of him. Before the messenger arrived, Elisha told the elders, “Do you see how this murderer’s son has sent someone to take off my head? When the messenger comes, shut the door and hold it against him. Isn’t the sound of his master’s footsteps behind him?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Elisha was sitting in his house, and the elders were sitting with him. The king sent a man from before him. Before the messenger came to him, Elisha said to the elders, “Do you see how this son of a murderer has sent to remove my head? See, when the messenger comes, shut the door and hold him at the door. Is not the sound of his lord’s feet behind him?”

verses.rationale: Leaves the final speaker uncertain as in the source.
verses.before: While he was still speaking with them, look, the messenger came down to him. And he said, “Look, this disaster is from the LORD. Why should I wait for the LORD any longer?”
verses.after: While he was still speaking, the messenger came down to him. Then came the words, “This disaster is from the LORD. Why should I wait for the LORD any longer?”
verses.tsw_comparator: While he was still speaking with them, behold, the messenger came down to him. And he said, “Look, this disaster is from the LORD. Why should I wait for the LORD any longer?”

verses.rationale: Retain both measures and the precise time and market location.
verses.before: Elisha said, “Hear the word of the LORD. Thus says the LORD: About this time tomorrow, a seah of fine flour will be sold for a shekel and two seahs of barley for a shekel at the gate of Samaria.”
verses.after: Elisha said, “Hear the LORD’s word! This is what the LORD says: Tomorrow about this time, a seah of fine flour will sell for a shekel, and two seahs of barley for a shekel, at Samaria’s gate.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Elisha said, “Hear the word of the LORD. Thus says the LORD: About this time tomorrow, a seah of fine flour will be sold for a shekel and two seahs of barley for a shekel at the gate of Samaria.”

verses.rationale: Keep the sky-window image and the seeing/eating contrast.
verses.before: Then the officer on whose hand the king leaned answered the man of God and said, “Look, even if the LORD made windows in the heavens, could this thing happen?” He said, “Look, you will see it with your eyes, but you will not eat from it.”
verses.after: The officer on whose arm the king leaned answered the man of God, “Even if the LORD opened windows in the sky, could this happen?” Elisha said, “You will see it with your own eyes, but you will not eat any of it.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the officer on whose hand the king leaned answered the man of God and said, “Look, even if the LORD made windows in the heavens, could this thing happen?” He said, “Look, you shall see it with your eyes, but you shall not eat from it.”

verses.rationale: Keep the excluded men and their urgent question without diagnosing Hansen’s disease.
verses.before: Now four men with skin disease were at the entrance of the gate. They said to one another, “Why are we sitting here until we die?
verses.after: Four men with a skin disease were at the entrance to the gate. They said to one another, “Why sit here until we die?
verses.tsw_comparator: Now four men with skin disease were at the entrance of the gate. They said to one another, “Why are we sitting here until we die?

verses.rationale: Preserve the repeated alternatives and their limited hope.
verses.before: If we say, ‘Let us enter the city,’ the famine is in the city, and we will die there. If we sit here, we will die. And now come, let us fall away to the camp of Aram. If they let us live, we will live; and if they put us to death, we will die.”
verses.after: If we decide to go into the city, the famine is there, and we will die there. If we stay here, we will die too. So let’s go over to the Aramean camp. If they let us live, we will live; if they kill us, we will die.”
verses.tsw_comparator: If we say, ‘Let us enter the city,’ the famine is in the city, and we will die there. If we sit here, we will die. And now come, let us fall away to the camp of Aram. If they let us live, we will live; and if they put us to death, we will die.”

verses.rationale: Retain dusk and the discovery at the camp’s edge.
verses.before: So they arose at twilight to go to the camp of Aram. They came to the edge of the camp of Aram, and look, there was no one there.
verses.after: At dusk they got up to go to the Aramean camp. When they reached its edge, no one was there.
verses.tsw_comparator: So they arose at twilight to go to the camp of Aram. They came to the edge of the camp of Aram, and look, there was no one there.

verses.rationale: Distinguish Adonai and retain the plural foreign kings in the soldiers’ inference.
verses.before: For the Lord had caused the camp of Aram to hear the sound of chariots, the sound of horses, the sound of a great army. They said to one another, “Look, the king of Israel has hired against us the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Egypt to come against us.”
verses.after: The Lord had made the Aramean army hear the sound of chariots, horses, and a great army. They said to one another, “Look! Israel’s king has hired the Hittite kings and the kings of Egypt to attack us!”
verses.tsw_comparator: For the Lord had caused the camp of Aram to hear the sound of chariots, the sound of horses, the sound of a great army. They said to one another, “Look, the king of Israel has hired against us the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Egypt to come against us.”

verses.rationale: Match dusk to verse 5 and preserve the abandoned animals.
verses.before: So they arose and fled at twilight and abandoned their tents, horses, and donkeys—the camp just as it was—and fled for their lives.
verses.after: So they fled at dusk, abandoning their tents, horses, and donkeys. They left the camp just as it was and ran for their lives.
verses.tsw_comparator: So they arose and fled at twilight and abandoned their tents, horses, and donkeys—the camp just as it was—and fled for their lives.

verses.rationale: Retain the two trips and concealment before the change of heart.
verses.before: When these men with skin disease came to the edge of the camp, they entered one tent, ate and drank, and carried from there silver, gold, and clothing and went and hid them. Then they returned and entered another tent, carried things from there, and went and hid them.
verses.after: When the men with the skin disease reached the edge of the camp, they entered a tent and ate and drank. They carried off silver, gold, and clothing and went and hid them. Then they returned, entered another tent, carried things off, and hid those too.
verses.tsw_comparator: When these men with skin disease came to the edge of the camp, they entered one tent, ate and drank, and carried from there silver, gold, and clothing and went and hid them. Then they returned and entered another tent, carried things from there, and went and hid them.

verses.rationale: Keep the moral recognition as the men’s speech rather than a narrator’s sermon.
verses.before: But they said to one another, “We are not doing right. This day is a day of good news, and we are keeping silent. If we wait until morning light, guilt will find us. And now come, let us go and tell the king’s household.”
verses.after: Then they said to one another, “What we’re doing isn’t right. This is a day of good news, and we’re keeping quiet. If we wait until morning, we will be held guilty. Come on—let’s go and tell the royal household.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But they said to one another, “We are not doing right. This day is a day of good news, and we are keeping silent. If we wait until morning light, guilt will find us. And now come, let us go and tell the king’s household.”

verses.rationale: Preserve both absence of people and absence of voices.
verses.before: So they came and called to the gatekeepers of the city and told them, saying, “We came to the camp of Aram, and look, there was no one there and no human voice—only horses tied, donkeys tied, and the tents as they were.”
verses.after: They went and called to the city’s gatekeepers: “We went into the Aramean camp. There wasn’t a person there, not even a human voice—only tethered horses and donkeys, and the tents left as they were.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So they came and called to the gatekeepers of the city and told them, saying, “We came to the camp of Aram, and look, there was no one there and no human voice—only horses tied, donkeys tied, and the tents as they were.”

verses.rationale: Make the relay of information clear without adding a named messenger.
verses.before: The gatekeepers called out, and they told it inside the king’s household.
verses.after: The gatekeepers called out the news, and it was reported inside the palace.
verses.tsw_comparator: The gatekeepers called out, and they told it inside the king’s household.

verses.rationale: Keep the suspected ambush explicitly the king’s interpretation.
verses.before: The king arose in the night and said to his servants, “Let me tell you what the Arameans have done to us. They know that we are hungry, so they have gone out from the camp to hide in the field, saying, ‘When they come out from the city, we will seize them alive and enter the city.’”
verses.after: The king got up in the night and said to his servants, “Let me tell you what the Arameans have done to us. They know we’re hungry, so they’ve left the camp to hide in the fields. They’re thinking, ‘When they come out of the city, we’ll take them alive and get into the city.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: The king arose in the night and said to his servants, “Let me tell you what the Arameans have done to us. They know that we are hungry, so they have gone out from the camp to hide in the field, saying, ‘When they come out from the city, we will seize them alive and enter the city.’”

verses.rationale: Retain the difficult repeated comparison with surviving and perished Israel.
verses.before: One of his servants answered and said, “Please let men take five of the horses that remain, which remain in the city. Look, they are like all the multitude of Israel that remains in it; look, they are like all the multitude of Israel that has perished. Let us send and see.”
verses.after: One of his servants answered, “Let some men take five of the horses still left in the city. Their fate will be like that of all the Israelites left here—like that of all the Israelites who have already perished. Let’s send them and see.”
verses.tsw_comparator: One of his servants answered and said, “Please let men take five of the horses that remain, which remain in the city. Look, they are like all the multitude of Israel that remains in it; look, they are like all the multitude of Israel that has perished. Let us send and see.”

verses.rationale: Keep two chariot teams distinct from the preceding proposal of five horses.
verses.before: So they took two chariots with horses, and the king sent after the army of Aram, saying, “Go and see.”
verses.after: They took two chariot teams, and the king sent them after the Aramean army, saying, “Go and see.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So they took two chariots with horses, and the king sent after the army of Aram, saying, “Go and see.”

verses.rationale: Retain the Jordan limit and physical evidence of hurried flight.
verses.before: They went after them as far as the Jordan, and look, all the way was full of garments and equipment that the Arameans had thrown away in their haste. The messengers returned and told the king.
verses.after: They followed them as far as the Jordan. The whole road was strewn with clothing and equipment the Arameans had thrown away in their haste. The messengers returned and told the king.
verses.tsw_comparator: They went after them as far as the Jordan, and look, all the way was full of garments and equipment that the Arameans had thrown away in their haste. The messengers returned and told the king.

verses.rationale: Repeat the promised prices exactly to make fulfillment audible.
verses.before: Then the people went out and plundered the camp of Aram. A seah of fine flour was sold for a shekel and two seahs of barley for a shekel, according to the word of the LORD.
verses.after: Then the people went out and plundered the Aramean camp. A seah of fine flour sold for a shekel, and two seahs of barley for a shekel, just as the LORD had said.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the people went out and plundered the camp of Aram. A seah of fine flour was sold for a shekel and two seahs of barley for a shekel, according to the word of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retain the officer’s identity, assignment, and manner of death.
verses.before: Now the king had appointed the officer on whose hand he leaned over the gate, but the people trampled him in the gate, and he died, just as the man of God had spoken when the king came down to him.
verses.after: The king had put the officer on whose arm he leaned in charge of the gate. The people trampled him there, and he died, just as the man of God had said when the king came down to him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the king had appointed the officer on whose hand he leaned over the gate, but the people trampled him in the gate, and he died, just as the man of God had spoken when the king came down to him.

verses.rationale: Preserve the full repeated prediction and its reversed order of commodities.
verses.before: And it happened just as the man of God had spoken to the king, saying, “Two seahs of barley for a shekel and a seah of fine flour for a shekel—about this time tomorrow at the gate of Samaria.”
verses.after: For when the man of God told the king, “Tomorrow about this time, two seahs of barley will sell for a shekel and a seah of fine flour for a shekel at Samaria’s gate,”
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened just as the man of God had spoken to the king, saying, “Two seahs of barley for a shekel and a seah of fine flour for a shekel—about this time tomorrow at the gate of Samaria.”

verses.rationale: Repeat the objection and answer rather than collapsing the retelling.
verses.before: The officer had answered the man of God and said, “Look, even if the LORD made windows in the heavens, could such a thing happen?” And he had said, “Look, you will see it with your eyes, but you will not eat from it.”
verses.after: the officer answered the man of God, “Even if the LORD opened windows in the sky, could this happen?” And he answered, “You will see it with your own eyes, but you will not eat any of it.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The officer had answered the man of God and said, “Look, even if the LORD made windows in the heavens, could such a thing happen?” And he had said, “Look, you shall see it with your eyes, but you shall not eat from it.”

verses.rationale: Keep the final repetition of the officer’s death.
verses.before: And so it happened to him, for the people trampled him in the gate, and he died.
verses.after: That is what happened to him: the people trampled him at the gate, and he died.
verses.tsw_comparator: And so it happened to him, for the people trampled him in the gate, and he died.

verses.rationale: Mark the earlier instruction and retain divine agency and seven years.
verses.before: Elisha spoke to the woman whose son he had restored to life, saying, “Rise and go, you and your household, and live as a resident alien wherever you can, for the LORD has called for a famine, and it will also come upon the land seven years.”
verses.after: Elisha had said to the woman whose son he had restored to life, “Get up and go away with your household. Stay wherever you can, because the LORD has called for a famine, and it will come on the land for seven years.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Elisha spoke to the woman whose son he had restored to life, saying, “Rise and go, you and your household, and live as a resident alien wherever you can, for the LORD has called for a famine, and it will also come upon the land seven years.”

verses.rationale: Repeat the duration and identify the place of temporary residence.
verses.before: The woman arose and did according to the word of the man of God. She went, she and her household, and lived as a resident alien in the land of the Philistines seven years.
verses.after: The woman did as the man of God said. She went away with her household and stayed in the land of the Philistines for seven years.
verses.tsw_comparator: The woman arose and did according to the word of the man of God. She went, she and her household, and lived as a resident alien in the land of the Philistines seven years.

verses.rationale: Keep house and field as the concrete objects of her appeal.
verses.before: At the end of seven years the woman returned from the land of the Philistines and went out to cry to the king concerning her house and concerning her field.
verses.after: At the end of seven years she returned from the land of the Philistines and went to appeal to the king for her house and field.
verses.tsw_comparator: At the end of seven years the woman returned from the land of the Philistines and went out to cry to the king concerning her house and concerning her field.

verses.rationale: Do not repair the chronology of Gehazi’s appearance after chapter 5.
verses.before: Now the king was speaking with Gehazi, servant of the man of God, saying, “Please recount to me all the great things that Elisha has done.”
verses.after: The king was talking with Gehazi, the man of God’s servant. “Tell me all the great things Elisha has done,” he said.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the king was speaking with Gehazi, servant of the man of God, saying, “Please recount to me all the great things that Elisha has done.”

verses.rationale: Keep the timing and both identifications rather than abbreviating the encounter.
verses.before: And it happened while he was recounting to the king how Elisha had restored the dead to life, look, the woman whose son he had restored to life cried out to the king concerning her house and field. Gehazi said, “My lord the king, this is the woman, and this is her son whom Elisha restored to life.”
verses.after: Just as Gehazi was telling the king how Elisha had restored the dead to life, the woman whose son he had restored came to appeal to the king for her house and field. Gehazi said, “My lord the king, this is the woman, and this is her son whom Elisha restored to life!”
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened while he was recounting to the king how Elisha had restored the dead to life, behold, the woman whose son he had restored to life cried out to the king concerning her house and field. Gehazi said, “My lord the king, this is the woman, and this is her son whom Elisha restored to life.”

verses.rationale: Retain the full period of restitution and avoid asserting the official’s anatomy.
verses.before: The king asked the woman, and she recounted it to him. Then the king appointed for her one court official, saying, “Restore all that belongs to her and all the produce of the field from the day she left the land until now.”
verses.after: The king questioned the woman, and she told him her story. He assigned a court official to her and said, “Restore everything that belongs to her, including all the produce of the field from the day she left the land until now.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The king asked the woman, and she recounted it to him. Then the king appointed for her one court official, saying, “Restore all that belongs to her and all the produce of the field from the day she left the land until now.”

verses.rationale: Keep the foreign setting and the report to the sick king.
verses.before: Elisha came to Damascus. Ben-Hadad king of Aram was sick, and it was told to him, saying, “The man of God has come here.”
verses.after: Elisha went to Damascus. Ben-hadad king of Aram was ill, and someone told him, “The man of God has come here.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Elisha came to Damascus. Ben-Hadad king of Aram was sick, and it was told to him, saying, “The man of God has come here.”

verses.rationale: Make the consultation through the prophet explicit.
verses.before: The king said to Hazael, “Take a gift in your hand and go to meet the man of God. Inquire of the LORD through him, saying, ‘Will I recover from this sickness?’”
verses.after: The king said to Hazael, “Take a gift with you and go meet the man of God. Ask the LORD through him, ‘Will I recover from this illness?’”
verses.tsw_comparator: The king said to Hazael, “Take a gift in your hand and go to meet the man of God. Inquire of the LORD through him, saying, ‘Will I recover from this sickness?’”

verses.rationale: Preserve forty loads and the diplomatic address your son.
verses.before: So Hazael went to meet him and took a gift in his hand, every good thing of Damascus, a load of forty camels. He came and stood before him and said, “Your son Ben-Hadad king of Aram has sent me to you, saying, ‘Will I recover from this sickness?’”
verses.after: Hazael went to meet him, taking a gift of every kind of fine thing Damascus had to offer—forty camel loads. He stood before Elisha and said, “Your son Ben-hadad king of Aram has sent me to ask, ‘Will I recover from this illness?’”
verses.tsw_comparator: So Hazael went to meet him and took a gift in his hand, every good thing of Damascus, a load of forty camels. He came and stood before him and said, “Your son Ben-Hadad king of Aram has sent me to you, saying, ‘Will I recover from this sickness?’”

verses.rationale: Follow the read text to him while preserving the tension between the two declarations.
verses.before: Elisha said to him, “Go, say to him, ‘You will surely recover.’ But the LORD has shown me that he will surely die.”
verses.after: Elisha said to him, “Go and tell him, ‘You will certainly recover.’ But the LORD has shown me that he will certainly die.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Elisha said to him, “Go, say to him, ‘You will surely recover.’ But the LORD has shown me that he will surely die.”

verses.rationale: Avoid fixing the ambiguous gaze’s participants or inventing a motive for the pause.
verses.before: He fixed his face and stared until Hazael was ashamed. Then the man of God wept.
verses.after: He held his gaze steady until it became uncomfortable. Then the man of God wept.
verses.tsw_comparator: He fixed his face and stared until Hazael was ashamed. Then the man of God wept.

verses.rationale: Preserve every threatened atrocity without softening or elaborating it.
verses.before: Hazael said, “Why is my lord weeping?” He said, “Because I know the evil that you will do to the children of Israel: you will set their fortresses on fire, kill their young men with the sword, dash their little children to pieces, and rip open their pregnant women.”
verses.after: Hazael asked, “Why is my lord weeping?” He answered, “Because I know the harm you will do to the Israelites. You will set their fortresses on fire, kill their young men with the sword, dash their little children to pieces, and rip open their pregnant women.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Hazael said, “Why is my lord weeping?” He said, “Because I know the evil that you will do to the children of Israel: you will set their fortresses on fire, kill their young men with the sword, dash their little children to pieces, and rip open their pregnant women.”

verses.rationale: Keep great thing and dog in Hazael’s response without turning it into a moral denial.
verses.before: Hazael said, “But what is your servant, this dog, that he should do this great thing?” Elisha said, “The LORD has shown me you as king over Aram.”
verses.after: Hazael said, “But what is your servant, a mere dog, that he could do such a great thing?” Elisha answered, “The LORD has shown me that you will be king over Aram.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Hazael said, “But what is your servant, this dog, that he should do this great thing?” Elisha said, “The LORD has shown me you as king over Aram.”

verses.rationale: Preserve the selective report and its omission of the predicted death.
verses.before: Then he went from Elisha and came to his lord. He said to him, “What did Elisha say to you?” He said, “He told me that you would surely recover.”
verses.after: He left Elisha and returned to his master, who asked, “What did Elisha say to you?” Hazael answered, “He told me that you would certainly recover.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he went from Elisha and came to his lord. He said to him, “What did Elisha say to you?” He said, “He told me that you would surely recover.”

verses.rationale: Identify the acting man from context and preserve the concrete killing action.
verses.before: But the next day he took the bed cover, dipped it in water, spread it over his face, and he died. Then Hazael became king in his place.
verses.after: The next day Hazael took a coverlet, dipped it in water, and spread it over the king’s face, and he died. Hazael became king in his place.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the next day he took the bed cover, dipped it in water, spread it over his face, and he died. Then Hazael became king in his place.

verses.rationale: Retain the overlapping reigns rather than harmonizing the chronology.
verses.before: In the fifth year of Joram son of Ahab king of Israel, while Jehoshaphat was king of Judah, Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah became king.
verses.after: In the fifth year of Joram son of Ahab, king of Israel, while Jehoshaphat was king of Judah, Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat began to reign as king of Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the fifth year of Joram son of Ahab king of Israel, while Jehoshaphat was king of Judah, Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah became king.

verses.rationale: Keep both numerical notices intact.
verses.before: He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.
verses.after: He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for eight years.
verses.tsw_comparator: He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Retain the marriage connection and the narrator’s evaluation.
verses.before: He walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as the house of Ahab had done, for the daughter of Ahab became his wife. He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD.
verses.after: He followed the way of Israel’s kings, as the house of Ahab had done, for Ahab’s daughter was his wife. He did what was evil in the LORD’s eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: He walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as the house of Ahab had done, for the daughter of Ahab became his wife. He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserve the lamp image and the dynastic promise.
verses.before: Yet the LORD was not willing to destroy Judah for the sake of David his servant, as he had spoken to him to give him a lamp for his sons all the days.
verses.after: Yet the LORD was unwilling to destroy Judah because of David his servant, since he had promised to give David a lamp for his sons always.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet the LORD was not willing to destroy Judah for the sake of David his servant, as he had spoken to him to give him a lamp for his sons all the days.

verses.rationale: Keep the political change concrete.
verses.before: In his days Edom rebelled from under the hand of Judah and set a king over themselves.
verses.after: In his days Edom rebelled against Judah’s rule and set up a king of its own.
verses.tsw_comparator: In his days Edom rebelled from under the hand of Judah and set a king over themselves.

verses.rationale: Retain the difficult battle sequence without inventing a decisive victory.
verses.before: Then Joram crossed over to Zair, and all the chariots with him. He arose by night and struck Edom, who had surrounded him, and the commanders of the chariots, but the people fled to their tents.
verses.after: Joram crossed over to Zair with all his chariots. He rose at night and struck the Edomites surrounding him and the chariot commanders. But his people fled to their tents.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Joram crossed over to Zair, and all the chariots with him. He arose by night and struck Edom, who had surrounded him, and the commanders of the chariots, but the people fled to their tents.

verses.rationale: Keep the narrator’s to this day and the separate revolt.
verses.before: So Edom rebelled from under the hand of Judah to this day. Then Libnah rebelled at that time.
verses.after: Edom has remained in rebellion against Judah’s rule to this day. Libnah also rebelled at that time.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Edom rebelled from under the hand of Judah to this day. Then Libnah rebelled at that time.

verses.rationale: Retain the source notice and Judah’s identity.
verses.before: Now the rest of the acts of Joram and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.after: The rest of Joram’s acts, and everything he did, are written in the annals of the kings of Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the rest of the acts of Joram and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?

verses.rationale: Keep the ancestral death idiom and succession.
verses.before: Joram lay down with his ancestors and was buried with his ancestors in the city of David. Ahaziah his son became king in his place.
verses.after: Joram rested with his ancestors and was buried with them in the City of David. His son Ahaziah became king in his place.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joram lay down with his ancestors and was buried with his ancestors in the city of David. Ahaziah his son became king in his place.

verses.rationale: Retain twelfth year despite the eleventh-year notice in 9:29.
verses.before: In the twelfth year of Joram son of Ahab king of Israel, Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah became king.
verses.after: In the twelfth year of Joram son of Ahab, king of Israel, Ahaziah son of Jehoram became king of Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the twelfth year of Joram son of Ahab king of Israel, Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah became king.

verses.rationale: Keep twenty-two and the source’s daughter relationship without importing Chronicles.
verses.before: Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Athaliah daughter of Omri king of Israel.
verses.after: Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for one year. His mother’s name was Athaliah, daughter of Omri king of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Athaliah daughter of Omri king of Israel.

verses.rationale: Preserve the repeated house language and marriage relationship.
verses.before: He walked in the way of the house of Ahab and did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, like the house of Ahab, for he was related by marriage to the house of Ahab.
verses.after: He followed the way of the house of Ahab and did what was evil in the LORD’s eyes, as the house of Ahab had done, for he was related by marriage to Ahab’s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: He walked in the way of the house of Ahab and did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, like the house of Ahab, for he was related by marriage to the house of Ahab.

verses.rationale: Keep the two allied kings and identify who was wounded.
verses.before: He went with Joram son of Ahab to war against Hazael king of Aram at Ramoth-Gilead, and the Arameans struck Joram.
verses.after: He went with Joram son of Ahab to fight Hazael king of Aram at Ramoth-gilead. The Arameans wounded Joram.
verses.tsw_comparator: He went with Joram son of Ahab to war against Hazael king of Aram at Ramoth-Gilead, and the Arameans struck Joram.

verses.rationale: Preserve both place forms and the relationship between the visit and battle wounds.
verses.before: King Joram returned to Jezreel to be healed from the wounds that the Arameans had struck him at Ramah when he fought against Hazael king of Aram. Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to see Joram son of Ahab in Jezreel because he was sick.
verses.after: King Joram returned to Jezreel to recover from the wounds the Arameans had inflicted on him at Ramah when he fought Hazael king of Aram. Ahaziah son of Jehoram, king of Judah, went down to Jezreel to see Joram son of Ahab because he was wounded.
verses.tsw_comparator: King Joram returned to Jezreel to be healed from the wounds that the Arameans had struck him at Ramah when he fought against Hazael king of Aram. Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to see Joram son of Ahab in Jezreel because he was sick.

verses.rationale: Render girding the waist as preparation for travel while retaining the oil flask.
verses.before: Elisha the prophet called one of the sons of the prophets and said to him, “Gird up your waist, take this flask of oil in your hand, and go to Ramoth-Gilead.
verses.after: Elisha the prophet called one of the company of prophets and said, “Tuck your robe into your belt, take this flask of oil with you, and go to Ramoth-gilead.
verses.tsw_comparator: Elisha the prophet called one of the sons of the prophets and said to him, “Gird up your waist, take this flask of oil in your hand, and go to Ramoth-Gilead.

verses.rationale: Preserve all three generations and the private setting.
verses.before: When you arrive there, look there for Jehu son of Jehoshaphat, son of Nimshi. Go in, make him rise from among his brothers, and bring him into an inner room.
verses.after: When you arrive, find Jehu son of Jehoshaphat, son of Nimshi. Go in, have him rise from among his fellow officers, and take him into an inner room.
verses.tsw_comparator: When you arrive there, look there for Jehu son of Jehoshaphat, son of Nimshi. Go in, make him rise from among his brothers, and bring him into an inner room.

verses.rationale: Keep the anointing formula and abrupt escape instruction.
verses.before: Take the flask of oil, pour it on his head, and say, ‘Thus says the LORD: I have anointed you king over Israel.’ Then open the door and flee; do not wait.”
verses.after: Take the flask of oil, pour it on his head, and say, ‘This is what the LORD says: I anoint you king over Israel.’ Then open the door and flee. Don’t wait.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Take the flask of oil, pour it on his head, and say, ‘Thus says the LORD: I have anointed you king over Israel.’ Then open the door and flee; do not wait.”

verses.rationale: Combine the repeated young-man description into natural English.
verses.before: So the young man, the young prophet, went to Ramoth-Gilead.
verses.after: So the young prophet went to Ramoth-gilead.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the young man, the young prophet, went to Ramoth-Gilead.

verses.rationale: Keep the uncertainty over the addressee and the repeated title.
verses.before: He came, and look, the commanders of the army were sitting. He said, “I have a word for you, commander.” Jehu said, “For which of us?” He said, “For you, commander.”
verses.after: When he arrived, the army commanders were sitting together. He said, “Commander, I have a message for you.” Jehu asked, “For which of us?” He answered, “For you, commander.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He came, and look, the commanders of the army were sitting. He said, “I have a word for you, commander.” Jehu said, “For which of us?” He said, “For you, commander.”

verses.rationale: Retain the expanded divine title and repeated people designation.
verses.before: He arose and went into the house. The young man poured the oil upon his head and said to him, “Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: I have anointed you king over the people of the LORD, over Israel.
verses.after: Jehu got up and went into the house. The prophet poured the oil on his head and said, “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I anoint you king over the LORD’s people, over Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: He arose and went into the house. The young man poured the oil upon his head and said to him, “Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: I have anointed you king over the people of the LORD, over Israel.

verses.rationale: Keep the blood language and Jezebel’s responsibility within the oracle.
verses.before: You will strike the house of Ahab your lord, so that I may avenge the blood of my servants the prophets and the blood of all the servants of the LORD from the hand of Jezebel.
verses.after: You are to strike down the house of Ahab your master, so that I may avenge the blood of my servants the prophets, and the blood of all the LORD’s servants, at Jezebel’s hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall strike the house of Ahab your lord, so that I may avenge the blood of my servants the prophets and the blood of all the servants of the LORD from the hand of Jezebel.

verses.rationale: Retain the coarse male image and the uncertain paired social categories.
verses.before: The whole house of Ahab will perish. I will cut off from Ahab every male, both slave and free in Israel.
verses.after: Ahab’s whole house will perish. I will cut off from Ahab every male who urinates against a wall, bound or free in Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: The whole house of Ahab shall perish. I will cut off from Ahab every male, both slave and free in Israel.

verses.rationale: Preserve both dynastic comparisons with their fathers’ names.
verses.before: I will make the house of Ahab like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah.
verses.after: I will make Ahab’s house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and the house of Baasha son of Ahijah.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will make the house of Ahab like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah.

verses.rationale: Keep the specified place and the prophet’s immediate departure.
verses.before: The dogs will eat Jezebel in the territory of Jezreel, and no one will bury her.” Then he opened the door and fled.
verses.after: Dogs will eat Jezebel on the plot of land at Jezreel, and no one will bury her.” Then he opened the door and fled.
verses.tsw_comparator: The dogs shall eat Jezebel in the territory of Jezreel, and no one shall bury her.” Then he opened the door and fled.

verses.rationale: Retain the officer’s dismissive label as speech rather than narrator judgment.
verses.before: Jehu came out to the servants of his lord, and one said to him, “Is all well? Why did this madman come to you?” He said to them, “You know the man and his talk.”
verses.after: Jehu came out to his master’s officers. One asked him, “Is everything all right? Why did that madman come to you?” He answered, “You know the man and his chatter.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Jehu came out to the servants of his lord, and one said to him, “Is all well? Why did this madman come to you?” He said to them, “You know the man and his talk.”

verses.rationale: Preserve the demand and Jehu’s selective quotation.
verses.before: But they said, “A lie! Please tell us.” So he said, “Thus and thus he spoke to me, saying, ‘Thus says the LORD: I have anointed you king over Israel.’”
verses.after: They said, “That’s a lie! Tell us.” So he said, “He told me this and that, including, ‘This is what the LORD says: I anoint you king over Israel.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: But they said, “A lie! Please tell us.” So he said, “Thus and thus he spoke to me, saying, ‘Thus says the LORD: I have anointed you king over Israel.’”

verses.rationale: Retain garments, the uncertain step location, and the proclamation.
verses.before: Then they hurried, and each took his garment and put it under him on the bare steps. They blew the ram’s horn and said, “Jehu is king!”
verses.after: At once each of them took his garment and spread it beneath Jehu on the bare steps. They blew the ram’s horn and proclaimed, “Jehu is king!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then they hurried, and each took his garment and put it under him on the bare steps. They blew the ram’s horn and said, “Jehu is king!”

verses.rationale: Connect the conspiracy with the military setting without importing motives.
verses.before: So Jehu son of Jehoshaphat, son of Nimshi, conspired against Joram. Now Joram had been guarding Ramoth-Gilead, he and all Israel, because of Hazael king of Aram.
verses.after: So Jehu son of Jehoshaphat, son of Nimshi, conspired against Joram. Joram and all Israel had been defending Ramoth-gilead against Hazael king of Aram.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Jehu son of Jehoshaphat, son of Nimshi, conspired against Joram. Now Joram had been guarding Ramoth-Gilead, he and all Israel, because of Hazael king of Aram.

verses.rationale: Keep the king’s absence and Jehu’s condition for secrecy.
verses.before: Yet King Joram had returned to Jezreel to be healed from the wounds that the Arameans had struck him when he fought with Hazael king of Aram. Jehu said, “If this is your desire, let no fugitive leave the city to go and tell it in Jezreel.”
verses.after: But King Joram had returned to Jezreel to recover from the wounds the Arameans had inflicted when he fought Hazael king of Aram. Jehu said, “If this is what you want, let no one escape from the city to take word to Jezreel.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But King Joram had returned to Jezreel to be healed from the wounds that the Arameans had struck him when he fought with Hazael king of Aram. Jehu said, “If this is your desire, let no fugitive leave the city to go and tell it in Jezreel.”

verses.rationale: Keep the convergence of all three kings.
verses.before: Then Jehu rode in a chariot and went to Jezreel, for Joram was lying there, and Ahaziah king of Judah had gone down to see Joram.
verses.after: Jehu mounted his chariot and went to Jezreel, where Joram lay recovering. Ahaziah king of Judah had come down to visit Joram.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Jehu rode in a chariot and went to Jezreel, for Joram was lying there, and Ahaziah king of Judah had gone down to see Joram.

verses.rationale: Preserve the watchtower perspective and recurring peace question.
verses.before: The watchman was standing on the tower in Jezreel, and he saw Jehu’s company as he came and said, “I see a company.” Joram said, “Take a horseman and send him to meet them, and let him say, ‘Is it peace?’”
verses.after: The lookout standing on Jezreel’s tower saw Jehu’s company approaching and said, “I see a company of men.” Joram said, “Send a horseman to meet them and ask, ‘Is it peace?’”
verses.tsw_comparator: The watchman was standing on the tower in Jezreel, and he saw Jehu’s company as he came and said, “I see a company.” Joram said, “Take a horseman and send him to meet them, and let him say, ‘Is it peace?’”

verses.rationale: Keep question, rebuff, and lookout report in sequence.
verses.before: So the rider on the horse went to meet him and said, “Thus says the king: ‘Is it peace?’” Jehu said, “What have you to do with peace? Turn behind me.” The watchman reported, saying, “The messenger came to them but does not return.”
verses.after: The horseman rode out to meet him and said, “The king asks, ‘Is it peace?’” Jehu answered, “What have you to do with peace? Fall in behind me.” The lookout reported, “The messenger reached them, but he isn’t coming back.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So the rider on the horse went to meet him and said, “Thus says the king: ‘Is it peace?’” Jehu said, “What have you to do with peace? Turn behind me.” The watchman reported, saying, “The messenger came to them but does not return.”

verses.rationale: Repeat the exchange as the source does.
verses.before: Then he sent a second rider on a horse. He came to them and said, “Thus says the king: ‘Is it peace?’” Jehu said, “What have you to do with peace? Turn behind me.”
verses.after: The king sent a second horseman. He reached them and said, “The king asks, ‘Is it peace?’” Jehu answered, “What have you to do with peace? Fall in behind me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he sent a second rider on a horse. He came to them and said, “Thus says the king: ‘Is it peace?’” Jehu said, “What have you to do with peace? Turn behind me.”

verses.rationale: Retain the madman link with verse 11 and the shortened patronymic.
verses.before: The watchman reported, saying, “He came to them but does not return, and the driving is like the driving of Jehu son of Nimshi, for he drives like a madman.”
verses.after: The lookout reported, “He reached them, but he isn’t coming back. The driving looks like Jehu son of Nimshi’s driving—he drives like a madman.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The watchman reported, saying, “He came to them but does not return, and the driving is like the driving of Jehu son of Nimshi, for he drives like a madman.”

verses.rationale: Keep the separate chariots and consequential meeting place.
verses.before: Joram said, “Harness!” So his chariot was harnessed. Joram king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah went out, each in his chariot. They went out to meet Jehu and found him in the property of Naboth the Jezreelite.
verses.after: Joram said, “Hitch up!” They hitched his chariot, and Joram king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah went out, each in his own chariot. They met Jehu on Naboth the Jezreelite’s plot of land.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joram said, “Harness!” So his chariot was harnessed. Joram king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah went out, each in his chariot. They went out to meet Jehu and found him in the property of Naboth the Jezreelite.

verses.rationale: Preserve the accusation’s force without converting its metaphor into biography.
verses.before: And it happened when Joram saw Jehu that he said, “Is it peace, Jehu?” He said, “What peace, as long as the prostitutions of Jezebel your mother and her sorceries are so many?”
verses.after: When Joram saw Jehu, he asked, “Is it peace, Jehu?” Jehu answered, “What peace can there be while your mother Jezebel’s whoring and her many sorceries go on?”
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened when Joram saw Jehu that he said, “Is it peace, Jehu?” He said, “What peace, as long as the prostitutions of Jezebel your mother and her sorceries are so many?”

verses.rationale: Keep the urgent direct warning.
verses.before: Then Joram turned his hands and fled and said to Ahaziah, “Treachery, Ahaziah!”
verses.after: Joram wheeled around and fled, calling to Ahaziah, “Treachery, Ahaziah!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Joram turned his hands and fled and said to Ahaziah, “Treachery, Ahaziah!”

verses.rationale: Retain the trajectory and bodily harm without added gore.
verses.before: Jehu drew his bow with his full strength and struck Joram between his arms. The arrow went out through his heart, and he sank down in his chariot.
verses.after: Jehu drew his bow with all his strength and struck Joram between the shoulders. The arrow came out through his heart, and he slumped in his chariot.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jehu drew his bow with his full strength and struck Joram between his arms. The arrow went out through his heart, and he sank down in his chariot.

verses.rationale: Retain the shared memory and prophetic burden image.
verses.before: Jehu said to Bidkar his officer, “Lift him and throw him into the field belonging to Naboth the Jezreelite. Remember when you and I rode together behind Ahab his father, and the LORD lifted up this pronouncement against him:
verses.after: Jehu said to Bidkar his officer, “Pick him up and throw him onto Naboth the Jezreelite’s plot. Remember how you and I rode together behind his father Ahab when the LORD pronounced this burden against him:
verses.tsw_comparator: Jehu said to Bidkar his officer, “Lift him and throw him into the field belonging to Naboth the Jezreelite. Remember when you and I rode together behind Ahab his father, and the LORD lifted up this pronouncement against him:

verses.rationale: Keep Naboth’s sons and yesterday rather than harmonizing with the earlier account.
verses.before: ‘Surely I saw yesterday the blood of Naboth and the blood of his sons,’ says the LORD, ‘and I will repay you in this field,’ says the LORD. And now, lift him and throw him into the field according to the word of the LORD.”
verses.after: ‘Yesterday I saw the blood of Naboth and the blood of his sons, declares the LORD. I will repay you on this plot, declares the LORD.’ So pick him up and throw him onto the plot, according to the LORD’s word.”
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘Surely I saw yesterday the blood of Naboth and the blood of his sons,’ says the LORD, ‘and I will repay you in this field,’ says the LORD. And now, lift him and throw him into the field according to the word of the LORD.”

verses.rationale: Supply the implied striking action while preserving the route and death location.

verses.after: When Ahaziah king of Judah saw this, he fled toward Beth-haggan. Jehu pursued him, saying, “Strike him too!” They struck him in his chariot at the ascent of Gur near Ibleam. He fled to Megiddo and died there.

verses.after: But when they went to bury her, they found only her skull, her feet, and the palms of her hands.

verses.rationale: Keep all four responding groups and their submission.

verses.tsw_comparator: So the one over the palace, the one over the city, the elders, and the guardians sent to Jehu, saying, “We are your servants, and all that you say to us we will do. We will not make anyone king. Do what is good in your eyes.”

verses.rationale: Keep the second letter’s deadline and the guardians’ responsibility.
verses.before: Then he wrote to them a second letter, saying, “If you are for me and listen to my voice, take the heads of the men, your lord’s sons, and come to me at Jezreel tomorrow at this time.” Now the king’s sons, seventy men, were with the great men of the city who were raising them.
verses.after: Jehu wrote them a second letter: “If you are on my side and will obey me, take the heads of your master’s sons and come to me at Jezreel by this time tomorrow.” The seventy royal sons were with the leading men of the city, who were raising them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he wrote to them a second letter, saying, “If you are for me and listen to my voice, take the heads of the men, your lord’s sons, and come to me at Jezreel tomorrow at this time.” Now the king’s sons, seventy men, were with the great men of the city who were raising them.

verses.rationale: Preserve the slaughter and transport without euphemism.

verses.after: When the letter reached them, they took the royal sons and slaughtered all seventy. They put their heads in baskets and sent them to Jehu at Jezreel.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened when the letter came to them that they took the king’s sons and slaughtered seventy men. They put their heads in baskets and sent them to him at Jezreel.

verses.rationale: Retain two heaps and the public display’s duration.

verses.after: A messenger came and told him, “They have brought the royal sons’ heads.” He said, “Put them in two heaps at the entrance to the gate until morning.”

verses.rationale: Keep the claim of innocence inside Jehu’s speech rather than endorsing it.

verses.rationale: Retain the falling-word image and Jehu’s appeal to prophecy.
verses.before: Know therefore that nothing from the word of the LORD will fall to the ground, which the LORD spoke concerning the house of Ahab. The LORD has done what he spoke by the hand of his servant Elijah.”
verses.after: Know, then, that not one word the LORD has spoken against Ahab’s house will fall to the ground. The LORD has done what he said through his servant Elijah.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Know therefore that nothing from the word of the LORD will fall to the ground, which the LORD spoke concerning the house of Ahab. The LORD has done what he spoke by the hand of his servant Elijah.”

verses.rationale: Keep the expanded circle of victims and totality claim.

verses.after: Jehu struck down everyone left of Ahab’s house in Jezreel—all his leading men, his close associates, and his priests. He left him no survivor.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Jehu struck all who remained of the house of Ahab in Jezreel, all his great men, his acquaintances, and his priests, until he left him no survivor.

verses.rationale: Retain the place name instead of replacing it with an uncertain function.

verses.after: Then he set out for Samaria. On the way, at Beth-eked of the Shepherds,
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he arose and came and went to Samaria. He was at Beth-Eked of the Shepherds on the way.

verses.rationale: Render brothers as wider kin in this context and retain both royal groups.

verses.after: Jehu met relatives of Ahaziah king of Judah. “Who are you?” he asked. They answered, “We are Ahaziah’s relatives. We’re going down to greet the king’s sons and the queen mother’s sons.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Jehu met the relatives of Ahaziah king of Judah and said, “Who are you?” They said, “We are relatives of Ahaziah, and we have come down to greet the sons of the king and the sons of the queen mother.”

verses.rationale: Preserve the contrast between live capture and subsequent killing.

verses.after: He said, “Take them alive!” They took them alive, then slaughtered them at the cistern of Beth-eked—all forty-two men. He left none of them alive.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “Take them alive.” So they took them alive and slaughtered them at the pit of Beth-Eked, forty-two men. He left not one of them.

verses.rationale: Keep the heart language and the physical pledge of alliance.

He blessed him and said to him, “Is your heart upright, as my heart is with your heart?” Jehonadab said, “It is.” “If it is, give me your hand.” So he gave him his hand, and Jehu brought him up to himself into the chariot.
verses.after: He went on from there and met Jehonadab son of Rechab coming toward him. Jehu greeted him and asked, “Is your heart true to mine, as mine is to yours?” Jehonadab answered, “It is.” “If so, give me your hand.” He gave him his hand, and Jehu brought him up into the chariot.
verses.tsw_comparator: He went from there and found Jehonadab son of Rechab coming to meet him. He blessed him and said to him, “Is your heart upright, as my heart is with your heart?” Jehonadab said, “It is.” “If it is, give me your hand.” So he gave him his hand, and Jehu brought him up to himself into the chariot.

verses.rationale: Make the narrator’s explicit disclosure of deceit clear.

verses.rationale: Retain the qualification and both calf locations.

verses.rationale: Keep the specific approval and four-generation promise without expanding it to all Jehu’s conduct.

verses.rationale: Preserve the narrator’s adverse judgment beside verse 30’s approval.

verses.after: But Jehu did not take care to walk in the instruction of the LORD, the God of Israel, with all his heart. He did not turn away from the sins Jeroboam had caused Israel to commit.
