verses.tsw_comparator: He was with her hidden in the house of the LORD six years, while Athaliah reigned over the land.

verses.rationale: Retain the named guard group and covenant before revealing the heir.
verses.before: In the seventh year Jehoiada sent and took the commanders of hundreds of the Carites and the guards and brought them to himself in the house of the LORD. He made a covenant with them and put them under oath in the house of the LORD, and he showed them the king’s son.
verses.after: In the seventh year Jehoiada sent for the commanders of hundreds of the Carites and the guards and brought them to him in the LORD’s house. He made a covenant with them, put them under oath there, and showed them the king’s son.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the seventh year Jehoiada sent and took the commanders of hundreds of the Carites and the guards and brought them to himself in the house of the LORD. He made a covenant with them and put them under oath in the house of the LORD, and he showed them the king’s son.

verses.rationale: Keep the first division and Sabbath change of duty.
verses.before: He commanded them, saying, “This is the thing that you will do: one third of you who come in on the Sabbath will keep watch over the king’s house;
verses.after: He commanded them, “This is what you must do: One third of you coming on duty on the Sabbath will guard the palace,
verses.tsw_comparator: He commanded them, saying, “This is the thing that you shall do: one third of you who come in on the Sabbath shall keep watch over the king’s house;

verses.rationale: Preserve the three posts and leave the difficult final term to a note.
verses.before: one third will be at the Gate of Sur, and one third at the gate behind the guards. You will keep watch over the house for defense.
verses.after: one third will be at the Sur Gate, and one third at the gate behind the guards. Keep a close watch over the palace.
verses.tsw_comparator: one third shall be at the Gate of Sur, and one third at the gate behind the guards. You shall keep watch over the house for defense.

verses.rationale: Distinguish off-duty divisions from the preceding incoming guards.
verses.before: And the two divisions of you who go out on the Sabbath will keep watch over the house of the LORD around the king.
verses.after: The other two divisions of you, all those going off duty on the Sabbath, must guard the LORD’s house around the king.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the two divisions of you who go out on the Sabbath shall keep watch over the house of the LORD around the king.

verses.rationale: Retain the lethal perimeter instruction and continuous protection.
verses.before: You will surround the king, each man with his weapons in his hand. Whoever comes within the ranks will be put to death. Be with the king when he goes out and when he comes in.”
verses.after: Surround the king, each man with his weapons in hand. Anyone who breaks through the ranks must be killed. Stay with the king wherever he goes.”
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall surround the king, each man with his weapons in his hand. Whoever comes within the ranks shall be put to death. Be with the king when he goes out and when he comes in.”

verses.rationale: Repeat both shifts in the execution of the order.
verses.before: The commanders of hundreds did according to all that Jehoiada the priest commanded. Each took his men, those coming in on the Sabbath together with those going out on the Sabbath, and came to Jehoiada the priest.
verses.after: The commanders of hundreds did everything Jehoiada the priest commanded. Each brought his men, those coming on duty on the Sabbath and those going off duty, to Jehoiada the priest.
verses.tsw_comparator: The commanders of hundreds did according to all that Jehoiada the priest commanded. Each took his men, those coming in on the Sabbath together with those going out on the Sabbath, and came to Jehoiada the priest.

verses.rationale: Keep the singular spear and Davidic provenance.
verses.before: The priest gave to the commanders of hundreds the spears and shields that had belonged to King David, which were in the house of the LORD.
verses.after: The priest gave the commanders of hundreds the spear and shields that had belonged to King David and were kept in the LORD’s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest gave to the commanders of hundreds the spears and shields that had belonged to King David, which were in the house of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Render right and left by the temple’s orientation while retaining the protective arrangement.
verses.before: The guards stood, each man with his weapons in his hand, from the south side of the house to the north side of the house, by the altar and the house, all around the king.
verses.after: The guards stood, each with his weapons in hand, from the south side of the house to its north side, around the altar and the house, surrounding the king.
verses.tsw_comparator: The guards stood, each man with his weapons in his hand, from the south side of the house to the north side of the house, by the altar and the house, all around the king.

verses.rationale: Preserve testimony as a distinct coronation object without specifying an unsupported document.
verses.before: Then he brought out the king’s son, put the crown upon him and the testimony, and they made him king and anointed him. They clapped their hands and said, “Long live the king!”
verses.after: Jehoiada brought out the king’s son, placed the crown on him, and gave him the covenant testimony. They made him king and anointed him, clapping their hands and calling, “Long live the king!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he brought out the king’s son, put the crown upon him and the testimony, and they made him king and anointed him. They clapped their hands and said, “Long live the king!”

verses.rationale: Keep the sound that draws her into the scene.
verses.before: Athaliah heard the sound of the guards and the people, and she came to the people at the house of the LORD.
verses.after: Athaliah heard the noise of the guards and the people and came to the people at the LORD’s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: Athaliah heard the sound of the guards and the people, and she came to the people at the house of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retain the customary pillar location and doubled cry.
verses.before: She looked, and look, the king was standing by the pillar according to the custom, with the commanders and the trumpeters beside the king, and all the people of the land rejoicing and blowing trumpets. Athaliah tore her clothes and cried, “Treason! Treason!”
verses.after: She looked, and there was the king standing by the pillar, as was customary. The commanders and trumpeters were beside him, and all the people of the land were rejoicing and blowing trumpets. Athaliah tore her clothes and cried, “Conspiracy! Conspiracy!”
verses.tsw_comparator: She looked, and behold, the king was standing by the pillar according to the custom, with the commanders and the trumpeters beside the king, and all the people of the land rejoicing and blowing trumpets. Athaliah tore her clothes and cried, “Treason! Treason!”

verses.rationale: Keep both the killing order and the restriction on its location.
verses.before: Then Jehoiada the priest commanded the commanders of hundreds who were appointed over the army and said to them, “Bring her out between the ranks. Whoever follows her, put to death with the sword.” For the priest had said, “She will not be put to death in the house of the LORD.”
verses.after: Jehoiada the priest ordered the commanders of hundreds in charge of the army, “Bring her out between the ranks. Kill anyone who follows her with the sword.” For the priest had said, “She must not be killed in the LORD’s house.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Jehoiada the priest commanded the commanders of hundreds who were appointed over the army and said to them, “Bring her out between the ranks. Whoever follows her, put to death with the sword.” For the priest had said, “She shall not be put to death in the house of the LORD.”

verses.rationale: Keep the route and execution place without importing another account.
verses.before: So they laid hands on her, and she went by the way of the horses’ entrance to the king’s house, and there she was put to death.
verses.after: They seized her and took her by the horses’ entrance to the palace, and she was killed there.
verses.tsw_comparator: So they laid hands on her, and she went by the way of the horses’ entrance to the king’s house, and there she was put to death.

verses.rationale: Make the two covenant relationships understandable.
verses.before: Jehoiada made a covenant between the LORD and the king and the people, that they should be the LORD’s people, and also between the king and the people.
verses.after: Jehoiada made a covenant between the LORD, the king, and the people, that they would be the LORD’s people. He also made a covenant between the king and the people.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jehoiada made a covenant between the LORD and the king and the people, that they should be the LORD’s people, and also between the king and the people.

verses.rationale: Preserve destruction and killing alongside the new guard arrangements.
verses.before: Then all the people of the land went to the house of Baal and tore it down. They completely broke its altars and images in pieces and killed Mattan priest of Baal before the altars. Then the priest appointed oversight over the house of the LORD.
verses.after: All the people of the land went to Baal’s temple and tore it down. They smashed its altars and images to pieces and killed Mattan, Baal’s priest, in front of the altars. Then the priest appointed guards over the LORD’s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then all the people of the land went to the house of Baal and tore it down. They completely broke its altars and images in pieces and killed Mattan priest of Baal before the altars. Then the priest appointed oversight over the house of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retain all participating groups and the route to enthronement.
verses.before: He took the commanders of hundreds, the Carites, the guards, and all the people of the land, and they brought the king down from the house of the LORD and came by the way of the gate of the guards to the king’s house. He sat upon the throne of the kings.
verses.after: He took the commanders of hundreds, the Carites, the guards, and all the people of the land, and they brought the king down from the LORD’s house. They entered the palace through the Guards’ Gate, and he sat on the royal throne.
verses.tsw_comparator: He took the commanders of hundreds, the Carites, the guards, and all the people of the land, and they brought the king down from the house of the LORD and came by the way of the gate of the guards to the king’s house. He sat upon the throne of the kings.

verses.rationale: Keep the concluding contrast without moralizing the quiet.
verses.before: All the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet after they had put Athaliah to death with the sword at the king’s house.
verses.after: All the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet. Athaliah had been put to death by the sword at the palace.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet after they had put Athaliah to death with the sword at the king’s house.

verses.rationale: Bind public 11:21 to original Hebrew 12:1.
verses.before: Joash was seven years old when he became king.
verses.after: Joash was seven years old when he became king.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joash was seven years old when he became king.

verses.rationale: Retain accession, duration, mother, and origin under public numbering.
verses.before: In the seventh year of Jehu, Joash became king, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Zibiah from Beersheba.
verses.after: Joash became king in Jehu’s seventh year and reigned in Jerusalem for forty years. His mother’s name was Zibiah, from Beer-sheba.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the seventh year of Jehu, Joash became king, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Zibiah from Beersheba.

verses.rationale: Preserve the relationship between instruction and conduct without importing later Chronicles events.
verses.before: Joash did what was right in the eyes of the LORD all his days in which Jehoiada the priest instructed him.
verses.after: Joash did what was right in the LORD’s eyes throughout the time Jehoiada the priest instructed him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joash did what was right in the eyes of the LORD all his days in which Jehoiada the priest instructed him.

verses.rationale: Keep the qualification to the favorable judgment.
verses.before: Only the high places were not removed. The people were still sacrificing and burning incense on the high places.
verses.after: Yet the high places were not removed. The people still sacrificed and burned offerings there.
verses.tsw_comparator: Only the high places were not removed. The people were still sacrificing and burning incense on the high places.

verses.rationale: Retain three revenue categories while noting uncertainty in the first expression.
verses.before: Joash said to the priests, “All the silver of the holy things that is brought into the house of the LORD—the silver of people who pass over, the silver of each person’s valuation, and all silver that comes upon a person’s heart to bring into the house of the LORD—
verses.after: Joash said to the priests, “All the money brought into the LORD’s house as sacred gifts—the money collected from those counted, the money from personal assessments, and all the money anyone’s heart prompts them to bring to the LORD’s house—
verses.tsw_comparator: Joash said to the priests, “All the silver of the holy things that is brought into the house of the LORD—the silver of those who pass over, the silver of each person’s valuation, and all silver that comes upon a person’s heart to bring into the house of the LORD—

verses.rationale: Keep the personal collection arrangement and comprehensive repairs.
verses.before: let the priests take it, each from his acquaintance, and let them repair the damage of the house wherever damage is found.”
verses.after: the priests are to receive, each from his acquaintances. They must repair the house wherever damage is found.”
verses.tsw_comparator: let the priests take it, each from his acquaintance, and let them repair the damage of the house wherever damage is found.”

verses.rationale: Retain the long delay without alleging unspoken theft.
verses.before: But in the twenty-third year of King Joash, the priests had not repaired the damage of the house.
verses.after: But by King Joash’s twenty-third year, the priests had still not repaired the damage to the house.
verses.tsw_comparator: But in the twenty-third year of King Joash, the priests had not repaired the damage of the house.

verses.rationale: Keep the rebuke and change in financial arrangements.
verses.before: So King Joash called Jehoiada the priest and the other priests and said to them, “Why are you not repairing the damage of the house? And now, do not take silver from your acquaintances for yourselves, but give it for the damage of the house.”
verses.after: So King Joash called Jehoiada the priest and the other priests and asked, “Why aren’t you repairing the damage to the house? From now on, stop taking money from your acquaintances. Hand it over for the repairs.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So King Joash called Jehoiada the priest and the other priests and said to them, “Why are you not repairing the damage of the house? And now, do not take silver from your acquaintances for yourselves, but give it for the damage of the house.”

verses.rationale: Preserve both parts of the agreement.
verses.before: The priests agreed that they would no longer take silver from the people and that they would not themselves repair the damage of the house.
verses.after: The priests agreed not to take any more money from the people and not to be responsible for repairing the house.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priests agreed that they would no longer take silver from the people and that they would not themselves repair the damage of the house.

verses.rationale: Retain the chest’s construction, position, and collecting officials.
verses.before: Jehoiada the priest took a chest, bored a hole in its lid, and placed it beside the altar, on the right side as one enters the house of the LORD. The priests who guarded the threshold put there all the silver that was brought into the house of the LORD.
verses.after: Jehoiada the priest took a chest, bored a hole in its lid, and placed it beside the altar, on the right as one entered the LORD’s house. The priests guarding the threshold put into it all the money brought to the LORD’s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jehoiada the priest took a chest, bored a hole in its lid, and placed it beside the altar, on the right side as one enters the house of the LORD. The priests who guarded the threshold put there all the silver that was brought into the house of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keep the joint oversight and the source’s sequence of actions.
verses.before: And it happened whenever they saw that there was much silver in the chest, the king’s scribe and the high priest would come up, bind and count the silver that was found in the house of the LORD.
verses.after: Whenever they saw that there was a great deal of money in the chest, the king’s secretary and the high priest came up, bagged it, and counted the money found in the LORD’s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened whenever they saw that there was much silver in the chest, the king’s scribe and the high priest would come up, bind and count the silver that was found in the house of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retain weighed money rather than modern coinage or accounting totals.
verses.before: They would give the weighed silver into the hands of those doing the work, those appointed over the house of the LORD. They paid it out to the carpenters and builders who worked on the house of the LORD,
verses.after: They gave the weighed money to those supervising the work on the LORD’s house. These paid it out to the carpenters and builders working on the house,
verses.tsw_comparator: They would give the weighed silver into the hands of those doing the work, those appointed over the house of the LORD. They paid it out to the carpenters and builders who worked on the house of the LORD,

verses.rationale: Preserve trades, materials, and other repair costs.
verses.before: to masons and stonecutters, and to buy timber and quarried stone to repair the damage of the house of the LORD and for everything that went out for repairing the house.
verses.after: to the masons and stonecutters, and for timber and dressed stone to repair the LORD’s house, as well as every other expense of the repairs.
verses.tsw_comparator: to masons and stonecutters, and to buy timber and quarried stone to repair the damage of the house of the LORD and for everything that went out for repairing the house.

verses.rationale: Keep the full excluded utensil list.
verses.before: But there were not made for the house of the LORD silver basins, snuffers, bowls, trumpets, or any vessel of gold or vessel of silver from the money brought into the house of the LORD,
verses.after: But none of the money brought into the LORD’s house was used to make silver basins, snuffers, bowls, trumpets, or any gold or silver utensils for the house.
verses.tsw_comparator: But there were not made for the house of the LORD silver basins, snuffers, bowls, trumpets, or any vessel of gold or vessel of silver from the money brought into the house of the LORD,

verses.rationale: Retain the repeated priority of repairs.
verses.before: for they gave it to those doing the work, and with it they repaired the house of the LORD.
verses.after: Instead, they gave it to the workers and used it to repair the LORD’s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: for they gave it to those doing the work, and with it they repaired the house of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keep the stated reason without making it a general financial rule.
verses.before: They did not require an accounting from the men into whose hand they gave the silver to give to those doing the work, for they were acting faithfully.
verses.after: No accounting was required from the men entrusted with paying the workers, because they acted faithfully.
verses.tsw_comparator: They did not require an accounting from the men into whose hand they gave the silver to give to those doing the work, for they were acting faithfully.

verses.rationale: Distinguish the two offering revenues from the repair funds.
verses.before: The silver of guilt offerings and the silver of sin offerings was not brought into the house of the LORD; it belonged to the priests.
verses.after: Money from guilt offerings and sin offerings was not brought into the LORD’s house; it belonged to the priests.
verses.tsw_comparator: The silver of guilt offerings and the silver of sin offerings was not brought into the house of the LORD; it belonged to the priests.

verses.rationale: Keep Gath’s capture before the threat to Jerusalem.
verses.before: Then Hazael king of Aram went up and fought against Gath and captured it. Hazael set his face to go up against Jerusalem.
verses.after: Then Hazael king of Aram came up, fought against Gath, and captured it. He turned his attention toward attacking Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Hazael king of Aram went up and fought against Gath and captured it. Hazael set his face to go up against Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Preserve all named predecessors and both treasuries.
verses.before: Joash king of Judah took all the holy things that Jehoshaphat, Jehoram, and Ahaziah his ancestors, kings of Judah, had consecrated, and his own holy things, and all the gold found in the treasuries of the house of the LORD and the king’s house, and sent them to Hazael king of Aram. Then he went away from Jerusalem.
verses.after: Joash king of Judah took all the sacred gifts dedicated by his ancestors Jehoshaphat, Jehoram, and Ahaziah, kings of Judah, along with his own sacred gifts and all the gold found in the treasuries of the LORD’s house and the palace. He sent them to Hazael king of Aram, who withdrew from Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joash king of Judah took all the holy things that Jehoshaphat, Jehoram, and Ahaziah his ancestors, kings of Judah, had consecrated, and his own holy things, and all the gold found in the treasuries of the house of the LORD and the king’s house, and sent them to Hazael king of Aram. Then he went away from Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Retain the royal source notice.
verses.before: Now the rest of the acts of Joash and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.after: The rest of Joash’s acts and everything he did are written in the annals of the kings of Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the rest of the acts of Joash and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?

verses.rationale: Keep the place names and avoid substituting Chronicles’ account.
verses.before: His servants arose and made a conspiracy and struck Joash at the house of Millo, on the way that goes down to Silla.
verses.after: His servants rose up, formed a conspiracy, and struck Joash down at Beth-millo, on the way down to Silla.
verses.tsw_comparator: His servants arose and made a conspiracy and struck Joash at the house of Millo, on the way that goes down to Silla.

verses.rationale: Follow the pinned name Jozabad rather than silently importing Jozacar.
verses.before: Jozacar son of Shimeath and Jehozabad son of Shomer, his servants, struck him, and he died. They buried him with his ancestors in the city of David. Amaziah his son became king in his place.
verses.after: His servants Jozabad son of Shimeath and Jehozabad son of Shomer struck him, and he died. They buried him with his ancestors in the City of David. His son Amaziah became king in his place.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jozacar son of Shimeath and Jehozabad son of Shomer, his servants, struck him, and he died. They buried him with his ancestors in the city of David. Amaziah his son became king in his place.

verses.rationale: Keep both kingdoms’ rulers distinct and retain both year counts.
verses.before: In the twenty-third year of Joash son of Ahaziah king of Judah, Jehoahaz son of Jehu became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned seventeen years.
verses.after: In the twenty-third year of Joash son of Ahaziah, king of Judah, Jehoahaz son of Jehu became king over Israel in Samaria. He reigned for seventeen years.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the twenty-third year of Joash son of Ahaziah king of Judah, Jehoahaz son of Jehu became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned seventeen years.

verses.rationale: Preserve the repeated pattern of inherited royal sin.
verses.before: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD and went after the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, by which he caused Israel to sin. He did not turn away from them.
verses.after: He did what was evil in the LORD’s eyes and followed the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, which he had caused Israel to commit. He did not turn away from them.
verses.tsw_comparator: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD and went after the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, by which he caused Israel to sin. He did not turn away from them.

verses.rationale: Retain divine agency and successive Aramean rulers.
verses.before: So the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and he gave them continually into the hand of Hazael king of Aram and into the hand of Ben-Hadad son of Hazael.
verses.after: The LORD’s anger burned against Israel, and he kept giving them into the hands of Hazael king of Aram and Ben-hadad son of Hazael.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and he gave them continually into the hand of Hazael king of Aram and into the hand of Ben-Hadad son of Hazael.

verses.rationale: Keep seeing oppression as the stated reason for listening.
verses.before: Yet Jehoahaz sought the favor of the LORD, and the LORD listened to him, for he saw the oppression of Israel, how the king of Aram oppressed them.
verses.after: Then Jehoahaz sought the LORD’s favor, and the LORD listened to him, for he saw how the king of Aram was oppressing Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Jehoahaz sought the favor of the LORD, and the LORD listened to him, for he saw the oppression of Israel, how the king of Aram oppressed them.

verses.rationale: Leave the deliverer unnamed and preserve tents rather than modernizing the image away.
verses.before: The LORD gave Israel a savior, and they went out from under the hand of Aram. Then the children of Israel lived in their tents as formerly.
verses.after: The LORD gave Israel a deliverer, and they escaped Aram’s power. The Israelites lived in their tents as they had before.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD gave Israel a savior, and they went out from under the hand of Aram. Then the children of Israel lived in their tents as formerly.

verses.rationale: Retain ongoing sin beside rescue and the singular cult object.
verses.before: Even so they did not turn away from the sins of the house of Jeroboam, by which he caused Israel to sin, but walked in them. The Asherah also remained standing in Samaria.
verses.after: Yet they did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam’s house, which he had caused Israel to commit. They continued in them, and the Asherah also remained standing in Samaria.
verses.tsw_comparator: Nevertheless they did not turn away from the sins of the house of Jeroboam, by which he caused Israel to sin, but walked in them. The Asherah also remained standing in Samaria.

verses.rationale: Preserve all force totals and the threshing image.
verses.before: For he left to Jehoahaz no army except fifty horsemen, ten chariots, and ten thousand foot soldiers, for the king of Aram had destroyed them and made them like dust at threshing.
verses.after: Jehoahaz was left with only fifty horsemen, ten chariots, and ten thousand foot soldiers. The king of Aram had destroyed the rest, making them like dust at threshing.
verses.tsw_comparator: For he left to Jehoahaz no army except fifty horsemen, ten chariots, and ten thousand foot soldiers, for the king of Aram had destroyed them and made them like dust at threshing.

verses.rationale: Keep all categories in the source notice.
verses.before: Now the rest of the acts of Jehoahaz and all that he did and his might, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.after: The rest of Jehoahaz’s acts, everything he did, and his might are written in the annals of the kings of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the rest of the acts of Jehoahaz and all that he did and his might, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

verses.rationale: Retain burial and succession.
verses.before: Jehoahaz lay down with his ancestors, and they buried him in Samaria. Joash his son became king in his place.
verses.after: Jehoahaz rested with his ancestors, and they buried him in Samaria. His son Joash became king in his place.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jehoahaz lay down with his ancestors, and they buried him in Samaria. Joash his son became king in his place.

verses.rationale: Keep the source’s longer name form and both chronological figures.
verses.before: In the thirty-seventh year of Joash king of Judah, Jehoash son of Jehoahaz became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned sixteen years.
verses.after: In the thirty-seventh year of Joash king of Judah, Jehoash son of Jehoahaz became king over Israel in Samaria. He reigned for sixteen years.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the thirty-seventh year of Joash king of Judah, Jehoash son of Jehoahaz became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned sixteen years.

verses.rationale: Retain the comprehensive negative judgment.
verses.before: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD. He did not turn away from all the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, by which he caused Israel to sin; he walked in them.
verses.after: He did what was evil in the LORD’s eyes. He did not turn away from any of the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, which he had caused Israel to commit, but continued in them.
verses.tsw_comparator: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD. He did not turn away from all the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, by which he caused Israel to sin; he walked in them.

verses.rationale: Keep the specific opponent in the source notice.
verses.before: Now the rest of the acts of Joash and all that he did and his might, how he fought Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.after: The rest of Joash’s acts, everything he did, and his might in fighting Amaziah king of Judah are written in the annals of the kings of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the rest of the acts of Joash and all that he did and his might, how he fought Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

verses.rationale: Retain succession before burial as narrated.
verses.before: Joash lay down with his ancestors, and Jeroboam sat upon his throne. Joash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.
verses.after: Joash rested with his ancestors, and Jeroboam sat on his throne. Joash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joash lay down with his ancestors, and Jeroboam sat upon his throne. Joash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.

verses.rationale: Repeat the chariot cry linking Elisha’s death to Elijah’s departure.
verses.before: Now Elisha became sick with the sickness from which he would die. Joash king of Israel went down to him, wept over his face, and said, “My father, my father! The chariots of Israel and its horsemen!”
verses.after: When Elisha was suffering from the illness that would kill him, Joash king of Israel came down to him and wept over him. “My father, my father!” he said. “Israel’s chariot and its horsemen!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Now Elisha became sick with the sickness from which he would die. Joash king of Israel went down to him, wept over his face, and said, “My father, my father! The chariots of Israel and its horsemen!”

verses.rationale: Preserve instruction and response.
verses.before: Elisha said to him, “Take a bow and arrows.” So he took a bow and arrows.
verses.after: Elisha said to him, “Take a bow and arrows.” So he took a bow and arrows.
verses.tsw_comparator: Elisha said to him, “Take a bow and arrows.” So he took a bow and arrows.

verses.rationale: Keep the hands-on-hands action without explaining its mechanism.
verses.before: Then he said to the king of Israel, “Put your hand on the bow.” He put his hand on it, and Elisha put his hands upon the king’s hands.
verses.after: He told the king of Israel, “Put your hand on the bow.” When he did, Elisha laid his hands on the king’s hands.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he said to the king of Israel, “Put your hand on the bow.” He put his hand on it, and Elisha put his hands upon the king’s hands.

verses.rationale: Retain direction, place, and doubled victory interpretation.
verses.before: He said, “Open the window eastward.” He opened it. Then Elisha said, “Shoot!” And he shot. He said, “The LORD’s arrow of victory, the arrow of victory over Aram! You will strike Aram at Aphek until you have brought it to an end.”
verses.after: “Open the window toward the east,” he said, and the king opened it. Elisha said, “Shoot!” He shot. Then Elisha said, “The LORD’s arrow of victory, an arrow of victory over Aram! You will strike Aram at Aphek until you have finished them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “Open the window eastward.” He opened it. Then Elisha said, “Shoot!” And he shot. He said, “The LORD’s arrow of victory, the arrow of victory over Aram! You shall strike Aram at Aphek until you have brought it to an end.”

verses.rationale: Preserve the three strikes without deciding whether arrows were shot or struck by hand.
verses.before: Then he said, “Take the arrows.” He took them. He said to the king of Israel, “Strike the ground.” He struck three times and stopped.
verses.after: Then he said, “Take the arrows.” He took them. Elisha told the king of Israel, “Strike the ground.” He struck three times and stopped.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he said, “Take the arrows.” He took them. He said to the king of Israel, “Strike the ground.” He struck three times and stopped.

verses.rationale: Keep the unannounced numerical expectation and limited outcome.
verses.before: The man of God became angry with him and said, “You should have struck five or six times; then you would have struck Aram until you brought it to an end. But now you will strike Aram only three times.”
verses.after: The man of God was angry with him. “You should have struck five or six times!” he said. “Then you would have struck Aram until you had finished them. Now you will strike Aram only three times.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The man of God became angry with him and said, “You should have struck five or six times; then you would have struck Aram until you brought it to an end. But now you will strike Aram only three times.”

verses.rationale: Retain the seasonal expression without supplying an exact month.
verses.before: Elisha died, and they buried him. Now raiding bands of Moab would enter the land at the coming of the year.
verses.after: Elisha died, and they buried him. Moabite raiding bands used to enter the land at the turn of the year.
verses.tsw_comparator: Elisha died, and they buried him. Now raiding bands of Moab would enter the land at the coming of the year.

verses.rationale: Preserve the accidental contact and bodily restoration without doctrinal additions.
verses.before: And it happened as they were burying a man that look, they saw a raiding band. They threw the man into Elisha’s grave. When the man touched the bones of Elisha, he revived and stood on his feet.
verses.after: Once, while people were burying a man, they saw a raiding band. They threw the man into Elisha’s tomb. When his body touched Elisha’s bones, he came to life and stood on his feet.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened as they were burying a man that behold, they saw a raiding band. They threw the man into Elisha’s grave. When the man touched the bones of Elisha, he revived and stood on his feet.

verses.rationale: Keep the full duration of oppression.
verses.before: Hazael king of Aram oppressed Israel all the days of Jehoahaz.
verses.after: Hazael king of Aram oppressed Israel throughout Jehoahaz’s reign.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hazael king of Aram oppressed Israel all the days of Jehoahaz.

verses.rationale: Preserve the three patriarchs and the temporal qualification until then.
verses.before: But the LORD was gracious to them and had compassion on them and turned toward them because of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. He was not willing to destroy them and did not cast them from his presence until now.
verses.after: But the LORD was gracious to them, had compassion on them, and turned toward them because of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. He was unwilling to destroy them, and until then he had not cast them out of his presence.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the LORD was gracious to them and had compassion on them and turned toward them because of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. He was not willing to destroy them and did not cast them from his presence until now.

verses.rationale: Keep the Aramean succession.
verses.before: Hazael king of Aram died, and Ben-Hadad his son became king in his place.
verses.after: Hazael king of Aram died, and his son Ben-hadad became king in his place.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hazael king of Aram died, and Ben-Hadad his son became king in his place.

verses.rationale: Keep the three victories as fulfillment of the arrow sign.
verses.before: Then Jehoash son of Jehoahaz took back from the hand of Ben-Hadad son of Hazael the cities that he had taken in war from the hand of Jehoahaz his father. Three times Joash struck him and recovered the cities of Israel.
verses.after: Jehoash son of Jehoahaz took back from Ben-hadad son of Hazael the towns Hazael had taken from his father Jehoahaz in war. Joash defeated him three times and recovered Israel’s towns.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Jehoash son of Jehoahaz took back from the hand of Ben-Hadad son of Hazael the cities that he had taken in war from the hand of Jehoahaz his father. Three times Joash struck him and recovered the cities of Israel.

verses.rationale: Keep the source’s shortened Joahaz and distinguish the two Joashes.
verses.before: In the second year of Joash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel, Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah became king.
verses.after: In the second year of Joash son of Joahaz, king of Israel, Amaziah son of Joash became king of Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the second year of Joash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel, Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah became king.

verses.rationale: Follow the read form of the mother’s name and retain both ages.
verses.before: He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Jehoaddin from Jerusalem.
verses.after: He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for twenty-nine years. His mother’s name was Jehoaddan, from Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Jehoaddin from Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Distinguish David as ancestor from the immediate father.
verses.before: He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, yet not like David his ancestor. He did according to all that Joash his father had done.
verses.after: He did what was right in the LORD’s eyes, though not like his ancestor David. He did everything as his father Joash had done.
verses.tsw_comparator: He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, yet not like David his ancestor. He did according to all that Joash his father had done.

verses.rationale: Repeat the recurring qualification consistently.
verses.before: Only the high places were not removed. The people were still sacrificing and burning incense on the high places.
verses.after: Yet the high places were not removed. The people still sacrificed and burned offerings there.
verses.tsw_comparator: Only the high places were not removed. The people were still sacrificing and burning incense on the high places.

verses.rationale: Retain the timing of the executions.
verses.before: And it happened when the kingdom was firmly in his hand that he struck his servants who had struck his father the king.
verses.after: Once the kingdom was secure in his hands, he struck down the servants who had killed his father the king.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened when the kingdom was firmly in his hand that he struck his servants who had struck his father the king.

verses.rationale: Preserve the quoted individual-liability rule and its Torah attribution.
verses.before: But the children of the murderers he did not put to death, according to what is written in the book of the instruction of Moses, where the LORD commanded, saying, “Fathers will not be put to death for sons, and sons will not be put to death for fathers, but each person will be put to death for his own sin.”
verses.after: But he did not put the killers’ sons to death, in keeping with what is written in the Book of Moses’ Instruction, where the LORD commanded: “Fathers must not be put to death for their children, nor children for their fathers. Each must be put to death for their own sin.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But the children of the murderers he did not put to death, according to what is written in the book of the instruction of Moses, where the LORD commanded, saying, “Fathers shall not be put to death for sons, and sons shall not be put to death for fathers, but each person shall be put to death for his own sin.”

verses.rationale: Keep the casualty count and renamed place.
verses.before: He struck ten thousand of Edom in the Valley of Salt and captured Sela in battle. He called its name Joktheel, as it is to this day.
verses.after: He struck down ten thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt and captured Sela in battle. He named it Joktheel, the name it bears to this day.
verses.tsw_comparator: He struck ten thousand of Edom in the Valley of Salt and captured Sela in battle. He called its name Joktheel, as it is to this day.

verses.rationale: Retain the face-to-face challenge and full lineage.
verses.before: Then Amaziah sent messengers to Jehoash son of Jehoahaz son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, “Come, let us look one another in the face.”
verses.after: Then Amaziah sent messengers to Jehoash son of Jehoahaz, son of Jehu, king of Israel: “Come, let us meet face to face.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Amaziah sent messengers to Jehoash son of Jehoahaz son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, “Come, let us look one another in the face.”

verses.rationale: Preserve the entire fable and repeated Lebanon setting.
verses.before: Jehoash king of Israel sent to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, “The thornbush that is in Lebanon sent to the cedar that is in Lebanon, saying, ‘Give your daughter to my son as wife.’ But a wild animal that was in Lebanon passed by and trampled the thornbush.
verses.after: Jehoash king of Israel sent this reply to Amaziah king of Judah: “A thistle in Lebanon sent word to a cedar in Lebanon, ‘Give your daughter to my son as his wife.’ Then a wild animal in Lebanon passed by and trampled the thistle.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jehoash king of Israel sent to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, “The thornbush that is in Lebanon sent to the cedar that is in Lebanon, saying, ‘Give your daughter to my son as wife.’ But a wild animal that was in Lebanon passed by and trampled the thornbush.

verses.rationale: Keep the heart image and threat to the wider kingdom.
verses.before: You have surely struck Edom, and your heart has lifted you up. Enjoy your glory and stay in your house. Why should you provoke disaster and fall, you and Judah with you?”
verses.after: You have indeed defeated Edom, and your heart has lifted you up. Enjoy your glory and stay home. Why stir up trouble and bring yourself down, and Judah with you?”
verses.tsw_comparator: You have surely struck Edom, and your heart has lifted you up. Enjoy your glory and stay in your house. Why should you provoke disaster and fall, you and Judah with you?”

verses.rationale: Repeat face to face as the challenge becomes battle.
verses.before: Yet Amaziah did not listen. So Jehoash king of Israel went up, and he and Amaziah king of Judah looked one another in the face at Beth-Shemesh, which belongs to Judah.
verses.after: But Amaziah would not listen. Jehoash king of Israel advanced, and he and Amaziah king of Judah met face to face at Beth-shemesh in Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Amaziah did not listen. So Jehoash king of Israel went up, and he and Amaziah king of Judah looked one another in the face at Beth-Shemesh, which belongs to Judah.

verses.rationale: Retain the tents idiom.
verses.before: Judah was struck before Israel, and each man fled to his tent.
verses.after: Judah was defeated by Israel, and everyone fled to his tents.
verses.tsw_comparator: Judah was struck before Israel, and each man fled to his tent.

verses.rationale: Retain the lineage, gates, and ancient measurement.
verses.before: Jehoash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah at Beth-Shemesh, and he came to Jerusalem and broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate, four hundred cubits.
verses.after: At Beth-shemesh, Jehoash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah, son of Jehoash, son of Ahaziah. He came to Jerusalem and broke down four hundred cubits of its wall, from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jehoash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah at Beth-Shemesh, and he came to Jerusalem and broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate, four hundred cubits.

verses.rationale: Keep hostages distinct from the plunder.
verses.before: He took all the gold and silver and all the vessels found in the house of the LORD and in the treasuries of the king’s house, as well as hostages, and returned to Samaria.
verses.after: He took all the gold and silver, all the utensils found in the LORD’s house and in the palace treasuries, and hostages. Then he returned to Samaria.
verses.tsw_comparator: He took all the gold and silver and all the vessels found in the house of the LORD and in the treasuries of the king’s house, as well as hostages, and returned to Samaria.

verses.rationale: Preserve the specific war in the source notice.
verses.before: Now the rest of the acts of Jehoash that he did and his might and how he fought Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.after: The rest of Jehoash’s acts, his might, and his war with Amaziah king of Judah are written in the annals of the kings of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the rest of the acts of Jehoash that he did and his might and how he fought Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

verses.rationale: Keep burial and succession.
verses.before: Jehoash lay down with his ancestors and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel. Jeroboam his son became king in his place.
verses.after: Jehoash rested with his ancestors and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel. His son Jeroboam became king in his place.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jehoash lay down with his ancestors and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel. Jeroboam his son became king in his place.

verses.rationale: Retain the relative chronology without calculating an unsupported date.
verses.before: Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah lived fifteen years after the death of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel.
verses.after: Amaziah son of Joash, king of Judah, lived fifteen years after the death of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah lived fifteen years after the death of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel.

verses.rationale: Keep the shorter source notice.
verses.before: Now the rest of the acts of Amaziah, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.after: The rest of Amaziah’s acts are written in the annals of the kings of Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the rest of the acts of Amaziah, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?

verses.rationale: Keep the pursuit and repeated refuge location.
verses.before: They made a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish. But they sent after him to Lachish and put him to death there.
verses.after: A conspiracy formed against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish. They sent men after him to Lachish and killed him there.
verses.tsw_comparator: They made a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish. But they sent after him to Lachish and put him to death there.

verses.rationale: Retain transport by horses and burial location.
verses.before: They carried him on horses, and he was buried in Jerusalem with his ancestors in the city of David.
verses.after: They brought him back on horses, and he was buried in Jerusalem with his ancestors in the City of David.
verses.tsw_comparator: They carried him on horses, and he was buried in Jerusalem with his ancestors in the city of David.

verses.rationale: Preserve the people’s agency and the young king’s age.
verses.before: Then all the people of Judah took Azariah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.
verses.after: All the people of Judah took Azariah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then all the people of Judah took Azariah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.

verses.rationale: Retain the temporal notice without inserting a regnal calculation.
verses.before: He built Elath and restored it to Judah after the king lay down with his ancestors.
verses.after: He rebuilt Elath and restored it to Judah after the king had rested with his ancestors.
verses.tsw_comparator: He built Elath and restored it to Judah after the king lay down with his ancestors.

verses.rationale: Keep the accession year and lengthy reign.
verses.before: In the fifteenth year of Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah, Jeroboam son of Joash king of Israel became king in Samaria, and he reigned forty-one years.
verses.after: In the fifteenth year of Amaziah son of Joash, king of Judah, Jeroboam son of Joash became king of Israel in Samaria. He reigned for forty-one years.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the fifteenth year of Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah, Jeroboam son of Joash king of Israel became king in Samaria, and he reigned forty-one years.

verses.rationale: Distinguish this Jeroboam from his earlier namesake by patronymic.
verses.before: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD. He did not turn away from all the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, by which he caused Israel to sin.
verses.after: He did what was evil in the LORD’s eyes. He did not turn away from any of the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, which he had caused Israel to commit.
verses.tsw_comparator: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD. He did not turn away from all the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, by which he caused Israel to sin.

verses.rationale: Preserve the borders and Jonah’s full identification.
verses.before: He restored the border of Israel from Lebo-Hamath as far as the Sea of the Arabah, according to the word of the LORD, the God of Israel, that he spoke by the hand of his servant Jonah son of Amittai, the prophet who was from Gath-Hepher.
verses.after: He restored Israel’s border from Lebo-hamath to the Sea of the Arabah, according to the word of the LORD, the God of Israel, spoken through his servant Jonah son of Amittai, the prophet from Gath-hepher.
verses.tsw_comparator: He restored the border of Israel from Lebo-Hamath as far as the Sea of the Arabah, according to the word of the LORD, the God of Israel, that he spoke by the hand of his servant Jonah son of Amittai, the prophet who was from Gath-Hepher.

verses.rationale: Keep the paired social expression and absence of help.
verses.before: For the LORD saw the very bitter affliction of Israel, that there was neither slave nor free, and there was no helper for Israel.
verses.after: For the LORD saw that Israel’s suffering was very bitter. There was no one left, bound or free, and no one to help Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the LORD saw the very bitter affliction of Israel, that there was neither slave nor free, and there was no helper for Israel.

verses.rationale: Preserve rescue through a negatively evaluated king.
verses.before: The LORD had not spoken to wipe out the name of Israel from under the heavens, so he saved them by the hand of Jeroboam son of Joash.
verses.after: The LORD had not said that he would blot out Israel’s name from under heaven. So he saved them through Jeroboam son of Joash.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD had not spoken to wipe out the name of Israel from under the heavens, so he saved them by the hand of Jeroboam son of Joash.

verses.rationale: Keep the difficult Judah/Israel clause and its uncertainty noted; place the relative clause next to Damascus and Hamath to avoid assigning it to Israel.
verses.before: Now the rest of the acts of Jeroboam and all that he did and his might, how he fought and how he restored Damascus and Hamath to Judah in Israel, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.after: The rest of Jeroboam’s acts, everything he did, his military might, and how he recovered for Israel Damascus and Hamath, which had belonged to Judah, are written in the annals of the kings of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the rest of the acts of Jeroboam and all that he did and his might, how he fought and how he restored Damascus and Hamath to Judah in Israel, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

verses.rationale: Keep the dynastic succession without adding a burial location.
verses.before: Jeroboam lay down with his ancestors, with the kings of Israel. Zechariah his son became king in his place.
verses.after: Jeroboam rested with his ancestors, with the kings of Israel. His son Zechariah became king in his place.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jeroboam lay down with his ancestors, with the kings of Israel. Zechariah his son became king in his place.

verses.rationale: Retain the source’s synchronism.
verses.before: In the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Azariah son of Amaziah king of Judah became king.
verses.after: In the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Azariah son of Amaziah became king of Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Azariah son of Amaziah king of Judah became king.

verses.rationale: Keep age, duration, and maternal identity.
verses.before: He was sixteen years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Jecoliah from Jerusalem.
verses.after: He was sixteen years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for fifty-two years. His mother’s name was Jecoliah, from Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: He was sixteen years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Jecoliah from Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Retain the limited ancestral comparison.
verses.before: He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, according to all that Amaziah his father had done.
verses.after: He did what was right in the LORD’s eyes, just as his father Amaziah had done.
verses.tsw_comparator: He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, according to all that Amaziah his father had done.

verses.rationale: Maintain the recurring high-place refrain.
verses.before: Only the high places were not removed. The people were still sacrificing and burning incense on the high places.
verses.after: Yet the high places were not removed. The people still sacrificed and burned offerings there.
verses.tsw_comparator: Only the high places were not removed. The people were still sacrificing and burning incense on the high places.

verses.rationale: Preserve divine agency without importing Chronicles’ explanation.
verses.before: The LORD struck the king, and he had a skin disease until the day of his death. He lived in a separate house, while Jotham the king’s son was over the household, judging the people of the land.
verses.after: The LORD struck the king with a skin disease that lasted until his death. He lived in a separate house, while Jotham the king’s son managed the palace and governed the people of the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD struck the king, and he had a skin disease until the day of his death. He lived in a separate house, while Jotham the king’s son was over the household, judging the people of the land.

verses.rationale: Keep the source notice.
verses.before: Now the rest of the acts of Azariah and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.after: The rest of Azariah’s acts and everything he did are written in the annals of the kings of Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the rest of the acts of Azariah and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?

verses.rationale: Retain the burial account as Kings gives it.
verses.before: Azariah lay down with his ancestors, and they buried him with his ancestors in the city of David. Jotham his son became king in his place.
verses.after: Azariah rested with his ancestors, and they buried him with them in the City of David. His son Jotham became king in his place.
verses.tsw_comparator: Azariah lay down with his ancestors, and they buried him with his ancestors in the city of David. Jotham his son became king in his place.

verses.rationale: Keep the short reign and accession year.
verses.before: In the thirty-eighth year of Azariah king of Judah, Zechariah son of Jeroboam became king over Israel in Samaria for six months.
verses.after: In the thirty-eighth year of Azariah king of Judah, Zechariah son of Jeroboam became king over Israel in Samaria. He reigned for six months.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the thirty-eighth year of Azariah king of Judah, Zechariah son of Jeroboam became king over Israel in Samaria for six months.

verses.rationale: Preserve the recurring judgment.
verses.before: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, as his ancestors had done. He did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, by which he caused Israel to sin.
verses.after: He did what was evil in the LORD’s eyes, as his ancestors had done. He did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, which he had caused Israel to commit.
verses.tsw_comparator: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, as his ancestors had done. He did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, by which he caused Israel to sin.

verses.rationale: Render the difficult public-location phrase without inventing a place name.
verses.before: Shallum son of Jabesh conspired against him, struck him before the people, and put him to death. He became king in his place.
verses.after: Shallum son of Jabesh conspired against him, struck him down in front of the people, killed him, and became king in his place.
verses.tsw_comparator: Shallum son of Jabesh conspired against him, struck him before the people, and put him to death. He became king in his place.

verses.rationale: Keep the concise record notice.
verses.before: Now the rest of the acts of Zechariah, look, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
verses.after: The rest of Zechariah’s acts are written in the annals of the kings of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the rest of the acts of Zechariah, look, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.

verses.rationale: Retain the narrator’s causal explanation and exodus foundation.

verses.rationale: Keep both foreign and royal sources of the practices.

verses.tsw_comparator: They walked in the statutes of the nations whom the LORD had dispossessed before the children of Israel and in the statutes that the kings of Israel had made.

verses.rationale: Preserve the secrecy reading and the settlement-range image.

verses.tsw_comparator: The children of Israel secretly did things against the LORD their God that were not right. They built for themselves high places in all their cities, from watchtower to fortified city.

verses.rationale: Keep the recurring cult objects and locations.

verses.after: They set up sacred pillars and Asherah poles on every high hill and under every leafy tree.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set up for themselves pillars and Asherah poles on every high hill and under every flourishing tree.

verses.rationale: Preserve the comparison and provocation.

verses.rationale: Keep both kingdoms, prophetic titles, and the repeated transmission of instruction.

verses.rationale: Preserve the bodily image and link to trust.
verses.before: But they would not listen. They stiffened their neck like the neck of their ancestors, who did not trust in the LORD their God.
verses.after: But they would not listen. They stiffened their necks like their ancestors, who had not trusted the LORD their God.
verses.tsw_comparator: But they would not listen. They stiffened their neck like the neck of their ancestors, who did not trust in the LORD their God.

verses.rationale: Retain the emptiness wordplay and all rejected obligations.

verses.after: They rejected his decrees, the covenant he had made with their ancestors, and the warnings he had given them. They followed what was empty and became empty themselves. They followed the surrounding nations, though the LORD had commanded them not to act as those nations did.
verses.tsw_comparator: They rejected his statutes and his covenant that he made with their ancestors and his testimonies with which he testified against them. verses.rationale: Keep the count, material, and heavenly-army image.

verses.rationale: Preserve both genders and the self-sale image.

verses.after: They made their sons and daughters pass through the fire, practiced divination and read omens, and sold themselves to do what was evil in the LORD’s eyes, provoking him to anger.

verses.rationale: Retain divine agency and actual deaths.

verses.tsw_comparator: They spoke to the king of Assyria, saying, “The nations whom you carried into exile and settled in the cities of Samaria do not know the custom of the god of the land. verses.rationale: Preserve the source’s plural departure with singular teaching priest.

verses.after: The king of Assyria commanded, “Send back one of the priests you deported from there. Let them go and settle there, and let him teach them the requirements of the god of the land.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the king of Assyria commanded, saying, “Send there one of the priests whom you carried into exile from there. Let him go and live there and teach them the custom of the god of the land.”

verses.after: So one of the priests deported from Samaria came and settled in Bethel. He taught them how to fear the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retain the repeated nation-by-nation arrangement.

verses.rationale: Preserve both predicates despite the next verse’s contrasting assessment.

verses.rationale: Retain the shift in evaluation rather than smoothing away the tension.

verses.rationale: Preserve the four prohibited acts.

verses.after: The LORD made a covenant with them and commanded them, “You must not fear other gods, bow to them, serve them, or sacrifice to them.

verses.rationale: Keep the exodus and bodily image.

verses.rationale: Retain the full instruction list and repeated prohibition.

verses.rationale: Preserve the closing mixed-worship description and generational continuity.

verses.rationale: Keep the three Judean officials and roles.

verses.after: They called for the king. Eliakim son of Hilkiah, the palace administrator, Shebnah the secretary, and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder, came out to them.
verses.tsw_comparator: They called to the king. Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, Shebnah the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph the recorder went out to them.

verses.rationale: Preserve the imperial title and recurring confidence theme.

verses.after: The Rab-shakeh said to them, “Tell Hezekiah: ‘This is what the great king, the king of Assyria, says: What is this confidence you have?
verses.tsw_comparator: The Rabshakeh said to them, “Please say to Hezekiah: Thus says the great king, the king of Assyria: What is this confidence in which you trust?

verses.rationale: Keep the challenge as the Assyrian king’s speech.
verses.before: You say—but it is only a word of lips—‘There is counsel and strength for war.’ And now, upon whom do you trust that you have rebelled against me?
verses.after: You say you have strategy and strength for war—but that is only talk. On whom are you relying, that you have rebelled against me?

verses.rationale: Preserve the full injury image.
verses.before: Now look, you trust upon the staff of this broken reed, upon Egypt, which, if a man leans upon it, goes into his palm and pierces it. So is Pharaoh king of Egypt to everyone who trust upon him.
verses.after: Look! You are relying on Egypt, that splintered reed of a staff. If anyone leans on it, it pierces his hand. That is what Pharaoh king of Egypt is like for everyone who relies on him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now look, you trust upon the staff of this broken reed, upon Egypt, which, if a man leans upon it, goes into his palm and pierces it. So is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who trust upon him.

verses.rationale: Keep the envoy’s interpretation of the reform distinct from the narrator’s.

verses.after: But if you tell me, “We rely on the LORD our God,” isn’t he the one whose high places and altars Hezekiah removed, telling Judah and Jerusalem, “You must bow before this altar in Jerusalem”?
verses.tsw_comparator: But if you say to me, ‘We trust in the LORD our God,’ is he not the one whose high places and altars Hezekiah removed and said to Judah and Jerusalem, ‘Before this altar in Jerusalem you shall bow down’?

verses.rationale: Retain the numerical taunt and condition.

verses.after: Now make a wager with my master, the king of Assyria. I will give you two thousand horses—if you can find riders for them!

verses.rationale: Keep the comparison of military weakness.

verses.after: How could you turn back even one governor, one of my master’s least servants, when you rely on Egypt for chariots and horsemen?
verses.tsw_comparator: How then can you turn back the face of one governor among the least of my lord’s servants while you trust in Egypt for chariots and horsemen?

verses.rationale: Preserve the claimed divine commission as speech without confirming it.

verses.after: And have I come to destroy this place without the LORD? The LORD told me, “Go up against this land and destroy it.”’”
verses.tsw_comparator: And now, have I come up without the LORD against this place to destroy it? The LORD said to me, ‘Go up against this land and destroy it.’”

verses.rationale: Retain the two language names and reason for the request.

verses.after: Eliakim son of Hilkiah, Shebnah, and Joah said to the Rab-shakeh, “Please speak to your servants in Aramaic; we understand it. Don’t speak to us in Judean within hearing of the people on the wall.”

verses.rationale: Keep the bodily siege threat without euphemizing its substance.

verses.after: But the Rab-shakeh answered, “Did my master send me to say these things only to your master and you? Didn’t he send me to the men sitting on the wall, who will have to eat their own excrement and drink their own urine along with you?”
verses.tsw_comparator: But the Rabshakeh said to them, “Has my lord sent me to speak these words to your lord and to you? Is it not to the men sitting upon the wall, who will eat their own dung and drink their own urine with you?”

verses.rationale: Retain the deliberate public-language choice.

verses.after: Then the Rab-shakeh stood and shouted in Judean, “Hear the word of the great king, the king of Assyria!
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the Rabshakeh stood and called with a loud voice in Judean and spoke and said, “Hear the word of the great king, the king of Assyria!

verses.rationale: Clarify the third-person royal referent without changing the threat.

verses.rationale: Preserve the repeated trust-and-rescue challenge.

verses.after: Don’t let Hezekiah make you rely on the LORD by saying, ‘The LORD will certainly rescue us. This city will not be handed over to the king of Assyria.’

verses.rationale: Keep the concrete promise of familiar prosperity.

verses.after: Don’t listen to Hezekiah. This is what the king of Assyria says: Make peace with me and come out to me. Then each of you can eat from your own vine and fig tree and drink water from your own cistern,

verses.rationale: Retain deportation beneath the appealing land description and all produce categories.
verses.before: until I come and take you to a land like your own land, a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards, a land of olive trees and honey, so that you may live and not die. Do not listen to Hezekiah when he misleads you, saying, ‘The LORD will rescue us.’
verses.after: until I come and take you to a land like your own—a land of grain and new wine, bread and vineyards, olive oil and honey. Live, and do not die! Don’t listen to Hezekiah when he misleads you by saying, ‘The LORD will rescue us.’
verses.tsw_comparator: until I come and take you to a land like your own land, a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards, a land of olive trees and honey, so that you may live and not die. Do not listen to Hezekiah when he misleads you, saying, ‘The LORD will rescue us.’

verses.rationale: Keep the rhetorical comparison.

verses.after: Have any of the nations’ gods rescued their lands from the king of Assyria’s hand?
verses.tsw_comparator: Have any of the gods of the nations ever rescued his land from the hand of the king of Assyria?

verses.rationale: Retain every place without replacing the difficult last comparison.

verses.after: Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah? Have they rescued Samaria from my hand?
verses.tsw_comparator: Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah? Have they rescued Samaria from my hand?

verses.rationale: Repeat hand and rescue to preserve the speech’s climax.
verses.before: Who among all the gods of the lands have rescued their land from my hand, that the LORD should rescue Jerusalem from my hand?”
verses.after: Which of all the gods of these lands has rescued its land from my hand? How, then, could the LORD rescue Jerusalem from my hand?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Who among all the gods of the lands have rescued their land from my hand, that the LORD should rescue Jerusalem from my hand?”

verses.rationale: Keep silence as obedience to the king’s order.

verses.after: The people were silent and did not answer him a word, for the king had commanded, “Do not answer him.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But the people were silent and did not answer him a word, for the king’s command was, “You shall not answer him.”

verses.rationale: Retain the grief gesture and full reporting delegation.
verses.before: Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph the recorder came to Hezekiah with their clothes torn and told him the words of the Rabshakeh.
verses.after: Eliakim son of Hilkiah, the palace administrator, Shebna the secretary, and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder, came to Hezekiah with their clothes torn and reported the Rab-shakeh’s words.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph the recorder came to Hezekiah with their clothes torn and told him the words of the Rabshakeh.

verses.rationale: Keep the three grief-and-petition actions.
verses.before: And it happened when King Hezekiah heard it that he tore his clothes, covered himself with sackcloth, and went into the house of the LORD.
verses.after: When King Hezekiah heard this, he tore his clothes, covered himself with sackcloth, and went into the LORD’s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened when King Hezekiah heard it that he tore his clothes, covered himself with sackcloth, and went into the house of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserve the delegation and full prophetic identity.
verses.before: He sent Eliakim, who was over the household, Shebna the scribe, and the elders of the priests, covered with sackcloth, to Isaiah the prophet son of Amoz.
verses.after: He sent Eliakim the palace administrator, Shebna the secretary, and the senior priests, all covered with sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.
verses.tsw_comparator: He sent Eliakim, who was over the household, Shebna the scribe, and the elders of the priests, covered with sackcloth, to Isaiah the prophet son of Amoz.

verses.rationale: Retain the dangerous childbirth image without replacing it with a general crisis.

verses.after: They said to him, “This is what Hezekiah says: Today is a day of distress, rebuke, and disgrace. Children have reached the opening of the womb, but there is no strength to give birth.
verses.tsw_comparator: They said to him, “Thus says Hezekiah: This day is a day of distress, rebuke, and contempt, for children have come to the opening of the womb, but there is no strength to give birth.

verses.rationale: Keep perhaps, living God, and the request for the remnant.
verses.before: Perhaps the LORD your God will hear all the words of the Rabshakeh, whom his lord the king of Assyria sent to taunt the living God, and will rebuke the words that the LORD your God has heard. Therefore lift up a prayer for the remnant that is found.”
verses.after: Perhaps the LORD your God will hear all the words of the Rab-shakeh, whom his master the king of Assyria sent to mock the living God, and will rebuke him for the words the LORD your God has heard. Lift up a prayer for the remnant still here.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Perhaps the LORD your God will hear all the words of the Rabshakeh, whom his lord the king of Assyria sent to taunt the living God, and will rebuke the words that the LORD your God has heard. Therefore lift up a prayer for the remnant that is found.”

verses.rationale: Keep the narrative resumption.
verses.before: So the servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah.
verses.after: When King Hezekiah’s servants came to Isaiah,
verses.tsw_comparator: So the servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah.

verses.rationale: Retain the direct divine response to the insult.

verses.after: Isaiah said to them, “Tell your master: This is what the LORD says: Do not be afraid of the words you have heard, with which the king of Assyria’s servants have insulted me.

verses.rationale: Keep spirit without specifying psychology or an angelic being.

verses.after: I am going to put a spirit in him, so that he will hear a report and return to his own land. There I will make him fall by the sword.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, I am putting a spirit in him, and he will hear a report and return to his land. I will cause him to fall by the sword in his own land.”

verses.rationale: Preserve the change of siege location.

verses.after: The Rab-shakeh returned and found the king of Assyria fighting against Libnah, for he had heard that the king had left Lachish.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Rabshakeh returned and found the king of Assyria fighting against Libnah, for he had heard that he had departed from Lachish.

verses.rationale: Retain the report and renewed message without harmonizing royal chronology.

verses.rationale: Keep the accusation against God within the king’s speech.

verses.after: “Tell Hezekiah king of Judah: Do not let the God you trust deceive you by saying, ‘Jerusalem will not be handed over to the king of Assyria.’

verses.rationale: Retain the destruction term and pointed question.

verses.after: You have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the lands, devoting them to destruction. Will you be rescued?
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, you have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the lands, devoting them to destruction. And will you be rescued?

verses.rationale: Keep every named example.

verses.after: Did the gods of the nations my ancestors destroyed rescue them—Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the people of Eden in Telassar?

verses.rationale: Keep cherubim, worldwide scope, and creation claim.

verses.rationale: Preserve paired bodily appeals and living God.

verses.after: Bend your ear, LORD, and hear. Open your eyes, LORD, and see. Hear Sennacherib’s words, which he has sent to mock the living God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Incline your ear, O LORD, and hear. Open your eyes, O LORD, and see. Hear the words of Sennacherib that he has sent to taunt the living God.

verses.rationale: Keep the concession in the prayer.

verses.rationale: Retain materials and the prayer’s explanation.

verses.rationale: Preserve the stated purpose beyond immediate rescue.

verses.after: Now, LORD our God, please save us from his hand, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you alone, LORD, are God.”

verses.rationale: Keep the named prayer subject and answered-hearing motif.

I cut down its tall cedars, the choice of its cypresses. I entered its farthest lodging place, its thickest forest.

verses.rationale: Keep the shift from Assyrian boasting to divine planning.

verses.rationale: Retain the full sequence of vulnerable plant images.

verses.rationale: Preserve the movement sequence and divine knowledge.

verses.rationale: Keep the humiliating restraint images without abstraction.

verses.rationale: Keep the balanced plant image as poetry.

verses.rationale: Include Armies from the source’s read addition.
