verses.after: In King Josiah’s eighteenth year, the king sent Shaphan the secretary, son of Azaliah, son of Meshullam, to the LORD’s house with this command:
verses.tsw_comparator: In the eighteenth year of King Josiah, the king sent Shaphan son of Azaliah son of Meshullam, the scribe, to the house of the LORD, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserve the accounting instruction and collection chain.
verses.before: “Go up to Hilkiah the high priest and let him count the silver that has been brought into the house of the LORD, which the keepers of the threshold have gathered from the people.
verses.after: “Go up to Hilkiah the high priest and have him total the money brought into the LORD’s house, which the threshold guards have collected from the people.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Go up to Hilkiah the high priest and let him count the silver that has been brought into the house of the LORD, which the keepers of the threshold have gathered from the people.

verses.rationale: Keep supervisors distinct from workers.
verses.before: Let them give it into the hand of those doing the work, those appointed over the house of the LORD, and let them give it to those doing the work who are in the house of the LORD to repair the damage of the house:
verses.after: Let them put it into the hands of those supervising the work on the LORD’s house, who are to pay the workers repairing the damage to the house—
verses.tsw_comparator: Let them give it into the hand of those doing the work, those appointed over the house of the LORD, and let them give it to those doing the work who are in the house of the LORD to repair the damage of the house:

verses.rationale: Retain trades and materials.
verses.before: to carpenters, builders, and masons, and to buy timber and quarried stone to repair the house.
verses.after: the carpenters, builders, and masons—and buy timber and dressed stone to repair the house.
verses.tsw_comparator: to carpenters, builders, and masons, and to buy timber and quarried stone to repair the house.

verses.rationale: Echo the earlier repair account without turning it into general advice.
verses.before: But no accounting will be required from them for the silver given into their hand, for they are acting faithfully.”
verses.after: But no accounting is to be required from them for the money entrusted to them, because they act faithfully.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But no accounting shall be required from them for the silver given into their hand, for they are acting faithfully.”

verses.rationale: Retain Torah’s book title without identifying an exact modern extent.
verses.before: Hilkiah the high priest said to Shaphan the scribe, “I have found the book of the instruction in the house of the LORD.” Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan, and he read it.
verses.after: Hilkiah the high priest told Shaphan the secretary, “I have found the Book of the Instruction in the LORD’s house.” Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan, and he read it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hilkiah the high priest said to Shaphan the scribe, “I have found the book of the instruction in the house of the LORD.” Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan, and he read it.

verses.rationale: Keep the financial report before the book report.
verses.before: Shaphan the scribe came to the king and returned a word to the king and said, “Your servants have poured out the silver that was found in the house and have given it into the hand of those doing the work, those appointed over the house of the LORD.”
verses.after: Shaphan the secretary came to the king and reported, “Your servants have emptied out the money found in the house and given it to those supervising the work on the LORD’s house.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Shaphan the scribe came to the king and returned a word to the king and said, “Your servants have poured out the silver that was found in the house and have given it into the hand of those doing the work, those appointed over the house of the LORD.”

verses.rationale: Preserve the understated report and oral reading.
verses.before: Then Shaphan the scribe told the king, saying, “Hilkiah the priest has given me a book.” And Shaphan read it before the king.
verses.after: Then Shaphan the secretary told the king, “Hilkiah the priest has given me a book.” And Shaphan read it aloud before the king.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Shaphan the scribe told the king, saying, “Hilkiah the priest has given me a book.” And Shaphan read it before the king.

verses.rationale: Keep hearing as the trigger of the grief gesture.
verses.before: And it happened when the king heard the words of the book of the instruction that he tore his clothes.
verses.after: When the king heard the words of the Book of the Instruction, he tore his clothes.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened when the king heard the words of the book of the instruction that he tore his clothes.

verses.rationale: Retain the five named delegates.
verses.before: The king commanded Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Achbor son of Micaiah, Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah servant of the king, saying,
verses.after: The king commanded Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Achbor son of Micaiah, Shaphan the secretary, and Asaiah the king’s servant:
verses.tsw_comparator: The king commanded Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Achbor son of Micaiah, Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah servant of the king, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserve all beneficiaries and the hearing/doing link.
verses.before: “Go, inquire of the LORD for me and for the people and for all Judah concerning the words of this book that has been found. For great is the fury of the LORD that is kindled against us because our ancestors did not listen to the words of this book, to do according to all that is written concerning us.”
verses.after: “Go and inquire of the LORD for me, for the people, and for all Judah concerning the words of this book that has been found. Great is the LORD’s wrath kindled against us, because our ancestors did not listen to this book’s words and do everything written for us.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Go, inquire of the LORD for me and for the people and for all Judah concerning the words of this book that has been found. For great is the fury of the LORD that is kindled against us because our ancestors did not listen to the words of this book, to do according to all that is written concerning us.”

verses.rationale: Retain Huldah’s prophetic title and her husband’s lineage and occupation.
verses.before: So Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam, Achbor, Shaphan, and Asaiah went to Huldah the prophet, wife of Shallum son of Tikvah son of Harhas, keeper of the garments. She lived in Jerusalem in the Second Quarter, and they spoke with her.
verses.after: Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam, Achbor, Shaphan, and Asaiah went to Huldah the prophetess, wife of Shallum son of Tikvah, son of Harhas, keeper of the wardrobe. She lived in Jerusalem’s Second Quarter. They spoke with her,
verses.tsw_comparator: So Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam, Achbor, Shaphan, and Asaiah went to Huldah the prophet, wife of Shallum son of Tikvah son of Harhas, keeper of the garments. She lived in Jerusalem in the Second Quarter, and they spoke with her.

verses.rationale: Keep the woman as authoritative oracle speaker and the unnamed man address.
verses.before: She said to them, “Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: Say to the man who sent you to me:
verses.after: and she said to them, “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Tell the man who sent you to me:
verses.tsw_comparator: She said to them, “Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: Say to the man who sent you to me:

verses.rationale: Preserve the oracle’s scope.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD: Look, I am bringing disaster upon this place and upon its inhabitants, all the words of the book that the king of Judah has read,
verses.after: This is what the LORD says: I am bringing disaster on this place and its inhabitants—all the words of the book the king of Judah has read.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD: Look, I am bringing disaster upon this place and upon its inhabitants, all the words of the book that the king of Judah has read,

verses.rationale: Keep the fire image and unquenched judgment.
verses.before: because they abandoned me and burned incense to other gods in order to provoke me to anger with all the work of their hands. My fury is kindled against this place and will not be extinguished.
verses.after: Because they abandoned me and burned offerings to other gods, provoking me with all the work of their hands, my wrath is kindled against this place and will not be quenched.
verses.tsw_comparator: because they abandoned me and burned incense to other gods in order to provoke me to anger with all the work of their hands. My fury is kindled against this place and will not be extinguished.

verses.rationale: Distinguish the personal royal response from the preceding public judgment.
verses.before: “But to the king of Judah who sent you to inquire of the LORD, thus you will say to him: Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel, concerning the words that you have heard:
verses.after: But tell the king of Judah, who sent you to inquire of the LORD: This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says concerning the words you heard:
verses.tsw_comparator: “But to the king of Judah who sent you to inquire of the LORD, thus you shall say to him: Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel, concerning the words that you have heard:

verses.rationale: Keep the reciprocal hearing and every response listed.
verses.before: Because your heart was tender and you humbled yourself before the LORD when you heard what I spoke against this place and against its inhabitants, that they would become a horror and a curse, and you tore your clothes and wept before me, I also have heard you, says the LORD.
verses.after: Because your heart was tender and you humbled yourself before the LORD when you heard what I said against this place and its inhabitants—that they would become a desolation and a curse—and because you tore your clothes and wept before me, I too have heard you, declares the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Because your heart was tender and you humbled yourself before the LORD when you heard what I spoke against this place and against its inhabitants, that they would become a horror and a curse, and you tore your clothes and wept before me, I also have heard you, says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserve in peace despite the later violent death; do not harmonize it away.
verses.before: So look, I am gathering you to your ancestors, and you will be gathered to your grave in peace. Your eyes will not see all the disaster that I am bringing upon this place.” Then they returned the word to the king.
verses.after: Therefore I will gather you to your ancestors, and you will be gathered to your grave in peace. Your eyes will not see all the disaster I am bringing on this place.” They took the reply back to the king.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore look, I am gathering you to your ancestors, and you shall be gathered to your grave in peace. Your eyes shall not see all the disaster that I am bringing upon this place.” Then they returned the word to the king.

verses.rationale: Keep both constituencies.
verses.before: Then the king sent, and they gathered to him all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.after: The king sent word, and all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem gathered to him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the king sent, and they gathered to him all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Retain every audience group and full public reading.
verses.before: The king went up to the house of the LORD, and with him all the men of Judah, all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the priests, the prophets, and all the people, from small to great. He read in their hearing all the words of the book of the covenant that had been found in the house of the LORD.
verses.after: The king went up to the LORD’s house with all the men of Judah, all Jerusalem’s inhabitants, the priests, the prophets, and all the people, from the least to the greatest. He read aloud to them all the words of the Book of the Covenant found in the LORD’s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king went up to the house of the LORD, and with him all the men of Judah, all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the priests, the prophets, and all the people, from small to great. He read in their hearing all the words of the book of the covenant that had been found in the house of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserve the pillar, full commitment, and people’s participation.
verses.before: The king stood by the pillar and made the covenant before the LORD, to walk after the LORD and keep his commandments, testimonies, and statutes with all his heart and with all his life, to establish the words of this covenant written in this book. And all the people stood in the covenant.
verses.after: The king stood by the pillar and made a covenant before the LORD: to follow the LORD and keep his commandments, testimonies, and decrees with all his heart and all his being, carrying out the words of this covenant written in the book. All the people joined in the covenant.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king stood by the pillar and made the covenant before the LORD, to walk after the LORD and keep his commandments, testimonies, and statutes with all his heart and with all his life, to establish the words of this covenant written in this book. And all the people stood in the covenant.

verses.rationale: Retain ranks, worship objects, and both disposal locations.
verses.before: The king commanded Hilkiah the high priest, the priests of the second rank, and the keepers of the threshold to bring out from the temple of the LORD all the vessels made for Baal, for Asherah, and for all the host of the heavens. He burned them outside Jerusalem in the fields of the Kidron and carried their ashes to Bethel.
verses.after: The king commanded Hilkiah the high priest, the second-ranking priests, and the threshold guards to remove from the LORD’s temple all the utensils made for Baal, Asherah, and all the army of heaven. He burned them outside Jerusalem in the fields of the Kidron and carried their ashes to Bethel.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king commanded Hilkiah the high priest, the priests of the second rank, and the keepers of the threshold to bring out from the temple of the LORD all the vessels made for Baal, for Asherah, and for all the host of the heavens. He burned them outside Jerusalem in the fields of the Kidron and carried their ashes to Bethel.

verses.rationale: Keep the distinct priest designation and full celestial list.
verses.before: He removed the idolatrous priests whom the kings of Judah had appointed to burn incense on the high places in the cities of Judah and around Jerusalem, people who burned incense to Baal, to the sun, the moon, the constellations, and all the host of the heavens.
verses.after: He removed the cult priests Judah’s kings had appointed to burn offerings at the high places in Judah’s towns and around Jerusalem, and those who burned offerings to Baal, the sun, the moon, the constellations, and all the army of heaven.
verses.tsw_comparator: He removed the idolatrous priests whom the kings of Judah had appointed to burn incense on the high places in the cities of Judah and around Jerusalem, those who burned incense to Baal, to the sun, the moon, the constellations, and all the host of the heavens.

verses.rationale: Preserve the sequence of destruction and grave contamination.
verses.before: He brought out the Asherah from the house of the LORD outside Jerusalem to the Wadi Kidron, burned it at the Wadi Kidron, ground it to dust, and threw its dust upon the graves of the common people.
verses.after: He brought the Asherah out of the LORD’s house to the Kidron Valley outside Jerusalem, burned it there, ground it to dust, and scattered its dust over the graves of the common people.
verses.tsw_comparator: He brought out the Asherah from the house of the LORD outside Jerusalem to the Wadi Kidron, burned it at the Wadi Kidron, ground it to dust, and threw its dust upon the graves of the common people.

verses.rationale: Keep the gendered groups and flag uncertain roles and woven objects in notes.
verses.before: He tore down the houses of the cult prostitutes that were in the house of the LORD, where the women were weaving coverings for Asherah.
verses.after: He tore down the quarters of the male shrine attendants in the LORD’s house, where women wove coverings for Asherah.
verses.tsw_comparator: He tore down the houses of the cult prostitutes that were in the house of the LORD, where the women were weaving coverings for Asherah.

verses.rationale: Retain the geographic extent and difficult gate location.
verses.before: He brought all the priests from the cities of Judah and defiled the high places where the priests had burned incense, from Geba as far as Beersheba. He tore down the high places of the gates that were at the entrance of the gate of Joshua, governor of the city, which were on one’s left at the city gate.
verses.after: He brought all the priests from Judah’s towns and defiled the high places where they had burned offerings, from Geba to Beer-sheba. He demolished the high places at the gates, at the entrance to the gate of Joshua the city governor, on the left as one entered the city gate.
verses.tsw_comparator: He brought all the priests from the cities of Judah and defiled the high places where the priests had burned incense, from Geba as far as Beersheba. He tore down the high places of the gates that were at the entrance of the gate of Joshua, governor of the city, which were on one’s left at the city gate.

verses.rationale: Keep exclusion from altar service distinct from shared food.
verses.before: Yet the priests of the high places did not come up to the altar of the LORD in Jerusalem, but they ate unleavened bread among their brothers.
verses.after: The priests of the high places did not go up to the LORD’s altar in Jerusalem, though they ate unleavened bread among their fellow priests.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet the priests of the high places did not come up to the altar of the LORD in Jerusalem, but they ate unleavened bread among their brothers.

verses.rationale: Preserve both genders, rite, and location.
verses.before: He defiled Topheth, which is in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, so that no one could make his son or daughter pass through the fire to Molech.
verses.after: He defiled Topheth in the Valley of Ben-hinnom, so that no one could make a son or daughter pass through the fire to Molech.
verses.tsw_comparator: He defiled Topheth, which is in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, so that no one could make his son or daughter pass through the fire to Molech.

verses.rationale: Keep horses and chariots distinct without saying the horses were burned.
verses.before: He removed the horses that the kings of Judah had dedicated to the sun at the entrance of the house of the LORD, by the chamber of Nathan-Melech the court official, which was in the precincts, and he burned the chariots of the sun with fire.
verses.after: He removed the horses Judah’s kings had dedicated to the sun at the entrance to the LORD’s house, near the chamber of Nathan-melech the court official in the precincts. He burned the sun’s chariots.
verses.tsw_comparator: He removed the horses that the kings of Judah had dedicated to the sun at the entrance of the house of the LORD, by the chamber of Nathan-Melech the court official, which was in the precincts, and he burned the chariots of the sun with fire.

verses.rationale: Retain the roof and both courtyards; avoid overstating the difficult removal verb.
verses.before: The altars that were on the roof of the upper room of Ahaz, which the kings of Judah had made, and the altars that Manasseh had made in the two courts of the house of the LORD, the king tore down and crushed there and threw their dust into the Wadi Kidron.
verses.after: The king demolished the altars Judah’s kings had made on the roof of Ahaz’s upper room and the altars Manasseh had made in both courtyards of the LORD’s house. He removed them from there and threw their dust into the Kidron Valley.
verses.tsw_comparator: The altars that were on the roof of the upper room of Ahaz, which the kings of Judah had made, and the altars that Manasseh had made in the two courts of the house of the LORD, the king tore down and crushed there and threw their dust into the Wadi Kidron.

verses.rationale: Preserve Solomon’s responsibility and all three national deities.
verses.before: The high places that were before Jerusalem, south of the Mount of Destruction, which Solomon king of Israel had built for Ashtoreth detestable thing of the Sidonians, for Chemosh detestable thing of Moab, and for Milcom abomination of the children of Ammon, the king defiled.
verses.after: The king defiled the high places east of Jerusalem, south of the Mount of Destruction, which Solomon king of Israel had built for Ashtoreth, the Sidonians’ detestable god, Chemosh, Moab’s detestable god, and Milcom, the Ammonites’ abhorrent god.
verses.tsw_comparator: The high places that were before Jerusalem, south of the Mount of Destruction, which Solomon king of Israel had built for Ashtoreth detestable thing of the Sidonians, for Chemosh detestable thing of Moab, and for Milcom abomination of the children of Ammon, the king defiled.

verses.rationale: Keep the deliberate use of human remains.
verses.before: He shattered the pillars, cut down the Asherah poles, and filled their places with human bones.
verses.after: He smashed the sacred pillars, cut down the Asherah poles, and filled their sites with human bones.
verses.tsw_comparator: He shattered the pillars, cut down the Asherah poles, and filled their places with human bones.

verses.rationale: Preserve the repeated demolition and distinct burning actions.
verses.before: Moreover, the altar that was at Bethel and the high place that Jeroboam son of Nebat had made, by which he caused Israel to sin—that altar and high place he tore down. He burned the high place, ground it to dust, and burned the Asherah.
verses.after: He also demolished the altar at Bethel and the high place Jeroboam son of Nebat had made, leading Israel into sin. He demolished that altar and high place, burned the high place, ground it to dust, and burned the Asherah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moreover, the altar that was at Bethel and the high place that Jeroboam son of Nebat had made, by which he caused Israel to sin—that altar and high place he tore down. He burned the high place, ground it to dust, and burned the Asherah.

verses.rationale: Keep the fulfillment connection with the earlier unnamed prophet.
verses.before: Josiah turned and saw the tombs that were there on the mountain. He sent and took the bones from the tombs and burned them upon the altar and defiled it according to the word of the LORD that the man of God had proclaimed, who proclaimed these things.
verses.after: Josiah turned and saw the tombs there on the hill. He had the bones taken from the tombs and burned on the altar, defiling it, according to the LORD’s word proclaimed by the man of God who had announced these things.
verses.tsw_comparator: Josiah turned and saw the tombs that were there on the mountain. He sent and took the bones from the tombs and burned them upon the altar and defiled it according to the word of the LORD that the man of God had proclaimed, who proclaimed these things.

verses.rationale: Retain the question and identifying report.
verses.before: He said, “What is this monument that I see?” The men of the city said to him, “It is the tomb of the man of God who came from Judah and proclaimed these things that you have done against the altar of Bethel.”
verses.after: He asked, “What is that monument I see?” The men of the city told him, “It is the tomb of the man of God who came from Judah and announced these things you have done to Bethel’s altar.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “What is this monument that I see?” The men of the city said to him, “It is the tomb of the man of God who came from Judah and proclaimed these things that you have done against the altar of Bethel.”

verses.rationale: Keep both prophets’ remains protected.
verses.before: He said, “Let him rest. Let no one move his bones.” So they left his bones with the bones of the prophet who had come from Samaria.
verses.after: He said, “Leave it alone. Let no one disturb his bones.” So they spared his bones, along with those of the prophet who had come from Samaria.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “Let him rest. Let no one move his bones.” So they left his bones with the bones of the prophet who had come from Samaria.

verses.rationale: Retain the extension into northern towns.
verses.before: Josiah also removed all the houses of the high places that were in the cities of Samaria, which the kings of Israel had made to provoke the LORD to anger, and he did to them according to all the acts he had done in Bethel.
verses.after: Josiah also removed all the high-place shrines in Samaria’s towns, which Israel’s kings had made and so provoked anger. He did to them everything he had done at Bethel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Josiah also removed all the houses of the high places that were in the cities of Samaria, which the kings of Israel had made to provoke the LORD to anger, and he did to them according to all the acts he had done in Bethel.

verses.rationale: Preserve the killing’s sacrificial diction and the return.
verses.before: He slaughtered all the priests of the high places who were there upon the altars and burned human bones upon them. Then he returned to Jerusalem.
verses.after: He slaughtered all the priests of the high places there on their altars and burned human bones on them. Then he returned to Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: He slaughtered all the priests of the high places who were there upon the altars and burned human bones upon them. Then he returned to Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Keep the festival and written authority.
verses.before: The king commanded all the people, saying, “Make a Passover to the LORD your God as it is written in this book of the covenant.”
verses.after: The king commanded all the people, “Celebrate Passover to the LORD your God, as written in this Book of the Covenant.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The king commanded all the people, saying, “Make a Passover to the LORD your God as it is written in this book of the covenant.”

verses.rationale: Retain like this rather than claiming no Passover at all.
verses.before: Surely no Passover like this had been made from the days of the judges who judged Israel or in all the days of the kings of Israel and the kings of Judah.
verses.after: No Passover like this had been celebrated since the days of the judges who judged Israel, or throughout the days of the kings of Israel and Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Surely no Passover like this had been made from the days of the judges who judged Israel or in all the days of the kings of Israel and the kings of Judah.

verses.rationale: Preserve date and location.
verses.before: But in the eighteenth year of King Josiah this Passover was made to the LORD in Jerusalem.
verses.after: It was in King Josiah’s eighteenth year that this Passover was celebrated to the LORD in Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: But in the eighteenth year of King Josiah this Passover was made to the LORD in Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Keep the full removal list and stated purpose.
verses.before: Moreover, Josiah removed the mediums, spiritists, household gods, idols, and all the detestable things that were seen in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem, in order to establish the words of the instruction written in the book that Hilkiah the priest had found in the house of the LORD.
verses.after: Josiah also cleared away the mediums, spiritists, household gods, idols, and all the detestable things seen in Judah and Jerusalem. He did this to carry out the words of the Instruction written in the book Hilkiah the priest had found in the LORD’s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moreover, Josiah removed the mediums, spiritists, household gods, idols, and all the detestable things that were seen in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem, in order to establish the words of the instruction written in the book that Hilkiah the priest had found in the house of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserve the exceptional claim and threefold total commitment.
verses.before: Before him there was no king like him who returned to the LORD with all his heart, with all his life, and with all his might, according to all the instruction of Moses, and after him none arose like him.
verses.after: No king before him had turned to the LORD as he did, with all his heart, all his being, and all his strength, following all Moses’ Instruction. Nor did anyone like him arise afterward.
verses.tsw_comparator: Before him there was no king like him who returned to the LORD with all his heart, with all his life, and with all his might, according to all the instruction of Moses, and after him none arose like him.

verses.rationale: Keep the failure of reform to reverse the stated judgment.
verses.before: Even so, the LORD did not turn from the great burning of his anger with which his anger burned against Judah because of all the provocations with which Manasseh had provoked him.
verses.after: Yet the LORD did not turn from his great, burning anger against Judah because of everything Manasseh had done to provoke him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Nevertheless, the LORD did not turn from the great burning of his anger with which his anger burned against Judah because of all the provocations with which Manasseh had provoked him.

verses.rationale: Retain both rejected chosen places and repeated removal language.
verses.before: The LORD said, “I will remove Judah also from my presence, as I removed Israel, and I will reject this city Jerusalem that I chose and the house of which I said, ‘My name will be there.’”
verses.after: The LORD said, “I will remove Judah from my presence too, just as I removed Israel. I will reject Jerusalem, this city I chose, and the house of which I said, ‘My name will be there.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said, “I will remove Judah also from my presence, as I removed Israel, and I will reject this city Jerusalem that I chose and the house of which I said, ‘My name shall be there.’”

verses.rationale: Keep the source notice.
verses.before: Now the rest of the acts of Josiah and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.after: The rest of Josiah’s acts and everything he did are written in the annals of the kings of Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the rest of the acts of Josiah and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?

verses.rationale: Leave the ambiguous relation to Assyria open and preserve Kings’ death location.
verses.before: In his days Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt went up to the king of Assyria at the Euphrates River. King Josiah went to meet him, and Pharaoh Neco put him to death at Megiddo when he saw him.
verses.after: In his days Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt went up to the king of Assyria at the Euphrates River. King Josiah went out to meet him, and Neco killed him at Megiddo when he saw him.
verses.tsw_comparator: In his days Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt went up to the king of Assyria at the Euphrates River. King Josiah went to meet him, and Pharaoh Neco put him to death at Megiddo when he saw him.

verses.rationale: Keep dead on transport rather than harmonizing Chronicles.
verses.before: His servants carried him dead in a chariot from Megiddo, brought him to Jerusalem, and buried him in his tomb. Then the people of the land took Jehoahaz son of Josiah, anointed him, and made him king in place of his father.
verses.after: His servants carried him dead from Megiddo to Jerusalem in a chariot and buried him in his tomb. The people of the land took Josiah’s son Jehoahaz, anointed him, and made him king in his father’s place.
verses.tsw_comparator: His servants carried him dead in a chariot from Megiddo, brought him to Jerusalem, and buried him in his tomb. Then the people of the land took Jehoahaz son of Josiah, anointed him, and made him king in place of his father.

verses.rationale: Preserve age, short reign, and maternal lineage.
verses.before: Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah.
verses.after: Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for three months. His mother’s name was Hamutal, daughter of Jeremiah, from Libnah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah.

verses.rationale: Keep the adverse judgment after Josiah.
verses.before: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, according to all that his ancestors had done.
verses.after: He did what was evil in the LORD’s eyes, just as his ancestors had done.
verses.tsw_comparator: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, according to all that his ancestors had done.

verses.rationale: Follow the read preventing and retain both tribute amounts.
verses.before: Pharaoh Neco bound him at Riblah in the land of Hamath so that he would not reign in Jerusalem, and imposed upon the land a tribute of one hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold.
verses.after: Pharaoh Neco imprisoned him at Riblah in the land of Hamath, preventing him from reigning in Jerusalem. He imposed on the land a levy of a hundred talents of silver and one talent of gold.
verses.tsw_comparator: Pharaoh Neco bound him at Riblah in the land of Hamath so that he would not reign in Jerusalem, and imposed upon the land a tribute of one hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold.

verses.rationale: Preserve the imposed name change and exile death.
verses.before: Pharaoh Neco made Eliakim son of Josiah king in place of Josiah his father and changed his name to Jehoiakim. But he took Jehoahaz, and he came to Egypt and died there.
verses.after: Pharaoh Neco made Eliakim son of Josiah king in place of his father Josiah and changed his name to Jehoiakim. He took Jehoahaz away to Egypt, where he died.
verses.tsw_comparator: Pharaoh Neco made Eliakim son of Josiah king in place of Josiah his father and changed his name to Jehoiakim. But he took Jehoahaz, and he came to Egypt and died there.

verses.rationale: Keep the burden’s transfer to the population.
verses.before: Jehoiakim gave the silver and gold to Pharaoh, but he assessed the land to give the silver according to Pharaoh’s command. He exacted the silver and gold from the people of the land, from each according to his assessment, to give to Pharaoh Neco.
verses.after: Jehoiakim gave Pharaoh the silver and gold, but he taxed the land to meet Pharaoh’s demand. He exacted silver and gold from the people of the land, each according to his assessment, to pay Pharaoh Neco.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jehoiakim gave the silver and gold to Pharaoh, but he assessed the land to give the silver according to Pharaoh’s command. He exacted the silver and gold from the people of the land, from each according to his assessment, to give to Pharaoh Neco.

verses.rationale: Follow the read maternal name and preserve all figures.
verses.before: Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Zebidah daughter of Pedaiah from Rumah.
verses.after: Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for eleven years. His mother’s name was Zebudah, daughter of Pedaiah, from Rumah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Zebidah daughter of Pedaiah from Rumah.

verses.rationale: Retain the closing judgment.
verses.before: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, according to all that his ancestors had done.
verses.after: He did what was evil in the LORD’s eyes, just as his ancestors had done.
verses.tsw_comparator: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, according to all that his ancestors had done.

verses.rationale: Retain the three-year submission before rebellion.
verses.before: In his days Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up, and Jehoiakim became his servant for three years. Then he turned and rebelled against him.
verses.after: In Jehoiakim’s days Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon invaded. Jehoiakim became his servant for three years, then turned and rebelled against him.
verses.tsw_comparator: In his days Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up, and Jehoiakim became his servant for three years. Then he turned and rebelled against him.

verses.rationale: Preserve divine agency and all four groups.
verses.before: The LORD sent against him raiding bands of Chaldeans, Arameans, Moabites, and children of Ammon. He sent them against Judah to destroy it, according to the word of the LORD that he had spoken by the hand of his servants the prophets.
verses.after: The LORD sent raiding bands of Chaldeans, Arameans, Moabites, and Ammonites against him. He sent them against Judah to destroy it, according to the LORD’s word spoken through his servants the prophets.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD sent against him raiding bands of Chaldeans, Arameans, Moabites, and children of Ammon. He sent them against Judah to destroy it, according to the word of the LORD that he had spoken by the hand of his servants the prophets.

verses.rationale: Keep the stated cause and sentence continuation.
verses.before: Surely this came upon Judah by the mouth of the LORD, to remove them from his presence because of the sins of Manasseh, according to all that he had done,
verses.after: This came upon Judah at the LORD’s command, to remove them from his presence because of Manasseh’s sins and everything he had done,
verses.tsw_comparator: Surely this came upon Judah by the mouth of the LORD, to remove them from his presence because of the sins of Manasseh, according to all that he had done,

verses.rationale: Retain repeated innocent blood and refusal to forgive.
verses.before: and also because of the innocent blood that he shed, for he filled Jerusalem with innocent blood, and the LORD was not willing to forgive.
verses.after: including the innocent blood he had shed. He had filled Jerusalem with innocent blood, and the LORD was unwilling to forgive.
verses.tsw_comparator: and also because of the innocent blood that he shed, for he filled Jerusalem with innocent blood, and the LORD was not willing to forgive.

verses.rationale: Keep the source notice.
verses.before: Now the rest of the acts of Jehoiakim and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.after: The rest of Jehoiakim’s acts and everything he did are written in the annals of the kings of Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the rest of the acts of Jehoiakim and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?

verses.rationale: Distinguish the similar royal names.
verses.before: Jehoiakim lay down with his ancestors. Jehoiachin his son became king in his place.
verses.after: Jehoiakim rested with his ancestors. His son Jehoiachin became king in his place.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jehoiakim lay down with his ancestors. Jehoiachin his son became king in his place.

verses.rationale: Retain the two boundaries and changed imperial control.
verses.before: The king of Egypt did not again go out from his land, for the king of Babylon had taken from the Wadi of Egypt as far as the Euphrates River all that belonged to the king of Egypt.
verses.after: The king of Egypt no longer came out of his land, because the king of Babylon had taken everything that had belonged to him, from the Wadi of Egypt to the Euphrates River.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king of Egypt did not again go out from his land, for the king of Babylon had taken from the Wadi of Egypt as far as the Euphrates River all that belonged to the king of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Keep eighteen rather than importing another book’s age.
verses.before: Jehoiachin was eighteen years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Nehushta daughter of Elnathan from Jerusalem.
verses.after: Jehoiachin was eighteen years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for three months. His mother’s name was Nehushta, daughter of Elnathan, from Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jehoiachin was eighteen years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Nehushta daughter of Elnathan from Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Retain the paternal comparison.
verses.before: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, according to all that his father had done.
verses.after: He did what was evil in the LORD’s eyes, just as his father had done.
verses.tsw_comparator: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, according to all that his father had done.

verses.rationale: Follow plural servants in the read text.
verses.before: At that time the servants of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon went up to Jerusalem, and the city came under siege.
verses.after: At that time the servants of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon advanced on Jerusalem, and the city came under siege.
verses.tsw_comparator: At that time the servants of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon went up to Jerusalem, and the city came under siege.

verses.rationale: Preserve the king’s subsequent personal arrival.
verses.before: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to the city while his servants were besieging it.
verses.after: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to the city while his servants were besieging it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to the city while his servants were besieging it.

verses.rationale: Retain the full surrender party and Babylonian regnal year.
verses.before: Then Jehoiachin king of Judah went out to the king of Babylon—he, his mother, his servants, his officials, and his court officers—and the king of Babylon took him in the eighth year of his reign.
verses.after: Jehoiachin king of Judah went out to the king of Babylon with his mother, servants, commanders, and court officials. The king of Babylon took him prisoner in the eighth year of his reign.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Jehoiachin king of Judah went out to the king of Babylon—he, his mother, his servants, his officials, and his court officers—and the king of Babylon took him in the eighth year of his reign.

verses.rationale: Preserve the destruction of Solomon’s utensils and both treasuries.
verses.before: He brought out from there all the treasures of the house of the LORD and the treasures of the king’s house and cut apart all the gold vessels that Solomon king of Israel had made in the temple of the LORD, as the LORD had spoken.
verses.after: He carried off all the treasures of the LORD’s house and the palace and cut apart all the gold utensils Solomon king of Israel had made for the LORD’s temple, just as the LORD had said.
verses.tsw_comparator: He brought out from there all the treasures of the house of the LORD and the treasures of the king’s house and cut apart all the gold vessels that Solomon king of Israel had made in the temple of the LORD, as the LORD had spoken.

verses.rationale: Retain the totalizing statement with its explicit exception and ten-thousand count.
verses.before: He carried all Jerusalem into exile: all the officials, all the mighty men of wealth, ten thousand exiles, and all the craftsmen and smiths. No one remained except the poorest people of the land.
verses.after: He deported all Jerusalem—all the leaders and capable fighting men, ten thousand exiles, along with all the craftsmen and metalworkers. Only the poorest people of the land remained.
verses.tsw_comparator: He carried all Jerusalem into exile: all the officials, all the mighty men of wealth, ten thousand exiles, and all the craftsmen and smiths. No one remained except the poorest people of the land.

verses.rationale: Keep the women and officials in the expanded list.
verses.before: He carried Jehoiachin into exile to Babylon, and the king’s mother, the king’s wives, his court officers, and the powerful people of the land he carried into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon.
verses.after: He deported Jehoiachin to Babylon. He also took the king’s mother, his wives, his court officials, and the leading men of the land into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon.
verses.tsw_comparator: He carried Jehoiachin into exile to Babylon, and the king’s mother, the king’s wives, his court officers, and the powerful people of the land he carried into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon.

verses.rationale: Preserve the separate subtotals without forcing a new grand total.
verses.before: All the men of strength, seven thousand, and the craftsmen and smiths, one thousand, all mighty men trained for war—the king of Babylon brought them into exile to Babylon.
verses.after: The king of Babylon took to Babylon all the fighting men, seven thousand, and the craftsmen and metalworkers, a thousand—all strong men fit for war.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the men of strength, seven thousand, and the craftsmen and smiths, one thousand, all mighty men trained for war—the king of Babylon brought them into exile to Babylon.

verses.rationale: Keep the uncle relationship and imposed name change.
verses.before: The king of Babylon made Mattaniah, Jehoiachin’s uncle, king in his place and changed his name to Zedekiah.
verses.after: The king of Babylon made Jehoiachin’s uncle Mattaniah king in his place and changed his name to Zedekiah.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king of Babylon made Mattaniah, Jehoiachin’s uncle, king in his place and changed his name to Zedekiah.

verses.rationale: Follow read Hamutal and retain all chronological details.
verses.before: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah.
verses.after: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for eleven years. His mother’s name was Hamutal, daughter of Jeremiah, from Libnah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah.

verses.rationale: Keep the named comparison.
verses.before: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, according to all that Jehoiakim had done.
verses.after: He did what was evil in the LORD’s eyes, just as Jehoiakim had done.
verses.tsw_comparator: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, according to all that Jehoiakim had done.

verses.rationale: Retain the theological summary before the rebellion narrative.
verses.before: For because of the anger of the LORD this happened in Jerusalem and Judah until he cast them away from his presence. Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.
verses.after: Because of the LORD’s anger, these things happened in Jerusalem and Judah until he cast them out of his presence. Then Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.
verses.tsw_comparator: For because of the anger of the LORD this happened in Jerusalem and Judah until he cast them away from his presence. And Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

verses.rationale: Keep the complete date and encirclement.
verses.before: And it happened in the ninth year of Zedekiah’s reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month, that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came, he and all his army, against Jerusalem. He camped against it and built siegeworks against it all around.
verses.after: In the ninth year of Zedekiah’s reign, on the tenth day of the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came against Jerusalem with his whole army. He camped against it, and they built siegeworks all around it.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened in the ninth year of Zedekiah’s reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month, that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came, he and all his army, against Jerusalem. He camped against it and built siegeworks against it all around.

verses.rationale: Retain the ending regnal year.
verses.before: So the city came under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
verses.after: The city remained under siege until King Zedekiah’s eleventh year.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the city came under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.

verses.rationale: Do not insert the fourth month from Jeremiah into Kings’ shorter date.
verses.before: On the ninth day of the fourth month the famine became severe in the city, and there was no bread for the people of the land.
verses.after: By the ninth day of the month, the famine in the city was severe, and there was no bread for the people of the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the ninth day of the fourth month the famine became severe in the city, and there was no bread for the people of the land.

verses.rationale: Supply the implied flight and identify the king from the next verse.
verses.before: Then the city was broken through, and all the men of war fled by night by the way of the gate between the two walls, which was by the king’s garden, while the Chaldeans were around the city. The king went by the way of the Arabah.
verses.after: The city wall was breached. That night all the fighting men fled through the gate between the two walls beside the king’s garden, while the Chaldeans surrounded the city. The king went toward the Arabah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the city was broken through, and all the men of war fled by night by the way of the gate between the two walls, which was by the king’s garden, while the Chaldeans were around the city. The king went by the way of the Arabah.

verses.rationale: Retain the capture location and abandonment.
verses.before: But the army of the Chaldeans pursued the king and overtook him in the plains of Jericho, and all his army was scattered from him.
verses.after: The Chaldean army pursued the king and overtook him in the plains of Jericho. His whole army had scattered from him.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the army of the Chaldeans pursued the king and overtook him in the plains of Jericho, and all his army was scattered from him.

verses.rationale: Keep the judicial scene before the punishment.
verses.before: They seized the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah, and they pronounced judgment upon him.
verses.after: They seized the king and brought him to the king of Babylon at Riblah, where judgment was pronounced against him.
verses.tsw_comparator: They seized the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah, and they pronounced judgment upon him.

verses.rationale: Preserve the cruel sequence and concrete shackles.
verses.before: They slaughtered Zedekiah’s sons before his eyes. Then they blinded Zedekiah’s eyes, bound him with bronze chains, and brought him to Babylon.
verses.after: They slaughtered Zedekiah’s sons before his eyes. Then the king of Babylon put out Zedekiah’s eyes, bound him in bronze shackles, and took him to Babylon.
verses.tsw_comparator: They slaughtered Zedekiah’s sons before his eyes. Then they blinded Zedekiah’s eyes, bound him with bronze chains, and brought him to Babylon.

verses.rationale: Retain seventh day rather than harmonizing Jeremiah’s tenth.
verses.before: In the fifth month, on the seventh day of the month—which was the nineteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon—Nebuzaradan captain of the guard, servant of the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.
verses.after: On the seventh day of the fifth month, in the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, Nebuzaradan, commander of the guard and servant of Babylon’s king, came to Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the fifth month, on the seventh day of the month—which was the nineteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon—Nebuzaradan captain of the guard, servant of the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Preserve the comprehensive burning and repeated emphasis.
verses.before: He burned the house of the LORD, the king’s house, and all the houses of Jerusalem. Every great house he burned with fire.
verses.after: He burned the LORD’s house, the palace, and all Jerusalem’s houses. Every great house he burned down.
verses.tsw_comparator: He burned the house of the LORD, the king’s house, and all the houses of Jerusalem. Every great house he burned with fire.

verses.rationale: Keep the army’s action distinct from the commander’s burning.
verses.before: All the army of the Chaldeans who were with the captain of the guard tore down the walls around Jerusalem.
verses.after: The whole Chaldean army with the commander of the guard tore down the walls around Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the army of the Chaldeans who were with the captain of the guard tore down the walls around Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Retain deserters among those deported.
verses.before: The rest of the people who remained in the city, the deserters who had fallen away to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the multitude Nebuzaradan captain of the guard carried into exile.
verses.after: Nebuzaradan, commander of the guard, deported the people left in the city, those who had deserted to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the population.
verses.tsw_comparator: The rest of the people who remained in the city, the deserters who had fallen away to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the multitude Nebuzaradan captain of the guard carried into exile.

verses.rationale: Keep the exception and agricultural roles.
verses.before: But the captain of the guard left some of the poorest of the land as vineyard workers and farmers.
verses.after: But the commander of the guard left some of the poorest people of the land to tend vineyards and fields.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the captain of the guard left some of the poorest of the land as vineyard workers and farmers.

verses.rationale: Preserve the named furnishings and destination.
verses.before: The bronze pillars that were in the house of the LORD, the stands, and the bronze Sea that was in the house of the LORD, the Chaldeans broke in pieces and carried their bronze to Babylon.
verses.after: The Chaldeans broke up the bronze pillars, the stands, and the bronze Sea in the LORD’s house, and carried their bronze to Babylon.
verses.tsw_comparator: The bronze pillars that were in the house of the LORD, the stands, and the bronze Sea that was in the house of the LORD, the Chaldeans broke in pieces and carried their bronze to Babylon.

verses.rationale: Keep the complete utensil list.
verses.before: They took the pots, shovels, snuffers, dishes, and all the bronze utensils with which the priests ministered.
verses.after: They took the pots, shovels, snuffers, dishes, and all the bronze utensils used in the service.
verses.tsw_comparator: They took the pots, shovels, snuffers, dishes, and all the bronze utensils with which the priests ministered.

verses.rationale: Retain the material-by-material phrasing.
verses.before: The captain of the guard took the firepans and bowls—what was gold as gold and what was silver as silver.
verses.after: The commander of the guard also took the firepans and bowls—whatever was gold as gold, and whatever was silver as silver.
verses.tsw_comparator: The captain of the guard took the firepans and bowls—what was gold as gold and what was silver as silver.

verses.rationale: Keep the counts and unweighed abundance.
verses.before: As for the two pillars, the one Sea, and the stands that Solomon had made for the house of the LORD, the bronze of all these vessels was beyond weight.
verses.after: The bronze of the two pillars, the one Sea, and the stands Solomon had made for the LORD’s house—all these objects—was beyond weighing.
verses.tsw_comparator: As for the two pillars, the one Sea, and the stands that Solomon had made for the house of the LORD, the bronze of all these vessels was beyond weight.

verses.rationale: Retain three-cubit capitals here rather than harmonizing the earlier five.
verses.before: The height of one pillar was eighteen cubits, and a bronze capital was upon it. The height of the capital was three cubits, with network and pomegranates upon the capital all around, all of bronze. The second pillar was like it with network.
verses.after: Each pillar was eighteen cubits high and had a bronze capital three cubits high, with bronze latticework and pomegranates all around it. The second pillar, with its latticework, was the same.
verses.tsw_comparator: The height of one pillar was eighteen cubits, and a bronze capital was upon it. The height of the capital was three cubits, with network and pomegranates upon the capital all around, all of bronze. The second pillar was like it with network.

verses.rationale: Keep ranks, names, and number of guards.
verses.before: The captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and three keepers of the threshold.
verses.after: The commander of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and the three threshold guards.
verses.tsw_comparator: The captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and three keepers of the threshold.

verses.rationale: Retain five advisers rather than Jeremiah’s seven and the other distinct counts.
verses.before: From the city he took one court officer who was appointed over the men of war, five men from people who saw the king’s face who were found in the city, the scribe of the commander of the army who mustered the people of the land, and sixty men from the people of the land who were found in the city.
verses.after: From the city he took one official in charge of the fighting men, five of the king’s close advisers who were found there, the army secretary responsible for mustering the people of the land, and sixty men of the land found in the city.
verses.tsw_comparator: From the city he took one court officer who was appointed over the men of war, five men from those who saw the king’s face who were found in the city, the scribe of the commander of the army who mustered the people of the land, and sixty men from the people of the land who were found in the city.

verses.rationale: Preserve the transfer for judgment.
verses.before: Nebuzaradan captain of the guard took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
verses.after: Nebuzaradan, commander of the guard, took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Nebuzaradan captain of the guard took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.

verses.rationale: Keep execution before the exile summary.
verses.before: The king of Babylon struck them and put them to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath. So Judah went into exile from its land.
verses.after: The king of Babylon struck them down and put them to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath. So Judah went into exile from its land.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king of Babylon struck them and put them to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath. So Judah went into exile from its land.

verses.rationale: Retain the three-generation connection to earlier officials.
verses.before: As for the people who remained in the land of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had left, he appointed over them Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan.
verses.after: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, over the people he had left in the land of Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: As for the people who remained in the land of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had left, he appointed over them Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan.

verses.rationale: Preserve all named commanders and origins.
verses.before: When all the commanders of the armies, they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah, they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah: Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan son of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, and Jaazaniah son of the Maacathite, they and their men.
verses.after: When all the army commanders and their men heard that Babylon’s king had appointed Gedaliah, they came to him at Mizpah: Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan son of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, and Jaazaniah son of the Maacathite, with their men.
verses.tsw_comparator: When all the commanders of the armies, they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah, they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah: Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan son of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, and Jaazaniah son of the Maacathite, they and their men.

verses.rationale: Retain the oath and practical assurance.
verses.before: Gedaliah swore to them and to their men and said to them, “Do not be afraid of the servants of the Chaldeans. Live in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will be well with you.”
verses.after: Gedaliah swore an oath to them and their men: “Do not be afraid of the Chaldean officials. Stay in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and things will go well for you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Gedaliah swore to them and to their men and said to them, “Do not be afraid of the servants of the Chaldeans. Live in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will be well with you.”

verses.rationale: Keep the royal lineage, ten companions, and both victim groups.
verses.before: But it happened in the seventh month that Ishmael son of Nethaniah, son of Elishama, from the royal offspring, came with ten men. They struck Gedaliah, and he died, along with the Judeans and Chaldeans who were with him at Mizpah.
verses.after: In the seventh month Ishmael son of Nethaniah, son of Elishama, a member of the royal line, came with ten men. They struck Gedaliah dead, along with the Judeans and Chaldeans who were with him at Mizpah.
verses.tsw_comparator: But it happened in the seventh month that Ishmael son of Nethaniah, son of Elishama, from the royal offspring, came with ten men. They struck Gedaliah, and he died, along with the Judeans and Chaldeans who were with him at Mizpah.

verses.rationale: Preserve fear as the stated reason for flight.
verses.before: Then all the people, from small to great, and the commanders of the armies arose and went to Egypt, for they were afraid of the Chaldeans.
verses.after: Then all the people, from the least to the greatest, and the army commanders left for Egypt because they were afraid of the Chaldeans.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then all the people, from small to great, and the commanders of the armies arose and went to Egypt, for they were afraid of the Chaldeans.

verses.rationale: Retain the complete date and lifted-head image.
verses.before: And it happened in the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, that Evil-Merodach king of Babylon, in the year he became king, lifted up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah from prison.
verses.after: In the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month, Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in the year he became king, lifted Jehoiachin’s head and released him from prison.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened in the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, that Evil-Merodach king of Babylon, in the year he became king, lifted up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah from prison.

verses.rationale: Keep the comparative honor without claiming restoration to Judah’s throne.
verses.before: He spoke good things with him and set his throne above the thrones of the kings who were with him in Babylon.
verses.after: He spoke kindly to him and gave him a seat above the seats of the other kings with him in Babylon.
verses.tsw_comparator: He spoke good things with him and set his throne above the thrones of the kings who were with him in Babylon.

verses.rationale: Retain the clothing change and ongoing meals.
verses.before: Jehoiachin changed his prison garments and ate bread continually before the king all the days of his life.
verses.after: Jehoiachin changed out of his prison clothes and regularly ate at the king’s table for the rest of his life.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jehoiachin changed his prison garments and ate bread continually before the king all the days of his life.

verses.rationale: Preserve the repeated daily and lifelong provision that closes the book.
verses.before: His allowance, a continual allowance, was given to him from the king, a daily portion, all the days of his life.
verses.after: The king gave him a regular allowance, a daily portion every day, for the rest of his life.
verses.tsw_comparator: His allowance, a continual allowance, was given to him from the king, a daily portion, all the days of his life.
